This R markdown prepares data and figures for the MORA Paradise Water System Water Supply 
Vulnerability Assessment.

# 1. Workspace setup

```{r setup}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,  
                      message = FALSE, 
                      warning = FALSE, 
                      eval = TRUE)

# This Rmd lives in Reports/, but all paths (data/, src/, setup.R) are relative
# to the project root. root.dir applies from the next chunk on.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

# Packages, src/ functions, palette, plot theme, analysis windows, and CRS are
# shared with Explore_MORA_Climate_Grid.Rmd.
source(here::here("Reports/report_setup.R"))

```

# 1b. Analysis functions

Shared helper functions live in `src/` and are loaded by `setup.R` (for example,
the NPS Park Tiles basemap helpers in `src/nps_basemap.R`).

Define park using 4-digit NPS Unit Code. Codes for all parks can be found at: 
<https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/foia/upload/NPS-Unit-List.xlsx>.

Download the park boundary from the NPS IRMA DataStore as an {sf} object.

```{r park_dat}

park <- "MORA"

# Get park geometry and metadata
park_boundary <- getParkBoundary(park = park)
state <- park_boundary$STATE

park_boundary <- st_transform(park_boundary,
                              crs_use)

mapview(park_boundary,
        col.regions = "seagreen")

```

# 2. Water supplies

A water supply system database was created for this project using various
NPS and public databases. The database contains a row for each water supply
system and source of water (e.g., individual wells, diversions, and springs)
associated with each supply. Here, we focus on the Paradise water supply
system per NPS WRD direction.

```{r}

# Import database and convert to spatial (sf) object
wsd <- get_wsd() %>%
  dplyr::filter(park_unit == park) %>%
  st_transform(., crs_use)

# Filter for Paradise
current_system <- wsd %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Paradise", water_system_name)) %>%
  st_transform(., crs_use)

proposed_samples <- bind_rows(
  st_read("data/park/MORA/From_WRD/field/Edith Creek.kml") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(watershed = "Edith Creek"),
  st_read("data/park/MORA/From_WRD/field/Paradise River.kml") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(watershed = "Paradise River")
)

# Select system + all water systems map
mapview(park_boundary,
        col.regions = "seagreen",
        alpha.regions = 0.2) +
mapview(wsd,
        col.regions = "dodgerblue",
        layer.name = "All Water Systems") +
mapview(current_system,
        color = "yellow",
        col.regions = "yellow",
        alpha.regions = 0,
        layer.name = "Select System",
        cex = 10,
        lwd = 5) +
  mapview(proposed_samples,
          col.region = "hotpink",
          cex = 3)

# Remove this for now since not needed
rm(wsd)
gc()

```

# 3. Load supplementary datasets

####### - NPS Building Footprints

With our water supplies identified, we now pull in other relevant datasets that 
we'll use to characterize the source area and contributing area.

## - Watersheds, Flowlines, and Stream Profiles

Get watershed associated with the water supply point and other watersheds that 
overlap the park.

#### - Surface Water

We delineate contributing watersheds for the current Edith Creek intake, the
proposed downstream intake, and the Paradise Valley groundwater-fed area below,
so that available water volumes can be compared across all three candidate
systems on a common basis (modeled runoff x catchment area).

#### - Surface Flow Data

Edith Creek is ungauged (one spot measurement: 1 CFS, Sept 2026 field visit), so
rather than calibrating a routing model to this system directly, supply is
estimated from monthly NPS WBM runoff converted to gallons per catchment. A
routing/VIC comparison against a downstream gauged basin is retained separately
in an appendix-style workflow as a sanity check on model performance, but does
not feed the main supply-demand analysis.

#### - Full Park 

```{r all_park_watersheds_and_flowlines}

# Get all watersheds overlapping park
park_watersheds <- get_huc(AOI = park_boundary %>%
                             st_transform(4326), 
                           type = "huc12") 

mapview(park_watersheds)

# Get flowlines for park
#fcode	Description
#46006	Stream/River: Perennial
#46003	Stream/River: Intermittent
#46007	Stream/River: Ephemeral
park_flowlines <- get_nhdplus(AOI = park_boundary %>% st_transform(4326)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fcode = as.factor(fcode),
                f_name = case_when(fcode == 46006 ~ "Perennial",
                                   fcode == 46003 ~ "Intermittent",
                                   fcode == 46007 ~ "Ephemeral",
                                   TRUE ~ "Other")) %>%
  st_transform(., crs_use)

# Plot watersheds + flow lines
mapview(park_boundary,
        color = "black",
        alpha.regions = 0,
        lwd = 2,
        layer.name = "PB") +
  mapview(park_flowlines,
          color = "dodgerblue4",
          zcol = "f_name",
          layer.name = "Flowlines") +
  mapview(park_watersheds,
          alpha.regions = 0) +
  mapview(current_system,
          col.regions = 'deeppink1')



# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(park_flowlines, park_watersheds)
gc()
```


#### - Current System (Edith) 

Load watershed for the current system on Edith Creek

```{r edith_watersheds}
# Get contributing area for edith_creek_system
# system_watershed <- getXYWatersheds(sf = select_system)

# instead, use lidar from Washington Geological Survey
# manually downloaded lidar dataset since it was a one-off
# system_watershed <- delineate_watershed(
#   dem = rast('data/park/MORA/lidar_DTM_paradise.tif'),
#   pour_point = select_system,
#   output_dir = './data/park/MORA',
#   file_prefix = 'edithcreek',
#   breach_dist = 10,
#   snap_buffer_dist = 20,
#   interactive_snap = TRUE,
#   write_gpkg = TRUE,
#   overwrite = TRUE,
#   crs_out = "EPSG:5070")

system_watershed <-  st_read('data/park/MORA/edithcreek_watershed.gpkg') %>%
  st_transform(crs_use)

system_watershed_ft2 <- st_area(system_watershed) %>% 
  set_units(ft^2) %>%
  as.numeric()

mapview(system_watershed)

# First run: Performs reprojection, crop, breach, and flow accumulation (takes time)
system_flowlines <-  delineate_streamlines(
  dem = rast('data/park/MORA/lidar_DTM_paradise.tif'),
  aoi = system_watershed, # sf polygon output from delineate_watershed()
  output_dir = "data/park/MORA",
  file_prefix = "edith_creek",
  threshold = 220000,
  aoi_buffer_dist = 20, # 200m buffer for edge processing
  crs_out = "EPSG:5070",
  output_option = "all"
)

mapview(system_flowlines)

# Subsequent runs: Skips reprojection, breaching, and flow accum; re-runs channel extraction in ~1 second
main_flowline <- delineate_streamlines(
  mainline_only = TRUE,
  output_dir = "data/park/MORA",
  file_prefix = "edith_creek",
  threshold = 220000,
  resume = TRUE
)

system_dem <- rast("data/park/MORA/edith_creek_dem.tif") * .3048

# Run profile
system_profile <- extract_stream_profile(
  flowlines = system_flowlines, 
  dem = system_dem, 
  sample_dist = 25,
  min_reach_length = 0
  )

ggplotly(system_profile$profile_plot)

mapview(system_watershed,
        color = "dodgerblue",
        col.regions = "dodgerblue",
        alpha.regions = 0.2) +
mapview(main_flowline,
        color = "navy",
        lwd = 6) +
  mapview(system_flowlines,
        color = "navy",
        alpha = 0.5) +
  mapview(current_system,
          col.regions = "hotpink")

# Get area
st_area(system_watershed) %>% 
  units::set_units("km^2")
# 0.70 km2


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(main_flowline, system_dem, system_flowlines)
gc()
```

### - geology profiles

Plot streamflow profiles with geology

```{r lava_flow_contacts}

add_geology_to_profile <- function(profile_nodes,
                                    geology,
                                    title_text,
                                    unit_field = "unit_name",
                                    spring_elev_ft = c(6000, 6500),
                                    spring_labels = NULL) {

  # Some error checking
  if (!unit_field %in% names(geology)) {
    stop("`unit_field` ('", unit_field, "') not found in `geology`. Available columns: ",
         paste(names(geology), collapse = ", "))
  }

  if (is.null(spring_labels)) {
    spring_labels <- paste0(spring_elev_ft, " ft spring")
  }
  # Match crs before spatial join
  if (sf::st_crs(profile_nodes) != sf::st_crs(geology)) {
    geology <- sf::st_transform(geology, sf::st_crs(profile_nodes))
  }

  # Spatial join: attach mapped geologic unit at each sampled profile point.
  # left = TRUE keeps points that fall outside all mapped polygons (geologic_unit
  # is NA) rather than silently dropping them.
  joined <- suppressWarnings(
    sf::st_join(profile_nodes, geology[, unit_field], join = sf::st_intersects, left = TRUE)
  )
  joined$geologic_unit <- joined[[unit_field]]

  # Re-sort along the profile in case st_join changed row order)
  joined <- joined[order(joined$cum_dist_m), ]

  # Flag the first node of each newly mapped unit as a contact crossing.
  # coalesce(..., FALSE) treats the first node, and any NA-to-NA transition, as
  # "no crossing" rather than propagating NA.
  joined <- joined %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      contact_crossing = dplyr::coalesce(geologic_unit != dplyr::lag(geologic_unit), FALSE)
    )

  contacts <- joined %>% dplyr::filter(contact_crossing)

  # Known spring elevations are conventionally reported in feet in NPS/WRD field
  # records; convert to meters to match extract_stream_profile()'s elevation_m.
  spring_ref <- data.frame(
    elevation_m = spring_elev_ft * 0.3048,
    label = spring_labels
  )
  
  # Plot
  p <- 
    ggplot(joined, aes(x = cum_dist_m, y = elevation_m)) +
    geom_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(color = geologic_unit), size = 1.8) +
    geom_vline(data = contacts,
              aes(xintercept = cum_dist_m),
              linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(data = spring_ref,
              aes(yintercept = elevation_m),
              linetype = "dashed", color = "steelblue4", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(data = spring_ref,
              aes(x = max(joined$cum_dist_m, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.02, 
                  y = elevation_m, label = label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.5, hjust = -.25, 
      size = 3, color = "steelblue4") +
    labs(
      title = title_text,
      x = "Cumulative Distance Downstream (m)",
      y = "Elevation (m)",
      color = "Geology") +
    theme_wsva() +

as_mainstem_sf <- function(x, label) {
  # mainstem_flowline comes back as a bare sfc (not a full sf data frame),
  # so wrap it directly rather than routing it through st_as_sfc() (which
  # has no method for an sfc input - that's what threw the original error).
  if (inherits(x, "sf")) {
    # already a full sf data frame - use as-is
  } else if (inherits(x, "sfc")) {
    x <- sf::st_sf(geometry = x)
  } else {
    x <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(x))
  }
  x %>% dplyr::mutate(system = label) %>% dplyr::select(system)
}
```

## - Snow persistence

Contiguous U.S. annual snow persistence and trends from 2001 to 2020: https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5f63790982ce38aaa23a3930

Megan Sears corresponded with John Hammond who provided a newer, unpublished snow persistence raster dataset. The google drive source for these files, as of 9/21/2026 is:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1m-4cSl2j7LD_QV0ZM9yKb-ui9mBVyLfI

Updated rasters were saved in the same directory as the published. Note that 2021 onward

He included this note: Of note, NASA recomputed all of the MOD10A2 values for collection 6.1 since the last time I calculate snow persistence.I noticed when comparing 2016 and 2017 SP from my USGS data release to the output of the new code that there were some areas with substantial differences, mostly in the PNW

```{r}

# Define some snow persistence related helper functions

# Function to read in snow persistence rasters
#' @param path full file path of raster
#' @param aoi sf aoi to clip raster to
#' @param target_crs crs of output raster
#' @return sp_masked - reprojected and masked sp raster
read_sp <- function(path, aoi, target_crs = NULL) {
  sp_meta <- rast(path)
  aoi_trans <- st_transform(aoi, crs = crs(sp_meta))
  sp <- rast(path, win = ext(aoi_trans))
  sp_masked <- mask(sp, vect(aoi_trans))
  if (!is.null(target_crs)) {
    if (!same.crs(sp_masked, target_crs)) {
      sp_masked <- project(sp_masked, target_crs, method = "bilinear")
    }
  }
  
  return(sp_masked)
}

# Helper function to compute Sen's slope across pixel time series
calc_sens_slope <- function(x) {
  x_clean <- na.omit(x)
  # Require at least 3 valid observations in the x-year window
  if (length(x_clean) < 3) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  # Calculate Sen's slope (returns change per year)
  return(as.numeric(trend::sens.slope(x_clean)$estimates))
}


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(aoi_trans, sp, sp_masked, sp_meta, x_clean)
gc()
```

To start, we'll create a buffered AOI of the Paradise watershed and read in snow persistence rasters across available years (2000-2026). 

```{r snow_persistence_timeseries}

library(tidyterra)


# Define AOI to evaluate sp - here we use Paradise Watershed 
aoi_buffered <- park_boundary %>%
  st_buffer(2000)

# Build file paths
years <- 2000:2026
base_dir <- "data/all/snow_persistence_hammond_2018"

file_paths <- file.path(base_dir, paste0("MOD10A2_SCI_", years, ".tif"))
valid_paths <- file_paths[file.exists(file_paths)]
valid_years <- as.numeric(str_extract(basename(valid_paths), "\\d{4}"))

# Target CRS
target_crs <- "EPSG:32149"

# Read rasters into list
sp_list <- map(valid_paths, ~ read_sp(.x, 
                                      aoi = aoi_buffered, 
                                      target_crs = target_crs))

# Align extents/resolutions to the first raster so rast() stacks cleanly
template_grid <- sp_list[[1]]
sp_list_aligned <- map(sp_list, ~ resample(.x, template_grid, method = "bilinear"))

# Combine into SpatRaster stack
sp_stack <- rast(sp_list_aligned)
names(sp_stack) <- paste0("Yr_", valid_years)

# Calculate statistics
window_size <- 5 # number of years if doing moving stats
stat_layers <- list()
stat_names <- c()

for (i in window_size:nlyr(sp_stack)) {
  # Subset 5 consecutive years
  sub_stack <- sp_stack[[(i - window_size + 1):i]]
  
  # Calculate pixel-wise mean or Sens slope
  stat <- mean(sub_stack, na.rm = TRUE) # Moving average mean
  #stat <- app(sub_stack, fun = calc_sens_slope) # sens slope
    
  start_yr <- valid_years[i - window_size + 1]
  end_yr <- valid_years[i]
  
  stat_layers[[length(stat_layers) + 1]] <- stat
  stat_names <- c(stat_names, paste0(start_yr, "-", end_yr))
}

# Combine moving average layers into a single SpatRaster stack
stat_stack <- rast(stat_layers)
names(stat_stack) <- stat_names

# 6. Convert SpatRaster stack to a tidy Data Frame
stat_df <- as.data.frame(stat_stack, xy = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(x, y),
    names_to = "period",
    values_to = "persistence"
  ) %>%
  # Filter out background NA values to keep plotting fast
  filter(!is.na(persistence))

# 7. Plot using native ggplot2 geom_raster
ggplot(stat_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = persistence)) +
  geom_raster() +
  facet_wrap(~period, ncol = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
  name = "Snow Persistence\n(5-Yr Moving Mean)",
  low = "#b2182b",      # Red for declining persistence
  mid = "#f7f7f7",      # Neutral white/light gray at zero
  high = "#2166ac",     # Blue for increasing persistence
  midpoint = 0,         # Centers scale explicitly at zero change
  labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1) # Format as % per year
) +
  coord_equal() + # Maintains 1:1 spatial aspect ratio
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "5-Year Moving Mean Snow Persistence (2000–2026)",
    subtitle = "Paradise River Watershed (+2km Buffer)"
  )


# 1. Generate 80% contour lines for each year in the annual raster stack

valid_years2 <- c(2001, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2025)

contour_list <- imap(valid_years2, function(yr, idx) {
  
  # Subset SpatRaster layer safely by numerical index
  r_layer <- sp_stack[[idx]]
  
  # Check max/min values to ensure 0.80 exists in the layer
  r_min <- global(r_layer, "min", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
  r_max <- global(r_layer, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
  
  # Determine if persistence is 0-1 or 0-100 scale
  target_level <- if (r_max > 1) 80 else 0.8
  
  # Skip layer if target level is out of raster value range
  if (is.na(r_min) || is.na(r_max) || r_max < target_level || r_min > target_level) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Generate contour lines
  c_poly <- terra::as.contour(r_layer, levels = target_level)
  
  if (nrow(c_poly) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Convert SpatVector to sf object and assign metadata
  sf::st_as_sf(c_poly) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      year = yr,
      year_factor = as.factor(yr)
    )
})

# Combine into a single sf dataframe
contours_sf <- bind_rows(contour_list)

# Combine all annual contours into a single sf object
contours_sf <- bind_rows(contour_list)

# 2. Option A: Faceted plot showing annual 80% contours over time
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = contours_sf, color = "#2166ac", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 5) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  theme_wsva(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual 80% Snow Persistence Contours (2000–2026)",
    subtitle = "Paradise River Watershed (+2km Buffer)"
  )

# 3. Option B: Overlaid plot showing contour contraction/expansion over time

bg_tile <- get_tiles(x = st_bbox(contours_sf), provider = "Esri.WorldImagery", zoom = 11)

ggplot() +
  # Render satellite raster
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = bg_tile) +
  
  # Overlay contours (use continuous 'year' instead of 'year_factor')
  geom_sf(data = contours_sf, aes(color = year), linewidth = 0.8, fill = NA) +
  
  # Continuous gradient from Ice Blue (Early) to Royal Blue (Recent)
  scale_color_gradient2(
    name = "Year",
    low = "dodgerblue",      # Light cool blue
    mid = "#ffffbf",      # Warm cream
    high = "#d73027",     # Vivid red/orange
    midpoint = median(contours_sf$year),
    breaks = seq(min(contours_sf$year), max(contours_sf$year), by = 5)
  ) +
  
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(st_bbox(contours_sf)["xmin"], st_bbox(contours_sf)["xmax"]),
    ylim = c(st_bbox(contours_sf)["ymin"], st_bbox(contours_sf)["ymax"]),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "80% Snow Persistence Contours (2000–2026)",
    subtitle = "Paradise River Watershed (+2km Buffer)"
  )


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(aoi_buffered, base_dir, bg_tile, c_poly, contour_list, contours_sf, file_paths, r_layer, r_max, r_min, sp_list, sp_list_aligned, start_yr, stat_df, stat_layers, stat_names, stat_stack, sub_stack, target_level, template_grid, valid_paths, valid_years, valid_years2, window_size)
gc()
```

Snow persistence trend by candidate system (Appendix A): watershed-mean annual
snow persistence for each candidate catchment, with Sen's slope and a
Mann-Kendall test. Trends are reported for the full record and for 2001-2020
only, because the 2021-onward rasters come from NASA's reprocessed MOD10A2
collection 6.1, which differs noticeably from the earlier collection in the
Pacific Northwest (see note above).

```{r sp_trend_by_system}

sp_systems <- list("Edith Current" = system_watershed,
                   "Edith Downstream" = down_edith_creek_watershed,
                   "Paradise GW" = paradise_river_watershed)

sp_system_ts <- purrr::imap_dfr(sp_systems, function(ws, sys_name) {
  ws_proj <- sf::st_transform(ws, crs = terra::crs(sp_stack))
  terra::extract(sp_stack, terra::vect(ws_proj), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::select(-ID) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "year_label", values_to = "mean_sp") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(year = as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(year_label, "\\d{4}")),
                  system = sys_name)
}) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(mean_sp))

sp_trend <- tidyr::crossing(system = names(sp_systems),
                            period = c("Full record", "2001-2020")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(stats = purrr::map2(system, period, function(sys, per) {
    d <- sp_system_ts %>%
      dplyr::filter(system == sys,
                    per == "Full record" | (year >= 2001 & year <= 2020)) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(year)
    tibble::tibble(first_year = min(d$year), last_year = max(d$year), n_years = nrow(d),
                   mean_sp = mean(d$mean_sp),
                   sens_slope_per_yr = as.numeric(trend::sens.slope(d$mean_sp)$estimates),
                   mk_p_value = trend::mk.test(d$mean_sp)$p.value)
  })) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(stats)

print(sp_trend)
readr::write_csv(sp_trend, "data/park/MORA/Tables/sp_trend_by_system.csv")

sp_ts_fig <- ggplot(sp_system_ts, aes(x = year, y = mean_sp, color = system)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2020.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Edith Current" = "#1b6ca8", "Edith Downstream" = "#459a74", "Paradise GW" = "#a1631f")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean annual snow persistence",
       caption = "Dashed line: rasters from 2021 onward use MOD10A2 collection 6.1.") +
  theme_wsva()
```

Moving-average windows smooth out multi-year variations, making it difficult to isolate elevation-dependent responses or single-season ENSO (El Niño / La Niña) signals.  To address this, the analytical framework can be restructured in two main ways: elevation-binned trend metrics and ENSO-conditioned anomaly decomposition.


Strategy 1: Snow Persistence vs. Elevation AnalysisInstead of evaluating trend statistics strictly across 2D map space, you can compress pixels by elevation bands. This reveals whether warming affects low-elevation margins (snowpack melting earlier) differently than high-elevation zones (snowpack staying frozen).


```{r sp_v_elevation}
# 1. Reload/Reproject DEM directly
sp_dem <- rast('data/park/MORA/lidar_DTM_paradise.tif') %>%
  project(sp_stack[[1]], method = "bilinear")

# 2. Define elevation break intervals (e.g., 800m to 4400m in 200m steps)
# Build a 3-column reclassification matrix: [from, to, new_value]
breaks <- seq(3615, 7141, by = 500)
rcl_matrix <- cbind(
  from = breaks[-length(breaks)],
  to   = breaks[-1],
  becomes = breaks[-length(breaks)] # or 1:(length(breaks)-1) for band indices
)

# 3. Classify using the valid sp_dem object
dem_binned <- classify(sp_dem, rcl = rcl_matrix)

# 3. Extract annual mean persistence by elevation band
elev_df <- tibble(
  elev_band = values(dem_binned, mat = FALSE),
  as.data.frame(sp_stack, na.rm = FALSE)
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(elev_band)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Yr_"),
    names_to = "year_label",
    values_to = "persistence"
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(str_extract(year_label, "\\d{4}"))) %>%
  group_by(elev_band, year) %>%
  summarize(mean_sp = mean(persistence, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Group elevation bands into broader imperial (feet) zones
elev_df_lines <- elev_df %>%
  mutate(
    tier = case_when(
      elev_band < 4000 ~ "Low (< 4,000 ft)",
      elev_band >= 4000 & elev_band < 5500 ~ "Mid (4,000 ft – 5,500 ft)",
      elev_band >= 5500 & elev_band < 7000 ~ "Subalpine (5,500 ft – 7,000 ft)",
      TRUE ~ "High Alpine (≥ 7,000 ft)"
    ),
    tier = factor(
      tier,
      levels = c(
        "Low (< 4,000 ft)",
        "Mid (4,000 ft – 5,500 ft)",
        "Subalpine (5,500 ft – 7,000 ft)",
        "High Alpine (≥ 7,000 ft)"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(tier, year) %>%
  summarize(
    tier_mean = mean(mean_sp, na.rm = TRUE),
    tier_sd   = sd(mean_sp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(tier))

# Plot trajectories with corrected imperial factor levels
sp_elev <- ggplot(elev_df_lines, aes(x = year, y = tier_mean, color = tier, fill = tier)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = pmax(0, tier_mean - tier_sd),
      ymax = pmin(1, tier_mean + tier_sd)
    ),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.85, name = "Elevation Zone") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.85, name = "Elevation Zone") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2026, by = 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  theme_wsva(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Snow Persistence Trajectories by Elevation Zone",
    subtitle = "Paradise River Watershed (2000–2026)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Snow Persistence (%)"
  )

sp_elev


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(dem_binned, elev_df, rcl_matrix, sp_dem, sp_stack)
gc()
```



Strategy 2: Isolate ENSO Effects via Linear Regression DecompositionThe Pacific Northwest generally experiences cooler, wetter winters during La Niña (higher snow persistence) and warmer, drier winters during El Niño (lower snow persistence).To isolate the underlying long-term climate trend from interannual ENSO fluctuations, you can fit a multiple linear regression at every pixel:$$\text{Snow Persistence}_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{Year}_t + \beta_2 \cdot \text{ENSO}_t + \varepsilon_t$$$\beta_1$ isolates the long-term trend per year, holding ENSO constant.$\beta_2$ quantifies pixel sensitivity to ENSO events.

```{r enso_sp}

library(rsoi) # Automatically fetches official NOAA ENSO indices


# 1. Download/prep ONI data
oni_data <- download_oni() %>%
  filter(ONI_month_window %in% c("DJF", "JFM")) %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarize(winter_oni = mean(ONI, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Classify ONI data into ENSO phases and define year bounding boxes
enso_phases <- oni_data %>%
  filter(Year >= 2000 & Year <= 2026) %>%
  mutate(
    phase = case_when(
      winter_oni >= 0.5  ~ "El Niño",
      winter_oni <= -0.5 ~ "La Niña",
      TRUE               ~ "Neutral"
    ),
    xmin = Year - 0.5,
    xmax = Year + 0.5,
    ymin = -Inf,
    ymax = Inf
  ) %>%
  filter(phase != "Neutral") # Only shade active El Niño / La Niña years

# 2. Plot with ENSO background rectangles
enso_plot <- ggplot() +
  # Background ENSO shading (placed FIRST so it stays behind lines)
  geom_rect(
    data = enso_phases,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = phase),
    alpha = 0.15,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "ENSO Phase",
    values = c("El Niño" = "#d95f02", "La Niña" = "#1b9e77"),
    guide = guide_legend(order = 1)
  ) +
  
  # Elevation ribbon bounds
  geom_ribbon(
    data = elev_df_lines,
    aes(x = year, ymin = pmax(0, tier_mean - tier_sd), ymax = pmin(1, tier_mean + tier_sd), fill = tier),
    alpha = 0.12,
    color = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # Trajectory lines and points
  geom_line(data = elev_df_lines, aes(x = year, y = tier_mean, color = tier), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = elev_df_lines, aes(x = year, y = tier_mean, color = tier), size = 2) +
  
  # Color scales for elevation tiers
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.85, name = "Elevation Zone") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2026, by = 4), expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  
  theme_wsva(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Snow Persistence Trajectories & ENSO Phases",
    subtitle = "Paradise River Watershed (2000–2026) | Background: El Niño (Red) vs La Niña (Green)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Snow Persistence (%)"
  )

ggarrange(
  sp_elev,
  enso_plot,
  ncol = 1,
  align = "v"
)




# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(elev_df_lines, enso_phases, enso_plot, oni_data, sp_elev)
gc()
```

### -- SNOTEL

Read in nearby SNOTEL sites and download and compare data to weather station.

Started with 20 km distance for SNOTEL. The sites that are farther away will
likely be removed before analysis because they are not representative of the 
system catchment.

```{r snotel}

# Read in snotel (if fails might be none in area, increase distance)
#snotel_hourly <- getSNOTEL(
#   aoi  = system_watershed,
#   dist = 1000,

# ) %>%

# saveRDS(snotel_daily, "data/park/MORA/snotel_daily.rds")
# saveRDS(snotel_hourly, "data/park/MORA/snotel_hourly.rds")

snotel_daily <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/snotel_daily.rds")
snotel_hourly <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/snotel_hourly.rds")

# Get SNOTEL locations
# Coordinates come in as WGS84 lon/lat, so project to albers
snotel_sites <- snotel_daily %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_use)

# Compare NOAA and SNOTEL stations
mapview(park_boundary, 
        col.regions = "seagreen") +
  mapview(snotel_sites,
          col.regions= 'purple') +
  mapview(system_watershed,
    col.regions = "dodgerblue",
    alpha.regions = 0.5
  )

snotel_daily_tidy <- snotel_daily %>%
  dplyr::select(date, 
                name, 
                value, 
                sensor_id, 
                water_year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date = as_date(date),
                value = as.numeric(value)) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  distinct(date, 
           name, 
           sensor_id, 
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sensor_id, 
              values_from = value) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # --- Calculate Incremental Daily Precipitation ---
  group_by(name) %>%
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    # Simple lag difference
    precip_diff = prec_i - lag(prec_i),
    
    # Handle Water Year reset (Oct 1) & initial day:
    # If it's the first record or prec_i dropped (reset), set to current prec_i
    daily_precip = case_when(
      is.na(precip_diff) ~ prec_i,
      precip_diff < 0    ~ prec_i,  # Handles WY reset or sensor recalibration
      TRUE               ~ precip_diff
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-precip_diff) %>%
  ungroup()

# Again remove unused data
rm(snotel_daily)
gc()

# Look at temporal overlap
ggplot(snotel_daily_tidy, 
       aes(x = date, 
           y = name, 
           color = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "", 
       color = "Station Name") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ggtitle('Temporal overlap')

# Prep snotel hourly data
  snotel_hourly <- snotel_hourly %>%
    # the date & time columns = the local time at MORA

    mutate(datetime = ymd_hm(paste(date, time))) %>%
    select(datetime,
           name,
           water_year,
           water_day,
           value,
           depth,
           sensor_id) %>% 
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value),
         depth = as.numeric(depth))
```

Based on the preliminary assessment above, only the following stations will be
considered.
- Cayuse Pass (SNOTEL)

A note on the Paradise SNOTEL, this is in a forested area at a lower elevation.
The snow persistence isn't that different (~93%), but will need to be careful
because there will be more interception here, less incoming shortwave radiation,
more transpiration, etc.

### -- Water Temp

Paradise River at Nadara Falls water and air temp from Aquarius. This is just
exploratory for now. Note sure if anything will be done with this.

```{r}

# Load water temp
water_temp <- read_csv('./data/park/MORA/aquarius/watertemp_MORA_Paradise_4440a.csv') %>%
  mutate(datetime_utc8 = mdy_hm(datetime_utc8))

# Data prep
wt <- water_temp %>%
  mutate(
    date = as_date(datetime_utc8),
    year = year(datetime_utc8),
    month = month(datetime_utc8),
    month_n = month(datetime_utc8),
    doy = yday(datetime_utc8),
    hour = hour(datetime_utc8),
    season = case_when(
      month_n %in% 3:5 ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
      month_n %in% 6:8 ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
      month_n %in% 9:11 ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)",
      TRUE ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)"
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("Spring (Mar–May)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
      "Fall (Sep–Nov)", "Winter (Dec–Feb)"))
  )

# Validated all-pairs (this chart overlays all 4 seasons at once, so the
# stricter all-pairs CVD/normal-vision check applies, not just adjacent).
# "Winter" is a deliberately darker neutral than the "Historical" gray used
# elsewhere - it clears CVD/normal-vision separation against the other 3
# colors cleanly at this depth, and only trips the validator's chroma-floor
# and lightness-band checks, the same accepted-neutral exception used for
# "Historical" (#595959) in the setup chunk.
season_colors <- c(
  "Spring (Mar–May)" = "#0f8a6b",
  "Summer (Jun–Aug)" = "#2a5ea8",
  "Fall (Sep–Nov)" = "#b0431f",
  "Winter (Dec–Feb)" = "#3d3d3d"
)

# Daily mean
daily <- wt %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_t = mean(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_t = min(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_t = max(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    amp = max_t - min_t,
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(doy = yday(date),
    year = year(date))

ggplot(daily, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_t, ymax = max_t), 
              fill = "#1f6feb", alpha = 0.20) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_t), 
            color = "#58a6ff", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = 'Daily mean water temp') +
  theme_wsva()

# Diurnal cycle by season
diurnal_season <- wt %>%
  group_by(season, hour) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_t = mean(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_t = median(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(watertemp_c, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(watertemp_c, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

ggplot(diurnal_season, 
       aes(x = hour, color = season, fill = season)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), 
              alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_t), linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = season_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = season_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 6, 12, 18, 23),
    labels = c("midnight", "6 am", "noon", "6 pm", "11 pm")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "°C")) +
  labs(title = "Diurnal Cycle by Season") +
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))


# Diurnal amplitude by month
amp_month <- wt %>%
  group_by(month_n, month) %>%
  # compute per-day amplitude first, then average
  group_by(date = as_date(datetime_utc8), 
           month_n, 
           month) %>%
  summarise(amp = max(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE) - 
              min(watertemp_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(month_n, month) %>%
  summarise(mean_amp = mean(amp, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_amp = sd(amp, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    season = case_when(
      month_n %in% 3:5 ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
      month_n %in% 6:8 ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
      month_n %in% 9:11 ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)",
      TRUE ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)"))

ggplot(amp_month, aes(x = month_n, 
                      y = mean_amp, 
                      fill = season)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_amp - se_amp, 
                    ymax = mean_amp + se_amp),
    width = 0.3, color = "#e6edf3", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = season_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12,
    labels = c("J", "F", "M", "A", "M", "J", "J", "A", "S", "O", "N", "D")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "°C")) +
  labs(
    title = "Diurnal Amplitude by Month",
    x = NULL, 
    y = "Amplitude") +
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(amp_month, diurnal_season, season_colors, water_temp, wt)
gc()
```

### -- USGS Surface Water

In this section, we analyze surface water using data from the USGS. We focus on
stream gages near the selected water supply system to establish baseline 
hydrological regimes and identify shifts in the timing and magnitude of peak
snowmelt and baseflow discharge.

This chunk retrieves daily discharge data for relevant stream gages, summarizes
hydrological patterns by Day of Year (DOY), and compares "early" vs. "late" 
historical periods alongside recent 2025 observations.

Gauges are way too far downstream to be used for Edith Creek or Paradise River
in MORA.

```{r usgs_sw, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# --- 1. Identify Nearby Stream Gages ---
# Define bounding box for the park unit
park_boundary_buffer <- park_boundary %>%
  st_buffer(dist = 4000)

bbox_vals <- park_boundary_buffer %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  sf::st_bbox() %>%
  as.numeric() %>%
  round(digits = 5)

# Retrieve monitoring locations and calculate distance to water sources
usgs_sw <- read_waterdata_monitoring_location(
  bbox = bbox_vals,
  site_type = "Stream") %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(park_boundary_buffer) %>%
  mutate(dist_m = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, st_transform(current_system, st_crs(park_boundary)))))

# Get availability metadata (POR) for those sites
# select only sites with data after 1980
site_availability <- read_waterdata_ts_meta(
  monitoring_location_id = usgs_sw$monitoring_location_id) %>%
   mutate(end_date = as.Date(end)) %>%
  filter(end_date > as.Date("1980-01-01")) %>%
  # Keep only unique site IDs that meet the criteria
  distinct(monitoring_location_id)
 
# Final filtered SF object
usgs_sw <- usgs_sw %>%
  filter(monitoring_location_id %in% site_availability$monitoring_location_id) 

# Select the nearest n sites for initial screening
nearest_usgs_sw <- usgs_sw %>%
  slice_min(order_by = dist_m, n = 1)

# Define USGS site ID with the required 'usgs-' prefix for NLDI queries
nldi_feature <- list(featureSource = "nwissite", 
                     featureID = nearest_usgs_sw$monitoring_location_id)


# Retrieve the upstream drainage basin polygon
basin <- get_nldi_basin(nldi_feature = nldi_feature)

basin_area <- st_area(basin)

mapview(basin)

# --- 2. Retrieve Daily Discharge Data ---
usgs_discharge <- read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = nearest_usgs_sw$monitoring_location_id,
  parameter_code = "00060" # Discharge, cubic feet per second
)

# Refine station list based on successful data retrieval
nearest_usgs_sw <- nearest_usgs_sw %>%
  dplyr::filter(monitoring_location_id %in% unique(usgs_discharge$monitoring_location_id))

# Join station metadata to discharge records
usgs_discharge <- usgs_discharge %>%
  left_join(nearest_usgs_sw %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
              dplyr::select(monitoring_location_id, monitoring_location_name, altitude, agency_code),
            by = "monitoring_location_id")

# Optional (add baseflow)
usgs_discharge_bf <- usgs_discharge %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_id) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(
    # See function desc. to modify alpha and BFImax based on geology
    # and expected baseflow lag
    bf_out = baseflow_eckhardt(value, 
                               alpha = 0.98, 
                               BFImax = 0.2)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    baseflow = bf_out$bf,
    stormflow = bf_out$quickflow
  ) %>%
  select(-bf_out) %>%
  ungroup()

# Lets see where the nearest is gauge is
mapview(usgs_sw) + mapview(park_boundary)
# Gauge is too far downstream and too large of a catchment to be a proxy or comparable
# to Edith Creek or Paradise River

ggplot(usgs_discharge_bf, aes(x = time)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = value, color = "Discharge")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = baseflow, color = "Baseflow")) +
  #geom_line(aes(y = stormflow)) +
  theme_wsva() +
  facet_wrap(~monitoring_location_id, scales = "free") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c(
    "Discharge" = "darkblue",
    "Baseflow" = "red"
  )) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
# nearest_usgs_sw is kept (not rm()'d) - it, and `basin` above, are
# used later for context on the site figure (see the Site Figure
# chunk). Everything else here is still cleaned up as before.
rm(nldi_feature, site_availability, usgs_sw)
gc()
```

### -- USGS thermal monitoring data on Paradise Creek

```{r paradise_creek}

# 1. Process Paradise Creek streamflow data
paradise_q <- read_csv("data/park/MORA/From_WRD/paradise_creek_ts.csv") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as_date(mdy_hm(date)), 
    across(-date, as.numeric)
  ) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) > 2010, year(date) < 2017) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    year = year(date),
    doy = yday(date) # Day of Year (1 - 365)
  ) %>%
  mutate(dummy_date = as.Date(paste0("2000-", format(date, "%m-%d"))),
         discharge_cfs = discharge_L_s * 0.035315,
         discharge_gal = discharge_cfs * 646317)

# 2. Process SNOTEL precipitation data
snotel_p <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    name == "Paradise",
    year(date) < 2017,
    year(date) > 2010
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    year = year(date),
    doy = yday(date)
  ) %>%
  mutate(dummy_date = as.Date(paste0("2000-", format(date, "%m-%d"))))

# 3. Calculate dynamic scaling factor
max_q <- max(paradise_q$discharge_cfs, na.rm = TRUE)
max_p <- max(snotel_p$daily_precip, na.rm = TRUE)
scale_factor <- max_q / max_p

# 4. Plot with facet_wrap by year
ggplot() +
  # Secondary Layer: Daily Precip Bars
  geom_col(
    data = snotel_p,
    aes(x = dummy_date, y = daily_precip * scale_factor, fill = "Daily Precip (in)"),
    alpha = 0.4,
    width = 1 # 1 day width on DOY scale
  ) +
  # Primary Layer: Daily Streamflow Line
  geom_line(
    data = paradise_q,
    aes(x = dummy_date, y = discharge_cfs, color = "Mean Daily Discharge (cfs)"),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  # Facet by Year
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  # Set axes & inverse scaling for secondary axis
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "2 months") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Discharge (cfs)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_factor, name = "Daily Precipitation (in)")
  ) +
  # Aesthetic mapping
  scale_color_manual(name = "", values = c("Mean Daily Discharge (cfs)" = "navy")) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "", values = c("Daily Precip (in)" = "skyblue3")) +
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "skyblue4"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"),
    text = element_text(size = 11)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    title = "Paradise Creek"
  )

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/Paradise_Creek_USGS.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 8, height = 4)

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(max_p, max_q, paradise_q, snotel_p)
gc()
```

### -- Groundwater Conceptual Model

Edith Creek has no continuous flow record, so we look for indirect evidence of
groundwater loss/gain by comparing WBM-modeled runoff against measured treatment
system outflow: if measured flow is consistently well below modeled runoff, that
gap is evidence water is going to groundwater storage rather than surface discharge
(consistent with Frank's (1995) hydrothermal/dilution conceptual model for this system).

### -- USGS Groundwater

In this segment, we examine groundwater levels and hydrography. 
Monitoring groundwater elevation (NAVD88) and converting it to depth-to-water 
provides insight into the storage capacity and saturation levels of the 
aquifers supporting the park's water systems.

This chunk identifies nearby USGS monitoring wells, retrieves field-measured 
groundwater elevations, and calculates depth-to-water by comparing measurements 
against digital elevation points. It also retrieves high-resolution 
hydrography (NHDPlusHR) for the study area.

```{r usgs_gw}

# --- 1. Identify Groundwater Monitoring Wells ---
park_boundary_buffer <- park_boundary %>%
  st_buffer(dist = 4000)

bbox_vals <- park_boundary_buffer %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  sf::st_bbox() %>%
  as.numeric() %>%
  round(digits = 5)

# Filter for sites classified as "Well" within the park boundary
usgs_groundwater <- read_waterdata_monitoring_location(bbox = bbox_vals, site_type = "Well") %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(park_boundary_buffer) %>%
  # Ensure vertical datum is present for elevation-to-depth calculations
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vertical_datum))

mapview(park_boundary, col.regions = "seagreen") +
mapview(usgs_groundwater) +
  mapview(current_system,
          col.regions = "yellow")

# --- 2. Retrieve Field Measurements ---
# Pull elevation data (62611 = GW elevation above datum) for the first five locations
usgs_groundwater_levels <- 
    dataRetrieval::read_waterdata_field_measurements(
      monitoring_location_id = usgs_groundwater$monitoring_location_id,
      parameter_code = "62611"
    ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.Date(time), 
    site_no = sub("USGS-", "", monitoring_location_id),
    ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) >= 1900) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, monitoring_location_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_lev = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(monitoring_location_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dev_mean = mean_lev - mean(mean_lev, na.rm = TRUE),
                count = n()) %>%
  dplyr::filter(count > 1)

# --- 3. Elevation and Depth-to-Water Calculation ---
# Extract surface elevation at wellheads to calculate depth
usgs_groundwater <- usgs_groundwater %>%
  dplyr::filter(monitoring_location_id %in% unique(usgs_groundwater_levels$monitoring_location_id)) 

# Join datasets to calculate depth-to-water (Surface Elevation - Water Elevation)
usgs_groundwater_levels <- usgs_groundwater_levels %>%
  left_join(usgs_groundwater %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% 
              dplyr::select(monitoring_location_id, altitude), by = "monitoring_location_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gw_depth_ft = altitude - mean_lev)

# --- 4. Visualization: Groundwater Depth Trends ---
colfunc <- colorRampPalette(c(c(pal$yellow,  pal$darkblue, pal$orange, pal$pink, pal$black)))

ggplot(usgs_groundwater_levels, 
       aes(x = ym, y = gw_depth_ft, col = monitoring_location_id)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) + 
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_reverse() + # Standard convention: depth increases downward
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(title = "Groundwater Depth Trends",
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Depth Below Surface (ft)") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = colfunc(nrow(usgs_groundwater)))


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(bbox_vals, park_boundary_buffer, usgs_groundwater, usgs_groundwater_levels)
gc()
```

# 4. Analyses with observed data

## -- Sep 2025 turbidity event

The soils were drier than what I had expected and there was little precip in
the few weeks leading up to the event. 

```{r}

# Focus on Paradise SNOTEL and the window around the Sep 6, 2025 turbidity event
# that shut down the water supply system
turbidity_event <- ymd_hm("2025-09-06 16:00")

sensor_labels <- c(
  "PREC.I"   = "Precip - increment (in)",
  "SNWD.I"   = "Snow Depth (in)",
  "WTEQ.I"   = "SWE (in)",
  "TAVG.H-2" = "Avg Temp (F)",
  "SMS.I_2"  = "Soil Moisture 2in (%)",
  "SMS.I_4"  = "Soil Moisture 4in (%)",
  "SMS.I_8"  = "Soil Moisture 8in (%)",
  "SMS.I_20" = "Soil Moisture 20in (%)",
  "SMS.I_32" = "Soil Moisture 32in (%)",
  "STO.I_2"  = "Soil Temp 2in (F)",
  "STO.I_4"  = "Soil Temp 4in (F)",
  "STO.I_8"  = "Soil Temp 8in (F)",
  "STO.I_20" = "Soil Temp 20in (F)",
  "STO.I_32" = "Soil Temp 32in (F)"
)

turbidity_window <- snotel_hourly %>%
  filter(name == "Paradise",
         datetime >= turbidity_event - days(14),
         datetime <= turbidity_event + days(7)) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  # PREC.I is cumulative (water year to date) - convert to per-step increment
  group_by(sensor_id, water_year) %>%
  mutate(value = if_else(sensor_id == "PREC.I",
                         value - lag(value, default = first(value)),
                         value)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sensor_label = sensor_labels[sensor_id])

ggplot(turbidity_window, aes(x = datetime, y = value)) +
  geom_line(color = pal$darkblue) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = turbidity_event,
             linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ sensor_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "",
       title = "Paradise SNOTEL conditions near Sep 6, 2025 turbidity event",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = event date")

# Precip event summary stats
precip_event <- turbidity_window %>%
  filter(sensor_id == "PREC.I")

# Storm window is known: Sep 6-7, 2025
storm_start <- ymd_hm("2025-09-05 20:00")
storm_end <- ymd_hm("2025-09-07 08:00")

storm_summary <- precip_event %>%
  filter(datetime >= storm_start, datetime <= storm_end) %>%
  summarize(
    total_precip_in = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    peak_hourly_precip_in = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    peak_time = datetime[which.max(value)]
  )

event_summary <- bind_cols(storm_summary)

kable(event_summary, digits = 2,
     caption = "Precipitation event summary - Paradise SNOTEL")


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(event_summary, precip_event, sensor_labels, storm_end, storm_start, turbidity_event, turbidity_window)
gc()
```

# 5. Climate and Water Balance

## - GCM Selection

Climate futures were previously compiled for park and Koppen centroids. This data was used to select which of the CMIP5 climate models to use to represent "hot dry" and "warm wet" scenarios. Here, we read in the pre-determined gcm selections.

We load these in, but at Mount Rainier, the greatest change in runoff (+ and -) corresponds to precipitation and specifically snow changes

```{r}

# Read in selected "Hot dry" "Warm Wet" climate futures
centroid_cfs <- data.table::fread('data/parkwide_gcms.csv') %>%
  dplyr::filter(park %in% {{park}},
                CF %in% c("Warm Wet", "Hot Dry")) %>%
  distinct(GCM, .keep_all = TRUE)

# If there is more than one model selection for a CF scenario, grab the more divergent.
if (nrow(centroid_cfs) > 2) {
  if (nrow(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Hot Dry")) > 1) {
    centroid_cfs <- centroid_cfs %>%
      group_by(CF) %>%
      slice_min(delta_pr)
  }
  if ((nrow(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Warm Wet")) > 1) ) {
    centroid_cfs <- centroid_cfs %>%
      group_by(CF) %>%
      slice_max(delta_pr)
  }
}

# Read in all available gcms
all_cfs <-
  read_delim( "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rossyndicate/CCRP_automated_climate_futures/master/data/general/GCM_skill_by_region.txt" ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Region == "PWR") %>% #,
                #Rank < 19) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-ES.", "HadGEM2-ES365.", GCM),
                GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-CC.", "HadGEM2-CC365.", GCM)) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(data.table(RCP = c("rcp45","rcp85"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM,RCP)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(Skill = ifelse(Rank > 18, "Low Skill", "High Skill"))
  

# GCMs available on amazon web services water balance model gridded datasets.
    wbm_gcms <- data.frame("GCM" = c(
      "inmcm4",
      "NorESM1-M",
      "MRI-CGCM3",
      "MIROC5",
      "MIROC-ESM-CHEM",
      "IPSL-CM5A-LR",
      "HadGEM2-CC365",
      "GFDL-ESM2G",
      "CanESM2",
      "CSIRO-Mk3-6-0",
      "CNRM-CM5",
      "CCSM4",
      "BNU-ESM"
    )) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(RCP = c("rcp45","rcp85")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM, '.',RCP)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-RCP)
    

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(wbm_gcms)
gc()
```

## - Climate data for the selected grid cells

GridMET (historical) and MACA (future) climate data were downloaded for all six
GridMET cells covering the buffered contributing area, and the WBM was run for
each cell to choose which cells represent the Paradise catchments. That cell
search, with its download code, per-cell WBM runs, and figures, is in
`Explore_MORA_Climate_Grid.Rmd`. Two cells were retained: the cell containing
the watershed and the cell to the west (`src/select_climate_cells.R` records the
rule and the reasoning). Here we load the cached all-cell climate data and keep
those two cells.

```{r climate_selected_cells}

contributing_area <- system_watershed %>%
  st_buffer(2000)

# GridMET grid for the contributing area (needed only to re-run the WBM below)
aoi_gridmet_grid <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/aoi_gridmet_grid_extra.rds")

clim_hist <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/clim_hist_extra.rds") %>%
  select_climate_cells()

clim_fut <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/clim_fut_extra.rds") %>%
  select_climate_cells()

# Cell centers for the selected cells (points argument of run_NPS_WBM_points)
select_clim_pts <- clim_hist %>%
  dplyr::group_by(x, y, area_weight) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(.groups = "drop") %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

```

## - Run WBM for select grids

We use the NPS water balance model (WBM) to calculate water budget components. 
The model requires temperature and precipitation inputs, which we've now 
downloaded for historical and projected periods. The water balance model is 
adapted from code base developed in NPS's {WaterBalance} package 
(<https://github.com/CCRP-Adaptation/WaterBalance>).

For our report, we ran the NPS water balance model (WBM) for each GridMET point
in the source area. The average soil moisture capacity, elevation, slope, and 
aspect are used as inputs for each model run. We then aggregate the values to 
the weighted mean for the recharge area, returning a spatially averaged daily 
value. We are running the historical and future datasets separately, but use 
final conditions from the historical as the starting conditions for the future.

```{r wbm_run_select_grids}

# FIX: renamed from "wbm_run" - duplicate of the chunk above (see its FIX
# note). Duplicate chunk labels are a hard knitr error.

hock_coef <- 5

#                             ret_final_cond = FALSE,

#saveRDS(hist_wbm, "data/park/MORA/hist_wbm.rds")
#saveRDS(fut_wbm, "data/park/MORA/fut_wbm.rds")

hist_wbm <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/hist_wbm.rds")
fut_wbm <- readRDS("data/park/MORA/fut_wbm.rds")

```

## - Differentials

Here, we apply the NPS scenario selection method to identify 4 GCMs that 
represent "hot dry", "warm dry", "hot wet", and "warm wet" climate scenarios and 
then, of those, we select the two end members that produce the maximum and 
minimum runoff, which is the key variable related to water supply.

First calculate differentials (future - baseline) for all climate & WBM data 
stats

```{r}

# Combine hist and fut wbm. All indicates still separate grid cells
# hist_wbm is a list: [[1]] daily results, [[2]] per-cell parameters/final
# conditions (used to start the future run). Bind only the daily results.
wbm_all <- hist_wbm[[1]] %>%
  bind_rows(fut_wbm) %>%
  as.data.table() %>%
  left_join(all_cfs, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_gal_edith_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * system_watershed_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
                runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm/12) * down_edith_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
                runoff_gal_paradise_wbm = (runoff_in_wbm/12) * paradise_watershed_ft2 * cf_to_gal)

# Clear space
rm(hist_wbm, fut_wbm)
gc()

all_clim_stats <- wbm_all %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                stat_period = 
                  ifelse(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2], "Baseline",
                      ifelse(year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2], "Future", "Other"))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stat_period == "Other",
                stat_period != "Baseline" | GCM == "GridMET") %>%
  dplyr::select(GCM, stat_period, Skill, precip_in_wbm, tmean_C, runoff_in_wbm, pet_in_wbm, aet_in_wbm, snow_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, stat_period, Skill) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_precip_in = mean(precip_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   mean_tmean_C = mean(tmean_C),
                   mean_runoff_in = mean(runoff_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   mean_snow_in = mean(snow_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   mean_aet_in = mean(aet_in_wbm) * 365.25,
                   median_runoff_in = quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75) * 365.25,
                   rel_var_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm - mean(runoff_in_wbm)),
                   sd_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm),
                   cv_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm)/mean(runoff_in_wbm),
                   iqr_runoff_in = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75)) - 
                     as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.25)),
                   q90_q10_runoff_in = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.9)) -
                     as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.1)),
                   peak_runoff_in = max(runoff_in_wbm),
                   mean_precip_minus_pet_in = mean(precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm),
                   fract_zero_runoff = sum(runoff_in_wbm == 0) / n() ,
                   .groups = "keep") 

# Extract baseline
baseline <- all_clim_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period == "Baseline")

# Extract future
future <- all_clim_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stat_period == "Baseline")

# Calculate differentials
future_differentials <- future %>%
  dplyr::mutate(delta_precip_in = mean_precip_in - baseline$mean_precip_in,
                delta_tmean_C = mean_tmean_C - baseline$mean_tmean_C,
                delta_runoff_in = mean_runoff_in - baseline$mean_runoff_in,
                delta_aet_in = mean_aet_in - baseline$mean_aet_in,
                delta_runoff_rel_var = rel_var_runoff_in - baseline$rel_var_runoff_in,
                fut_runoff_rel_var = rel_var_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_sd = sd_runoff_in - baseline$sd_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_cv = cv_runoff_in - baseline$cv_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_iqr = iqr_runoff_in - baseline$iqr_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_median = median_runoff_in - baseline$median_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_q90_q10 = q90_q10_runoff_in - baseline$q90_q10_runoff_in,
                delta_snow_in = mean_snow_in - baseline$mean_snow_in,
                delta_runoff_in_peak = peak_runoff_in - baseline$peak_runoff_in,
                delta_precip_minus_pet = mean_precip_minus_pet_in - baseline$mean_precip_minus_pet_in,
                delta_fract_zero_runoff = fract_zero_runoff - baseline$fract_zero_runoff) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::select(GCM, CF), by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::rename(c("centroid_cf" = CF)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(centroid_cf = ifelse(centroid_cf %in% c("Hot Dry","Warm Wet"), centroid_cf ,

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(all_cfs, all_clim_stats, baseline, centroid_cfs, down_edith_ft2, paradise_watershed_ft2, system_watershed_ft2)
gc()
```

## - Hock Calibration

Compare simulated snowpack from the historical (GridMET-driven) WBM run against
observed SNOTEL SWE at Paradise, to assess how well the current `hock_coef`
(set in the `wbm_run_select_grids` chunk above) reproduces observed snow accumulation/melt
timing and magnitude. Note the SNOTEL station is a single point at a lower,
forested elevation, while the WBM grid cells span the full AOI elevation range,
so this is an approximate calibration, not an exact match.

```{r hock_calibration}

# Snowpack from the historical run, already averaged over the two selected
# cells (aggregate = TRUE in wbm_run_select_grids)
hist_wbm_mean <- wbm_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(GCM == "GridMET") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, mean_snowpack = snowpack_in_wbm)

# Observed SNOTEL SWE at Paradise
snotel_paradise <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "Paradise") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, swe_in)

# --- Quantitative fit, across the full period of overlap ---
hock_compare <- snotel_paradise %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(hist_wbm_mean, by = "date") %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(swe_in, mean_snowpack)

rmse_val <- Metrics::rmse(hock_compare$swe_in, hock_compare$mean_snowpack)

# Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (1 = perfect fit, 0 = no better than the observed
# mean, <0 = worse than the observed mean). Hand-computed since hydroGOF isn't
# in setup.R - flag if you'd rather add that package and use NSE() directly.
nse_val <- 1 - sum((hock_compare$swe_in - hock_compare$mean_snowpack)^2) /
  sum((hock_compare$swe_in - mean(hock_compare$swe_in))^2)

message("Hock coef: ", hock_coef,
       " | RMSE: ", round(rmse_val, 2), " in",
       " | NSE: ", round(nse_val, 3))

# Collect model fit statistics so they are saved to a table (written in the
# run-methods chunk), not only printed to the console.
fit_stats <- tibble::tibble(
  model = "Hock snowmelt calibration (WBM vs. Paradise SNOTEL SWE)",
  statistic = c("hock_coef", "RMSE (in)", "NSE", "overlap_start", "overlap_end"),
  value = c(as.character(hock_coef), signif(rmse_val, 4), signif(nse_val, 4),
            as.character(min(hock_compare$date)), as.character(max(hock_compare$date))))

# --- Visual check for one selected water year ---
# calc_water_year() is sourced from src/calc_water_year.R via setup.R
calibration_water_year <- 2020

hist_wbm_mean_wy <- hist_wbm_mean %>%
  dplyr::mutate(water_year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(water_year == calibration_water_year)

ggplot(hist_wbm_mean_wy %>%
    dplyr::left_join(snotel_paradise, by = "date"),
  aes(x = date)
) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_snowpack, color = "WBM MEAN"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = swe_in, color = "SNOTEL"), linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Snowpack (in)",
       title = paste0("Water Year ", calibration_water_year,
                      " | Hock Coef: ", hock_coef, " | Overall NSE: ", round(nse_val, 2))) +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("WBM MEAN" = "black", "SNOTEL" = "#b02a24")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(paste0("data/park/MORA/Figs/2024_Hock_", hock_coef, "_WY", calibration_water_year, ".jpg"),
      width = 5, height = 4, dpi = 600)


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
# hock_coef is kept: the Nisqually basin WBM run below uses it.
rm(calibration_water_year, hist_wbm_mean, hist_wbm_mean_wy, hock_compare, nse_val, rmse_val, snotel_paradise)
gc()
```

To calibrate, adjust `hock_coef` in the `wbm_run_select_grids` chunk above, rerun the historical
WBM (and this section), and compare RMSE/NSE across attempts - higher NSE and
lower RMSE indicate a better match to observed SNOTEL SWE.

Classic NPS climate-future selection plots temperature and precipitation deltas
against each other to define "hot/warm" x "wet/dry" corners (demonstrated above).
For MORA, snow -- not temperature -- turns out to be the bigger driver of runoff
change, so we re-run the same selection method (Amber's method) with delta snow
and delta precip on the axes instead, producing "Snowy Wet" and "Less Snowy Dry"
as the two climate futures that bound the runoff-change end members. This snow-based
selection is what propagates through the rest of the analysis.
for MORA, when we do that, we quickly see that temperature and precip aren't the two end members that describe the greatest variance. Rather, it is total precip and total snow. We start with the classic and then demonstrate the snow version- and move forward with snow. 

```{r hot_dry_warm_wet}

y <- "delta_precip_in"

high_y = "Wet"
low_y = "Dry"

# Run selection function (Amber's method)

                                      x = x,

                                      y_name = y_name,

# Extract selected

  dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Warm Wet", "Warm Dry", "Hot Wet", "Hot Dry")) %>%

selected_gcms[[2]]

                     dplyr::select(c(GCM, "select_CF" = CF)), by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM_Meta = case_when(centroid_cf == "Low Skill" ~ "Low Skill",
                                     !is.na(select_CF) ~ select_CF,
                                     TRUE ~ "Other")) # CF, GCM_Meta))
                    
                    , aes(x = reorder(GCM, delta_runoff_in), 
                                                   y = delta_runoff_in, 
                                              fill = GCM_Meta)) +
                                              #fill = centroid_cf)) +  
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_wsva() +
  #theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  labs(x = "", y = "Change in Annual Runoff (in)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 76, vjust = 0.5, hjust=.5)) +

  # contrast outright (gray80 -> the validated "Other" gray; the pale
  # rosybrown1/#c1dff5 pastels -> readable warm/cool steps).
  scale_fill_manual("", 
                    values = c(nps_pal$red, 
                               "lightblue", 
                               "black", 
                               "gray70", 
                               "pink", 
                               nps_pal$blue), 
                               na.value="gray20")


ggsave(filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/differentials_ww_hd.tiff", width = 7, height = 5,  dpi = 600)
```

```{r routing_nisqually_compare_to_vic}
# Clean data - apply multiplier to runoff

# Optional
scale_factor <- 1



mod_dat <- usgs_discharge_bf %>% 
              dplyr::filter(year(time) > 1980) %>%

                            discharge_m3s = 0.0283168 * value,

  ungroup()

ggplot(mod_dat, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = runoff_m3s))

cal_dat <- mod_dat %>%
 dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% c(min(year(vic_dat$date)):max(year(vic_dat$date))))


# --- Routing parameter optimization (maximize NSE) -------------------------
# Previously set by hand (tau_q = 3, tau_s = 100, vs = 0.34, loss = 0). Here
# the parameters are fit to observed discharge in two steps: (1) a random
# search over the ranges below, then (2) bounded local optimization
# (L-BFGS-B) started from the best few random sets. To fix a parameter, set
# its lower and upper bounds equal. Routing runs over the full record (from
# 1981) so the slow store is warmed up before the evaluation period; NSE is
# scored only on the calibration dates (the VIC overlap, cal_dat).
routing_bounds <- tibble::tribble(
  ~param,  ~lower, ~upper,
  "tau_q",    0.5,     30,   # quickflow recession (days)
  "tau_s",     10,    400,   # slowflow recession (days)
  "vs",      0.05,   0.99,   # fraction of runoff routed as slowflow
  "loss",       0,    0.5    # fraction of slowflow lost to deep groundwater
)
routing_n_random <- 500      # random parameter sets in step 1
routing_n_starts <- 5        # best random sets used as optim() starts

routing_input <- mod_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(runoff_m3s)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(date)
routing_cal_idx <- routing_input$date %in% cal_dat$date

# NSE for one named parameter vector
routing_nse <- function(par) {
  sim <- runoff_routing_gw(df = routing_input,
                           runoff_col = "runoff_m3s",
                           date_col = "date",
                           tau_q = par[["tau_q"]],
                           tau_s = par[["tau_s"]],
                           vs = par[["vs"]],
                           loss = par[["loss"]],
                           baseflow = 0,
                           delay = 0,
                           slow_only = TRUE,
                           max_inf = 5000)$Q_tot
  NSE(obs = routing_input$discharge_m3s[routing_cal_idx], sim = sim[routing_cal_idx])
}

free_par  <- routing_bounds$lower < routing_bounds$upper
fixed_par <- stats::setNames(routing_bounds$lower[!free_par], routing_bounds$param[!free_par])
full_par  <- function(x) c(stats::setNames(x, routing_bounds$param[free_par]), fixed_par)

# Step 1: random search
set.seed(2026)
routing_random <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(routing_n_random), function(i) {
  x <- stats::runif(sum(free_par), routing_bounds$lower[free_par], routing_bounds$upper[free_par])
  tibble::as_tibble_row(c(full_par(x), nse = routing_nse(full_par(x))))
}) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(nse))

# Step 2: bounded local optimization from the best random sets
routing_fits <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(routing_n_starts), function(i) {
  start <- unlist(routing_random[i, routing_bounds$param[free_par]])
  fit <- stats::optim(par = start,
                      fn = function(x) -routing_nse(full_par(x)),
                      method = "L-BFGS-B",
                      lower = routing_bounds$lower[free_par],
                      upper = routing_bounds$upper[free_par])
  tibble::as_tibble_row(c(full_par(fit$par), nse = -fit$value, convergence = fit$convergence))
}) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(nse))

routing_best <- as.list(routing_fits[1, ])
routing_fits
routing_best

# Split-sample check of the best set: NSE in each half of the calibration
# period. A large drop between halves would point to overfitting.
routing_halves <- split(seq_along(routing_input$date)[routing_cal_idx],
                        routing_input$date[routing_cal_idx] <
                          stats::median(routing_input$date[routing_cal_idx]))
routing_best_sim <- runoff_routing_gw(df = routing_input, runoff_col = "runoff_m3s", date_col = "date",
                                      tau_q = routing_best$tau_q, tau_s = routing_best$tau_s,
                                      vs = routing_best$vs, loss = routing_best$loss,
                                      slow_only = TRUE, max_inf = 5000)$Q_tot
routing_split <- tibble::tibble(
  period = c("First half", "Second half"),
  start = purrr::map_chr(routing_halves[c("TRUE", "FALSE")], ~ as.character(min(routing_input$date[.x]))),
  end   = purrr::map_chr(routing_halves[c("TRUE", "FALSE")], ~ as.character(max(routing_input$date[.x]))),
  nse   = purrr::map_dbl(routing_halves[c("TRUE", "FALSE")],
                         ~ NSE(obs = routing_input$discharge_m3s[.x], sim = routing_best_sim[.x])))
routing_split

readr::write_csv(dplyr::bind_rows(routing_fits %>% dplyr::mutate(step = "optim"),
                                  routing_random %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
                                    dplyr::mutate(step = "random (top 20)")),
                 "data/park/MORA/Tables/nisqually_routing_optim.csv")

# Run routing model with the optimized parameters (full record for warm-up,
# then kept to the calibration dates)
routing <-  runoff_routing_gw(df = routing_input,
                                 runoff_col = "runoff_m3s",
                                 date_col = "date",
                                 tau_q = routing_best$tau_q,
                                 tau_s = routing_best$tau_s,
                                 vs = routing_best$vs,
                                 loss = routing_best$loss,
                                 baseflow = 0,
                                 delay = 0,
                                 slow_only = TRUE,
                                 return_components = TRUE,
                                 max_inf = 5000) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(cal_dat, by = "date")

  geom_line(data = vic_dat, aes(x = date, y = streamflow_cms, color = "Modeled VIC", linetype = "Modeled VIC"), linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
```
