## - Edith Routing

```{r}

observed_flow <- data.frame(date = c(as.Date("2026-09-03")),
                            flow_cfs = c(1.0),
                            CF = "Observed")

### Now - apply a routing Model to Edith Creek - note that we have no data for this

gpd_to_cfs <- function(gpd) {
  gpd / 646316.928
}

gpm_to_cfs <- function(gpm) {
  gpm / 448.831
}

# 1. Define parameter grid ranges
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  tau_q = seq(1, 15, length.out = 10),
  tau_s = seq(25, 60, length.out = 10),
  vs    = seq(0.6, 0.99, length.out = 10)
)

# Run runoff_routing_gw across every row of param_grid for ONE runoff
# column, returning the row-wise min/mean/max routed discharge (gal/day)
# across the parameter ensemble. Factored out so the same 1,000-combination
# sweep can be applied to all three candidate systems' runoff series below
# instead of copy-pasting it per system.
route_ensemble <- function(dates, runoff_gal, param_grid) {
  simulations <- purrr::pmap(param_grid, function(tau_q, tau_s, vs) {
    res <- runoff_routing_gw(
      # Explicitly name these V1/V2 - data.table(dates, runoff_gal) would
      # otherwise name the columns after the bare argument symbols
      # ("dates"/"runoff_gal") rather than falling back to V1/V2 like the
      # original data.table(current_df$date, current_df$runoff_gal_edith_wbm)
      # call did (deparse.level=1 only auto-names V1/V2 for non-symbol
      # expressions), which is what broke date_col/runoff_col below.
      df = data.table(V1 = dates, V2 = runoff_gal),
      tau_q = tau_q,
      tau_s = tau_s,
      vs = vs,
      runoff_col = "V2",
      date_col = "V1",
      return_components = FALSE
    )
    # Extract routed discharge vector
    res[[2]]
  })
  # Combine results into a matrix (rows = time steps, cols = parameter iterations)
  sim_matrix <- do.call(cbind, simulations)
  tibble::tibble(
    min  = apply(sim_matrix, 1, min,  na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = apply(sim_matrix, 1, mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    max  = apply(sim_matrix, 1, max,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# 2. Run routing across parameter space and summarize by group, for all
# three candidate systems (Edith Current, Edith Downstream, Paradise GW) so
# each has its own discharge range - not just Edith Current as before. This
# triples the routing runtime of this chunk (three ensembles instead of
# one, per GCM x CF group).
wbm <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {
    current_df <- .x

    edith      <- route_ensemble(current_df$date, current_df$runoff_gal_edith_wbm, param_grid)
    down_edith <- route_ensemble(current_df$date, current_df$runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm, param_grid)
    paradise   <- route_ensemble(current_df$date, current_df$runoff_gal_paradise_wbm, param_grid)

    # Calculate row-wise summary metrics across parameter runs, per system
    current_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        min_edith_discharge  = edith$min,
        mean_edith_discharge = edith$mean,
        max_edith_discharge  = edith$max,
        min_down_edith_discharge  = down_edith$min,
        mean_down_edith_discharge = down_edith$mean,
        max_down_edith_discharge  = down_edith$max,
        min_paradise_discharge  = paradise$min,
        mean_paradise_discharge = paradise$mean,
        max_paradise_discharge  = paradise$max
      )
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


ggplot(wbm %>% dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% c(2025, 2026),
                             CF == "Historical"),
       aes(x = date, y = gpd_to_cfs(mean_edith_discharge), color = CF)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = gpd_to_cfs(min_edith_discharge), 
                  ymax = gpd_to_cfs(max_edith_discharge), fill = CF), alpha = 0.2, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = observed_flow, aes(x = date, y = flow_cfs, color = CF, fill = CF)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = gpm_to_cfs(80), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Discharge (cfs)") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors)

# Second figure: general change in hydrograph shape from historical to each
# future period, for all three candidate systems. Grid: rows = system
# (Edith Current / Edith Downstream / Paradise GW), columns = future CF
# (Less Snowy Dry / Snowy Wet). Each panel overlays the Historical DOY
# hydrograph (gray - mean daily discharge +- min/max across years in
# hist_yrs) against that column's future scenario (colored - same, across
# years in fut_yrs), so the historical rows are duplicated into both future
# columns to appear alongside each one.
hydro_grid_dat <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(doy = yday(date), year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2] |
                year >= fut_yrs[1]  & year <= fut_yrs[2]) %>%
  dplyr::select(doy, year, CF, GCM,
                `Edith Current`    = mean_edith_discharge,
                `Edith Downstream` = mean_down_edith_discharge,
                `Paradise GW`      = mean_paradise_discharge) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(`Edith Current`, `Edith Downstream`, `Paradise GW`),
                       names_to = "system", values_to = "discharge_gpd") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = c("Edith Current", "Edith Downstream", "Paradise GW")),
                # gpd -> gpm, matching the discharge units used in the
                # Snowmelt Timing and Fraction section.
                discharge_gpm = discharge_gpd / 1440) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, CF, doy) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(disc_min  = min(discharge_gpm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   disc_mean = mean(discharge_gpm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   disc_max  = max(discharge_gpm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31"))

future_cfs <- c("Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")

# Duplicate the Historical rows into both future-scenario columns so each
# panel can show Historical + that column's future together; "panel_cf"
# drives the facet column, "CF" (unchanged - stays "Historical" for the
# duplicated rows) drives the color so Historical stays gray in every panel
# and each future keeps its own plot_colors color.
hydro_grid_plot_dat <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  hydro_grid_dat %>%
    dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>%
    tidyr::crossing(panel_cf = future_cfs),
  hydro_grid_dat %>%
    dplyr::filter(CF %in% future_cfs) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(panel_cf = CF)
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(panel_cf = factor(panel_cf, levels = future_cfs),
                CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

# Edith Current's actual diversion/treatment capacity (used in the
# tank_storage simulation above) is tiny relative to catchment discharge;
# overlay it on the Edith Current row only, to show the system never
# captures more than a small fraction of Edith Creek's flow, regardless of
# climate future. Uses 80 gpm, the higher of the two seasonal rates.
treatment_capacity_ref <- tibble::tibble(system = "Edith Current", yint = 80)

hydro_shift_fig <- ggplot(hydro_grid_plot_dat, aes(x = doy_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = disc_min, ymax = disc_max, fill = CF), alpha = 0.3, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = disc_mean, group = CF), color = "black", lwd = 1.2, lineend = "round") +
  geom_line(aes(y = disc_mean, color = CF), lwd = 0.8, lineend = "round") +
  geom_hline(data = treatment_capacity_ref, aes(yintercept = yint),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(system ~ panel_cf, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Mean Daily Discharge (gpm)",
       subtitle = "Dashed line (Edith Current only) = current diversion/treatment capacity (up to 80 gpm)") +
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"),
        strip.text = element_text(colour = "black", face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1))

hydro_shift_fig

ggsave(hydro_shift_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/hydrograph_shift_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 9, height = 8)

# Summary of the routed hydrographs (Appendix B): timing and size of the peak
# in the mean daily hydrograph, and mean late-summer (August-September)
# discharge, by system and climate future.
hydrograph_summary <- hydro_grid_dat %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(peak_date = format(doy_date[which.max(disc_mean)], "%b %d"),
                   peak_doy = doy[which.max(disc_mean)],
                   peak_gpm = max(disc_mean),
                   aug_sep_mean_gpm = mean(disc_mean[doy >= 213 & doy <= 273]),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(peak_shift_days = peak_doy[CF == "Historical"] - peak_doy,
                aug_sep_pct_change = 100 * (aug_sep_mean_gpm / aug_sep_mean_gpm[CF == "Historical"] - 1)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

print(hydrograph_summary)
readr::write_csv(hydrograph_summary, "data/park/MORA/Tables/hydrograph_summary.csv")

rm(hydro_grid_dat, hydro_grid_plot_dat, future_cfs)


# Now, for temporal aggregation, some variables require mean, other's sum,
# and for snowpack, we'll look at the maximum annual snowpack.
mean_cols <- c("soil_in_wbm", "tmean_F", "tmean_C")
sum_cols <- c("precip_in_wbm", "runoff_in_wbm", "rain_in_wbm",
              "snow_in_wbm", "melt_in_wbm", "aet_in_wbm", "pet_in_wbm",
              "runoff_gal_edith_wbm", 
              "runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm",
              "runoff_gal_paradise_wbm",
              "mean_edith_discharge", "min_edith_discharge", "max_edith_discharge",
              "mean_down_edith_discharge", "min_down_edith_discharge", "max_down_edith_discharge",
              "mean_paradise_discharge", "min_paradise_discharge", "max_paradise_discharge")
max_cols <- c("snowpack_in_wbm")

wbm_annual <- wbm %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                month = month(date)) %>%
                #year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year,GCM,CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Summarize specific columns with sum()
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Summarize all other columns with mean()
    across(all_of(sum_cols), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(max_cols), \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

wbm_monthly <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Summarize specific columns with sum()
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Summarize all other columns with mean()
    across(all_of(sum_cols), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(max_cols), \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# Percentage Changes
wbm_stats <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::filter((year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) | (year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmean_F = mean(tmean_F),
                   precip_in = mean(precip_in_wbm),
                   rain_in = mean(rain_in_wbm),
                   snow_in = mean(snow_in_wbm),
                   melt_in = mean(melt_in_wbm),
                   aet_in = mean(aet_in_wbm),
                   pet_in = mean(pet_in_wbm),
                   runoff_in = mean(runoff_in_wbm)) %>%
  # Calculate percentage changes
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), 
                ~ (. - .[CF == "Historical"]) / .[CF == "Historical"] * 100)) %>%
  filter(CF != "Historical")

print(wbm_stats)

# Create table of monthly mean, max, min, sd, and cv of historical visitors
monthly_visitor_proportions <- visitors %>%
           dplyr::group_by(month) %>%

                            TV_cv = TV_sd / TV_mean,
                            PV_mean = mean(ParadiseVisitors,na.rm = TRUE),
                            PV_max = max(ParadiseVisitors,na.rm = TRUE),
                            PV_min = min(ParadiseVisitors, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
           dplyr::mutate(month_date = as_date(paste0("2000-",month,"-01")),

                       values = c("Paradise" = pal$orange, "Total" = pal$darkblue)) +
    theme_wsva(), 
  ggplot(visitors, aes(x = TotalVisitors, y = ParadiseVisitors, color = year(ym))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Total Visitors", y = "Paradise Visitors") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = pal$darkblue) +
  theme_wsva(),
  common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom")



# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(visitors_an)
gc()
```



Now, we'll develop a model to estimate future visitation. We'll develop a couple of models and select the one that performs best. National Park visitation has a complex set of drivers, many which we are beyond our ability to forecast. Here,  we account for two major drivers of visitation: overall population increase and weather. 

```{r run-methods}

vis_clim_df <- wbm_monthly %>%
                     select(ym, tmean_F, snowpack_in_wbm, CF) %>% 
                    dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  left_join(visitors %>% dplyr::select(-BusPassengers),
                   by = "ym")


OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR <- 2025   # first year the future scenarios begin
FUTURE_END_YEAR <- 2099   # last year present

# output_resolution = "monthly" is used for every method below so that each
# result carries BOTH $annual and $monthly (the annual envelope is always
# computed regardless of output_resolution; requesting "monthly" additionally
# disaggregates it) -- this lets Figure 1 (annual) and Figure 2 (monthly)
# below both be built from the same set of method calls, run once.

# linear_trend and annual_growth_rate run first, matching their order in the
# sections above (simplest, least data-hungry methods first); linear_trend
# is run WITHOUT climate (its intended baseline/sanity-check role) and
# annual_growth_rate is climate-blind by design. The remaining three methods
# all use tmean_F as their climate predictor.
lin_res <- project_visitation(
  df = vis_clim_df, method = "linear_trend",
  visitor_col = "ParadiseVisitors",
  obs_cutoff_year = OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, future_end_year = FUTURE_END_YEAR,
  output_resolution = "monthly"
)

# Climate-blind by design -- growth_rate_mid = 0.05 (5%/yr) matches how the
# park has historically estimated visitation growth. No climate_vars/
# temp_var argument here, since this method doesn't use one.
growth_res <- project_visitation(
  df = vis_clim_df, method = "annual_growth_rate",
  visitor_col = "ParadiseVisitors", growth_rate_mid = 0.05,
  obs_cutoff_year = OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, future_end_year = FUTURE_END_YEAR,
  output_resolution = "monthly"
)

gam_res <- project_visitation(
  df = vis_clim_df, method = "gam_logistic",
  visitor_col = "ParadiseVisitors", climate_vars = c("tmean_F"),
  obs_cutoff_year = OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, future_end_year = FUTURE_END_YEAR,
  output_resolution = "monthly"
)

arima_res <- project_visitation(
  df = vis_clim_df, method = "arima_climate",
  visitor_col = "ParadiseVisitors", climate_vars = c("tmean_F", "snowpack_in_wbm"),
  obs_cutoff_year = OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, future_end_year = FUTURE_END_YEAR,
  output_resolution = "monthly"
)

fis_res <- project_visitation(
  df = vis_clim_df, method = "fisichelli",
  visitor_col = "ParadiseVisitors", temp_var = "tmean_F",
  obs_cutoff_year = OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, future_end_year = FUTURE_END_YEAR,
  output_resolution = "monthly"
)

method_levels <- c(
  "Linear Trend\n(linear_trend)",
  "Annual Growth Rate\n(annual_growth_rate, 5%/yr)",
  "GAM + Logistic Growth\n(gam_logistic)",
  "ARIMA + Climate\n(arima_climate)",
  "Fisichelli et al. (2015)\n(fisichelli)"
)

all_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lin_res$annual    %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[1]),
  growth_res$annual %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[2]),
  gam_res$annual    %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[3]),
  arima_res$annual  %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[4]),
  fis_res$annual    %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[5])
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(method = factor(method, levels = method_levels))

all_results_monthly <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lin_res$monthly    %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[1]),
  growth_res$monthly %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[2]),
  gam_res$monthly    %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[3]),
  arima_res$monthly  %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[4]),
  fis_res$monthly    %>% dplyr::mutate(method = method_levels[5])
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(method = factor(method, levels = method_levels))

# Validated for adjacent-legend/facet-strip comparison (this figure facets
# by method, so the strip label is the secondary encoding the one
# CVD warn-band pair - rust vs green - calls for).
method_colors <- stats::setNames(
  c("#1b6ca8", "#1a7a4c", "#b0431f", "#6a3d9a", "#8a6d00"),
  method_levels
)

# Annual Plot models
obs_dat <- dplyr::filter(all_results, source == "observed")

proj_dat <- all_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(source == "projected") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ribbon_low  = pmin(visitors_low, visitors_high),
                ribbon_high = pmax(visitors_low, visitors_high))

fig_comparison_annual <- ggplot(all_results, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = proj_dat, aes(ymin = ribbon_low, ymax = ribbon_high, fill = method),
              alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = obs_dat, aes(y = visitors_mid), color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = proj_dat, aes(y = visitors_mid, color = method), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray40") +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = method_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual Visitors") +
#       title = "Comparison of Visitation Projection Methods: Paradise") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(fig_comparison_annual)

# Also save a standalone copy of the figure into this same folder, in case
# it's needed outside of the knit Word document (e.g. embedded elsewhere).
ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/vis_method_comparison_figure.png", 
       fig_comparison_annual, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 600)


# Monthly Plot Models
obs_dat_m <- dplyr::filter(all_results_monthly, source == "observed")

proj_dat_m <- all_results_monthly %>%
  dplyr::filter(source == "projected") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ribbon_low  = pmin(visitors_low, visitors_high),
                ribbon_high = pmax(visitors_low, visitors_high))

fig_comparison_monthly <- ggplot(all_results_monthly, aes(x = ym)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = proj_dat_m, aes(ymin = ribbon_low, ymax = ribbon_high, fill = method),
              alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = obs_dat_m, aes(y = visitors_mid), color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = proj_dat_m, aes(y = visitors_mid, color = method), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(as.Date(paste0(OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, "-01-01"))),
             linetype = "dotted", color = "gray40") +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = method_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Monthly Visitors") +
#       title = "Comparison of Visitation Projection Methods: Paradise") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(fig_comparison_monthly)

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/vis_comparison_figure_monthly.png", 
       fig_comparison_monthly, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 600)

ggarrange(
  fig_comparison_annual, 
  fig_comparison_monthly, 
  ncol = 1, 
  labels = c("a)", "b)"),
  font.label = list(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "black")
)

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/vis_comp_all.png",
       width = 7, height = 8, dpi = 600)

# Model Stats
gam_r2      <- summary(gam_res$gam_model)$r.sq

# GAM fit diagnostics (observed vs. modeled, residuals, 1:1), Appendix A
ggsave(gam_res$gam_diagnostics, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/gam_fit_fig.jpg",
       width = 6.5, height = 8, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
lin_r2      <- summary(lin_res$lm_model)$r.squared
lin_slope   <- coef(lin_res$lm_model)[["year"]]
arima_order <- forecast::arimaorder(arima_res$arima_model)
arima_aic   <- arima_res$arima_model$aic

fit_stats <- fit_stats %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(
    model = "Visitation models (Appendix A, Table A2)",
    statistic = c("GAM R2 (adj.)", "Linear R2", "Linear slope (visitors/yr)",
                  "ARIMA order (p,d,q)", "ARIMA AIC"),
    value = c(signif(gam_r2, 4), signif(lin_r2, 4), signif(lin_slope, 4),
              paste(arima_order, collapse = ","), signif(arima_aic, 4))))
print(fit_stats)
readr::write_csv(fit_stats, "data/park/MORA/Tables/fit_stats.csv")


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(FUTURE_END_YEAR, OBS_CUTOFF_YEAR, all_results, all_results_monthly, arima_res, fig_comparison_annual, fig_comparison_monthly, fis_res, growth_res, lin_res, obs_dat, obs_dat_m, proj_dat, proj_dat_m, vis_clim_df, visitors)
gc()
```

The GAM logistic model offers the most practical projections. Move forward with 
that method for monthly and annual projections

```{r select_vis}

monthly_visitation <- gam_res$monthly %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = case_when(year(ym) < 2026 ~ "Historical",
                                  year(ym) >= fut_yrs[1] & year(ym) <= fut_yrs[2] ~ "Projected",
                                  TRUE ~ "Other"))

annual_visitation <- gam_res$annual %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(year < 2026 ~ "Historical",
                           year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2] ~ "Projected",
                           TRUE ~ "Other"))

monthly_visitor_proportions <- calc_monthly_proportions(df = monthly_visitation %>%
                                                          dplyr::filter(visitors_mid > 0), # drop 0 - likely recording error
                                                        date_col = "ym",
                                                        value_col = "visitors_mid",
                                                        group_vars = "group",
                                                        monthly_agg_fun = "sum") %>%
  rename(c("mean_vis" = "mean_val",
           "min_vis" = "min_val",
            "max_vis" = "max_val"))

ggplot(monthly_visitor_proportions %>% dplyr::filter(group != "Other"), 
       aes(x = month_date, y = mean_vis * fraction, color = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_vis * fraction, ymax = max_vis * fraction, fill = group), alpha = 0.3, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +

  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Historical" = pal$darkblue, "Projected" = pal$orange)) +

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.

## - Water use

Public water suppliers are required to report useage to the state. However, at
many parks, there are no available records for water use. Use this section to
search for or bring in water use data. If none are avaailable, estimate
using per-visitor use rates. 

```{r load_wateruse}

# 1. Load Daily Data & Aggregate safely by Year-Month
wateruse_daily <- read_excel(
  "data/park/MORA/MORA_wateruse_visitation_climate/MORA_water demand_visitation analysis.xlsx",
  sheet = "Daily_final"
) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    date,
    use_gal = actul_usage_gal,
    turbidity_ntu = turbidity_fin
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    use_gal = as.numeric(use_gal),
    turbidity_ntu = as.numeric(turbidity_ntu)
  )

# Full daily turbidity record, kept separate from wateruse_daily (which is
# cleaned up below) so it survives for the turbidity/precipitation section.
turbidity_daily <- wateruse_daily %>%
  dplyr::select(date, turbidity_ntu)

daily_monthly_agg <- wateruse_daily %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Require at least 25 valid daily entries to consider the monthly sum complete
    use_gal_from_daily = if (sum(!is.na(use_gal)) >= 25) sum(use_gal, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Load Monthly Data, Join, and Coalesce
wateruse_monthly <- read_excel(
  "data/park/MORA/MORA_wateruse_visitation_climate/MORA_water demand_visitation analysis.xlsx",
  sheet = "Monthly_final"
) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ym = cal_month_year,
    use_gal = actual_usage_gal
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ym = floor_date(as.Date(ym), "month"),
    use_gal = as.numeric(use_gal)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(ym = seq.Date(min(ym), max(ym), by = "month")) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(daily_monthly_agg, by = "ym") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pre_interp_use = dplyr::coalesce(use_gal, use_gal_from_daily),
    total_use = zoo::na.approx(pre_interp_use, na.rm = FALSE),
    source = dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(use_gal) ~ "Reported Monthly",
      is.na(use_gal) & !is.na(use_gal_from_daily) ~ "Imputed from Daily",
      is.na(pre_interp_use) & !is.na(total_use) ~ "Interpolated",
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    )
  )

wateruse_annual <- wateruse_monthly %>%
  mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  filter(total_use >= 0,
         !is.na(total_use)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  filter(n() == 12) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    total_use = sum(total_use, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  

# Plot Monthly Water Use

ggarrange(
ggplot(wateruse_monthly, aes(x = ym)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = total_use), color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = total_use, color = source, shape = source), size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Data Source",
    values = c("Reported Monthly" = nps_pal$blue, 
               "Imputed from Daily" = nps_pal$red, 
               "Interpolated" = "#595959")) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Data Source",
                    values = c("Reported Monthly" = 16, 
                               "Imputed from Daily" = 17, 
                               "Interpolated" = 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k gal")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Monthly Water Use (gal)") +
  theme_wsva(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ),

ggplot(wateruse_annual, aes(x = year, y = total_use)) +
  geom_line(color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = nps_pal$blue, size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k gal")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty()) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Annual Water Use (gal)"
  ) +
  theme_wsva(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ),
ncol = 1, align = "hv")

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/observed_water_use.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 5)



# Workspace cleanup
rm(daily_monthly_agg)
gc()



# Observed daily use, summarized here because wateruse_daily is removed below
# (used in the water use summary table). Days with zero or missing use are
# treated as unmetered.
observed_daily_summary <- wateruse_daily %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(use_gal), use_gal > 0) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(first_date = min(date),
                   last_date = max(date),
                   n_days = dplyr::n(),
                   mean_daily_gal = mean(use_gal),
                   max_daily_gal = max(use_gal),
                   max_daily_date = date[which.max(use_gal)])

# Peak-day to average-day ratio within each well-metered month (>= 25 days),
# a check on the assumption that peak daily use is about twice the average
# daily use for the month
daily_peak_ratio <- wateruse_daily %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(use_gal), use_gal > 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 25) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_daily_gal = mean(use_gal),
                   max_daily_gal = max(use_gal),
                   peak_ratio = max_daily_gal / mean_daily_gal,
                   .groups = "drop")

print(observed_daily_summary)
print(summary(daily_peak_ratio$peak_ratio))

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(daily_monthly_agg, wateruse_daily)
gc()
```


## - Turbidity and precipitation

Paradise's most consistently reported water quality issue is turbidity, not
a chronic contaminant (see Sep 2025 turbidity event, above, for the single
best-documented episode). Here we look at the full multi-year daily
turbidity record together with daily precipitation at the Paradise SNOTEL
station, to see whether that event-level pattern - elevated turbidity
tracking precipitation - holds more broadly across the record, not just
around the single shutdown event.

```{r turbidity_precip}

# Daily precipitation at Paradise SNOTEL (already computed above, see SNOTEL)
paradise_precip_daily <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "Paradise") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, daily_precip) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(date, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mov_daily_precip = rollsum(daily_precip, 
                                           k = 3, 
                                           align = "right", 
                                           na.pad = TRUE))

# Join the full daily turbidity record to daily precip
turbidity_precip <- turbidity_daily %>%
  dplyr::left_join(paradise_precip_daily, by = "date") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(date) %>%
  dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% c(5,6,7,8,9,10))

# How much of the turbidity record is actually populated? (this is the
# missing data that kept an earlier version of this chunk from running)
turbidity_coverage <- turbidity_precip %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_days_total     = dplyr::n(),
    n_days_turbidity = sum(!is.na(turbidity_ntu)),
    pct_turbidity    = round(100 * n_days_turbidity / n_days_total, 1),
    date_min         = min(date[!is.na(turbidity_ntu)], na.rm = TRUE),
    date_max         = max(date[!is.na(turbidity_ntu)], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(turbidity_coverage)

# Hourly precipitation at Paradise SNOTEL (full record), converted from the
# cumulative PREC.I sensor to an hourly increment (same water-year-reset /
# recalibration handling as the daily series above, see SNOTEL), restricted
# to the same May-Oct window and date range as turbidity_precip.
precip_hourly_full <- snotel_hourly %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "Paradise", sensor_id == "PREC.I") %>%
  # De-duplicate the Daylight Saving "fall back" hour (1am occurs twice in
  # local time each November; the raw pull carries both as separate rows
  # with the same timestamp).
  dplyr::distinct(datetime, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # FIX: datetime comes through as character, not POSIXct -- this worked
    # by accident for string comparisons/sorting so far, but scale_x_datetime()
    # requires a real POSIXct column and errors otherwise.
    datetime = as.POSIXct(datetime),
    water_year = as.numeric(as.character(water_year)),
    value = as.numeric(as.character(value)),
    # A handful of raw readings (9 hours, all water year 2007) are
    # physically impossible for a single water year's cumulative precip at
    # Paradise (up to 2,834 in, vs. a real max nowhere near that -- the
    # 3rd quartile of the whole record is 110.8 in). Almost certainly bad
    # sensor/QC data; flag as missing rather than feed into the diff below.
    value = dplyr::if_else(value > 200, NA_real_, value)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(datetime) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(water_year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    precip_diff = value - dplyr::lag(value),
    # Paradise's real water-year cumulative PREC.I legitimately runs into
    # the 40-150+ in range by mid-to-late season, so a small negative dip
    # from one hour to the next is NOT usually a "reset" -- it's sensor
    # noise (gauge draindown, thermal jitter), a documented SNOTEL quirk.
    # A genuine water-year reset brings the cumulative value back down
    # near zero (Oct 1 restart); only treat it as a reset if it does.
    precip_hourly = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(precip_diff)          ~ NA_real_,  # first reading of the record, or adjacent to a flagged bad value
      precip_diff < 0 & value < 5  ~ value,     # genuine water-year reset
      precip_diff < 0              ~ 0,         # small negative dip: sensor noise, not real "negative rain"
      TRUE                         ~ precip_diff
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    lubridate::month(datetime) %in% 5:10,
    as.Date(datetime) >= min(turbidity_precip$date, na.rm = TRUE),
    as.Date(datetime) <= max(turbidity_precip$date, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(datetime, precip_hourly) %>%
  # FLAG: 20 in/hr is a placeholder outlier ceiling, not yet tied to a
  # known physical maximum -- confirm/replace once we've looked at the
  # real range of plausible hourly totals.
  dplyr::mutate(precip_hourly = dplyr::case_when(
    precip_hourly > 20 ~ NA_real_,
    precip_hourly < 0 ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ precip_hourly),
    mov_precip_hourly = rollsum(precip_hourly, 2, align = "right", na.pad = TRUE))

# Sep 6, 2025 was another documented turbidity event (see Sep 2025 turbidity
# event, above) - mark it on the figure the same way as the precip event
# marker there.
turbidity_event_2025 <- as.Date("2025-09-06")

# Edith Creek reservoir was dredged on July 23, 2024 (reported by Kristen) -
# mark it on the same figure, in a distinct color from the Sep 2025 turbidity
# failure event above, since it is a maintenance action rather than a storm event.
dredge_event_2024 <- as.Date("2024-07-23")

# Full turbidity record (top), 3-day precip sum (middle), and hourly precip
# (bottom), shared x-axis. NOTE: relabeled the middle panel's y-axis from
# "Daily Precip (in)" to "3-Day Precip Sum (in)" to match what's actually
# plotted (mov_daily_precip), which was out of sync with the label above.
turbidity_fig <- ggarrange(
  ggplot(turbidity_precip, aes(x = date, y = turbidity_ntu)) +
    geom_point(color = pal$darkblue, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = turbidity_event_2025, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
    annotate("text", x = turbidity_event_2025, y = Inf, label = "Sep 6, 2025",
             angle = -90,
             vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1, size = 3, color = "firebrick") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dredge_event_2024, linetype = "dashed", color = pal$teal) +
    annotate("text", x = dredge_event_2024, y = Inf, label = "Reservoir dredged",
             angle = -90,
             vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1, size = 3, color = pal$teal) +
    theme_wsva() +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Turbidity (NTU)"),
  ggplot(turbidity_precip, aes(x = date, y = mov_daily_precip)) +
    geom_col(color = "gray40", fill = "gray40", na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = turbidity_event_2025, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = dredge_event_2024, linetype = "dashed", color = pal$teal) +
    theme_wsva() +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "3-Day Precip Sum (in)"),
  ggplot(precip_hourly_full %>% dplyr::filter(lubridate::month(datetime) %in% 5:10),
         aes(x = datetime, y = mov_precip_hourly)) +
    geom_col(color = "gray40", fill = "gray40", na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.POSIXct(turbidity_event_2025), linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = as.POSIXct(dredge_event_2024), linetype = "dashed", color = pal$teal) +
    theme_wsva() +

  ncol = 1, align = "hv"

turbidity_fig

ggsave(turbidity_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/turbidity_precip_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 6)

# Same-day and lagged correlation between turbidity and precip (Spearman,
# since the turbidity-precip relationship isn't necessarily linear) - checks
# whether elevated turbidity tracks precip with a short lag (sediment
# mobilization/travel time) rather than strictly same-day.
turbidity_lag_cor <- purrr::map_dfr(0:3, function(lag_days) {
  dat <- turbidity_precip %>%
    dplyr::mutate(precip_lag = dplyr::lag(daily_precip, lag_days)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(turbidity_ntu), !is.na(precip_lag))
  tibble::tibble(
    lag_days = lag_days,
    n_obs    = nrow(dat),
    cor      = if (nrow(dat) >= 10) cor(dat$turbidity_ntu, dat$precip_lag, method = "spearman") else NA_real_
  )
})

print(turbidity_lag_cor)

# Days with elevated turbidity, and what fraction had measurable precip in
# the prior 3 days. FLAG: 5 NTU is a placeholder threshold, not yet tied to
# an actual regulatory or operational trigger - confirm/replace once we
# know what value(s) actually triggered past shutdowns (e.g., Sep 2025).
turbidity_threshold <- 5

turbidity_events <- turbidity_precip %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(turbidity_ntu)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    precip_prior_3d = zoo::rollapplyr(dplyr::coalesce(daily_precip, 0), 3, sum, partial = TRUE),
    elevated = turbidity_ntu >= turbidity_threshold
  )

turbidity_event_summary <- turbidity_events %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_elevated_days          = sum(elevated, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_elevated_with_precip = round(100 * mean(precip_prior_3d[elevated] > 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )

print(turbidity_event_summary)

## - September 2025 event: SNOTEL precipitation percentiles

Percentile rank of the September 6-7, 2025 window within the full May-Oct hourly and
daily Paradise SNOTEL precipitation distributions, to put the event in context against
the rest of the record (see the hourly precip data-quality fixes above for how
precip_hourly_full was derived).

```{r sep2025_precip_percentiles}

sep2025_dates <- as.Date(c("2025-09-06", "2025-09-07"))

# Hourly percentiles: rank each hourly value and each 2-hr moving sum
# against the full May-Oct hourly record (all years), then pull out the
# Sep 6-7, 2025 window
hourly_pctiles <- precip_hourly_full %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    precip_hourly_pctile = 100 * dplyr::percent_rank(precip_hourly),
    mov_precip_hourly_pctile = 100 * dplyr::percent_rank(mov_precip_hourly)
  )

sep2025_hourly <- hourly_pctiles %>%
  dplyr::filter(as.Date(datetime) %in% sep2025_dates) %>%
  dplyr::select(datetime, precip_hourly, precip_hourly_pctile,
                mov_precip_hourly, mov_precip_hourly_pctile) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(datetime)

print(sep2025_hourly, n = 100)

# Peak hourly value and peak 2-hr moving sum during the event window, with
# their percentile rank against the full hourly record
sep2025_hourly_peak <- sep2025_hourly %>% dplyr::slice_max(precip_hourly, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
sep2025_hourly_2hr_peak <- sep2025_hourly %>% dplyr::slice_max(mov_precip_hourly, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

print(sep2025_hourly_peak)
print(sep2025_hourly_2hr_peak)

# Daily percentiles: rank each daily value and each 3-day moving sum
# against the full May-Oct daily record (all years, from turbidity_precip),

# appears to attribute the event to Sep 7 rather than Sep 6 (see the

daily_pctiles <- turbidity_precip %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

sep2025_daily <- daily_pctiles %>%
  dplyr::filter(date %in% sep2025_dates) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, daily_precip, daily_precip_pctile,
                mov_daily_precip, mov_daily_precip_pctile)

print(sep2025_daily)

## - Antecedent dryness and turbidity

We hypothesized that turbidity spikes are best predicted not by precipitation
alone, but by the combination of (a) how long it has been since the last
comparably large precipitation event and (b) the size of the current event -
a long dry stretch lets fine sediment accumulate before a storm large enough
to mobilize it arrives, so the same storm produces a bigger turbidity
response after a long dry spell than after recent rain has already flushed
the supply. We restrict this analysis to May-Oct: the SNOTEL PREC.I sensor
records all precipitation, including snow water equivalent, and only rain
(not snowfall) drives this kind of sediment mobilization.

```{r turbidity_dryness_metric}

# Restrict to the rain season (May-Oct)
turbidity_rain_season <- turbidity_precip %>%
  dplyr::filter(lubridate::month(date) %in% 5:10) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(date)

# 3-day moving sum of precip (matches the exploratory approach above)
turbidity_rain_season <- turbidity_rain_season %>%
  dplyr::mutate(precip_3day = zoo::rollapplyr(dplyr::coalesce(daily_precip, 0), 3, sum, partial = TRUE))

# "Large" precip event threshold: a single climatological percentile of the
# 3-day sum, pooled across all years' May-Oct records (not computed
# separately per year - a single season only has ~184 days, so a per-year
# percentile would be a noisy, small-sample estimate, and "large" should
# mean the same thing every year for the dry-spell clock below to be
# comparable across years).
large_event_pctile <- 0.90
large_event_threshold <- quantile(turbidity_rain_season$precip_3day, probs = large_event_pctile, na.rm = TRUE)

print(paste0(scales::percent(large_event_pctile), " percentile of 3-day precip sum (May-Oct, all years) = ",
            round(large_event_threshold, 2), " in"))

# Days since the last "large" event, reset each year on May 1 (winter/
# snowmelt provides a fresh sediment supply each spring, so the dry-spell
# clock does not carry over from the previous fall).
turbidity_rain_season <- turbidity_rain_season %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    is_large_event = precip_3day >= large_event_threshold,
    # days elapsed since the start of the season (May 1 = day 0)
    days_into_season = as.numeric(date - min(date)),
    # season-day of the most recent large event on or before this day
    # (NA until the season's first large event occurs)
    last_large_event_day = dplyr::if_else(is_large_event, days_into_season, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::fill(last_large_event_day, .direction = "down") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # before the season's first large event, May 1 (season start) is
    # treated as the dry-spell clock's baseline start
    days_since_large_event = days_into_season - dplyr::coalesce(last_large_event_day, 0)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Percentile rank of each day's antecedent dry spell and event magnitude,
# combined into a single interpretable 0-1 "sediment mobilization
# potential" index (high only when both are high at once).
turbidity_rain_season <- turbidity_rain_season %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    event_magnitude_pctile = dplyr::percent_rank(precip_3day),
    antecedent_dry_pctile   = dplyr::percent_rank(days_since_large_event),
    mobilization_index      = event_magnitude_pctile * antecedent_dry_pctile
  )

# Visualize the hypothesis directly: is turbidity highest where a big event
# (y-axis) follows a long dry spell (x-axis)?
mobilization_fig <- ggplot(turbidity_rain_season %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(turbidity_ntu)),
                           aes(x = days_since_large_event, y = precip_3day,
                               size = turbidity_ntu, color = turbidity_ntu)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = -1) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "Days Since Last Large Precip Event (3-day sum)",
       y = "Current 3-Day Precip Sum (in)",
       size = "Turbidity (NTU)", color = "Turbidity (NTU)",
       title = "Turbidity as a function of antecedent dryness and event size")

mobilization_fig

ggsave(mobilization_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/turbidity_mobilization_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 8, height = 6)

# Regression: does the antecedent-dryness x event-size interaction predict
# turbidity better than either term alone? Response is log1p(turbidity),
# since turbidity is strongly right-skewed (a few very large spikes). We
# test two response definitions, since sediment delivery to the sampling
# point may lag the storm itself by a day or two (see the same-day vs.
# lagged correlation check above): same-day turbidity, and peak turbidity
# over the current day plus the next 3 days.
turbidity_rain_season <- turbidity_rain_season %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    turbidity_peak_3d = zoo::rollapply(turbidity_ntu, width = 4, align = "left",
                                       FUN = function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                                       partial = TRUE, fill = NA)
  )

reg_dat <- turbidity_rain_season %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(precip_3day), !is.na(days_since_large_event))

mod_sameday <- lm(log1p(turbidity_ntu) ~ precip_3day * days_since_large_event,
                  data = reg_dat %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(turbidity_ntu)))

mod_peak3d <- lm(log1p(turbidity_peak_3d) ~ precip_3day * days_since_large_event,
                 data = reg_dat %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(turbidity_peak_3d)))

summary(mod_sameday)
summary(mod_peak3d)

turbidity_models <- data.frame(
  model = c("Same-day turbidity", "Peak turbidity, next 3 days"),
  n = c(nobs(mod_sameday), nobs(mod_peak3d)),
  r_squared = c(summary(mod_sameday)$r.squared, summary(mod_peak3d)$r.squared),
  aic = c(AIC(mod_sameday), AIC(mod_peak3d))
)
print(turbidity_models)
readr::write_csv(turbidity_models, "data/park/MORA/Tables/turbidity_dryness_models.csv")

```

## - Intense precipitation frequency: historical vs. projected

Park staff also noted that roughly 8 inches of rain fell on Paradise in 48
hours around the time of the September 2025 shutdown - a storm on a scale
our own daily turbidity/precipitation data can't directly confirm (the
turbidity record has a gap exactly over that event; see above), but one we
can evaluate using the water balance model's daily precipitation record,
which spans both the historical baseline and the mid-century projection
period. Here we compare the frequency of 2-day rain totals at or above that
8-inch benchmark between the historical baseline (1980-2012) and the
projection period (2035-2064), under both climate futures.

```{r intense_precip_frequency}

# Restrict to the historical baseline (GridMET) and the two selected future
# climate futures, each over its own analysis window.
intense_precip_dat <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    (CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
    (CF %in% c("Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet") & year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(GCM, date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # 2-day (48-hour) rolling sum of RAIN specifically (rain_in_wbm, not
    # precip_in_wbm) -- matches "8 inches of RAIN" as reported, and excludes
    # snow water equivalent, which the total precip variable would include.
    rain_2day = zoo::rollsum(rain_in_wbm, 2, align = "right", fill = NA)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

intense_precip_threshold <- 8  # in, matching the reported Sep 2025 event

# Count distinct STORM EVENTS at/above the threshold, not just days: a
# single multi-day storm can push the 2-day rolling sum over the threshold
# on several consecutive days, which would double- or triple-count one
# event if we just counted days.
count_events <- function(exceeds) {
  r <- rle(exceeds)
  sum(r$values, na.rm = TRUE)
}

intense_precip_summary <- intense_precip_dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(exceeds = !is.na(rain_2day) & rain_2day >= intense_precip_threshold) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, GCM) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_years          = dplyr::n_distinct(year),
    n_events         = count_events(exceeds),
    events_per_yr    = round(n_events / n_years, 3),
    max_2day_rain_in = round(max(rain_2day, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(intense_precip_summary)

# Full distribution of annual-maximum 2-day rain totals, historical vs. each
# future climate future -- shows the shift in the whole tail, not just
# whether the 8 in threshold specifically is crossed.
annual_max_2day <- intense_precip_dat %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, GCM, year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(annual_max_2day_rain = max(rain_2day, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

intense_precip_fig <- ggplot(annual_max_2day, aes(x = CF, y = annual_max_2day_rain, fill = CF)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = intense_precip_threshold, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = plot_colors) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Annual Maximum 2-Day Rain Total (in)",
       subtitle = paste0("Dashed line = ", intense_precip_threshold,
                        " in, the approximate scale of the Sep 2025 event")) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

intense_precip_fig

ggsave(intense_precip_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/intense_precip_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 5)

```

```{r investigate_leak, fig.alt="Two-panel figure comparing Paradise water use before and after the 2019 leak. Left panel: line and shaded min/max ribbon chart of average monthly water use for two periods, pre-June 2019 baseline and post-June 2019 post-leak, with dashed reference lines marking the wastewater treatment plant's average and maximum monthly capacity; post-leak mean use exceeds the average-flow line from May through September but stays below the maximum-month line in every calendar month. Right panel: bar chart of the percent change in average monthly use from baseline to post-leak, labeled with the percentage on each bar; every month shows a substantial increase."}

# Clearly a significant leak started in 2017, and fully sprung in 2019. Now,
# we'll plot monthly average, min, and max values for the pre-2019 period and
# post-2019 leak period, removing one outlier month in June 2017 when the leak
# presumably started but possibly was temporarily fixed.

# In September 2026, Micah. Henderson provided wastewater flow data:
wastewater_flow <- data.frame(
  year = c(2022, 2023, 2024),
  max_day = c(92100,67700,67800),
  max_month = c(52900, 44600, 51900),
  avg_day = c(20200, 21500, 22200),
  design_cap_day = c(91500,91500,91500),
  design_cap_month = c(75000, 75000, 75000)
)

# 1. Segment data into Pre- and Post-June 2019 groups and calculate monthly metrics
monthly_leak_summary <- wateruse_monthly %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(total_use),
                !ym == as.Date("2017-06-01")) %>% # Remove outlier leak event
   dplyr::mutate(period = factor(
     if_else(ym < as.Date("2019-06-01"),
            "Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)",
            "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)"),
        levels = c("Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)", "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)")),
    m_num = month(ym),
    m_label = month(ym, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(period, m_num, m_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    avg_use = mean(total_use, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_use = min(total_use, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_use = max(total_use, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

monthly_pct_change <- monthly_leak_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(m_num, m_label, period, avg_use) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = avg_use) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    absolute_change_gal = post_june_2019_post_leak - pre_june_2019_baseline,
    pct_change = (absolute_change_gal / pre_june_2019_baseline) * 100
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(m_num)

# Reference values: the highest observed maximum-month wastewater flow and
# the mean average-day flow (x 30.5 days) across the three years Micah
# Henderson provided. These are observed flows, not the plant's design
# capacity (75,000 gpd monthly design = ~2.29 Mgal/month, which metered use
# never exceeds). Post-leak monthly mean use exceeds the average-flow line
# May-September (29 of 69 individual post-leak months) and the max-month
# line in 5 of 69 months; pre-leak use exceeds neither. Use above what
# returns to the sewer is consistent with water lost to a supply-side leak.
wastewater_max_month <- wastewater_flow$max_month %>% max() * 30.5
wastewater_avg <- wastewater_flow$avg_day %>% mean() * 30.5

# Plot average monthly profiles with min/max shaded envelope
leak_fig <- ggarrange(
ggplot(monthly_leak_summary, aes(x = m_num, group = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_use, ymax = max_use, fill = period), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = avg_use, color = period), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = avg_use, color = period), size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = wastewater_max_month,
             color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(x = 1, y = wastewater_max_month,
                label = paste0("Max monthly WWTP flow (2022-2024): ",
                               scales::comma(wastewater_max_month), " gal")),
            hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 2.8, color = "gray30",
            fontface = "italic", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = wastewater_avg,
             color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(x = 1, y = wastewater_avg,
                label = paste0("Avg monthly WWTP flow (2022-2024): ",
                               scales::comma(wastewater_avg), " gal")),
            hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 2.8, color = "gray30",
            fontface = "italic", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k gal")) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Period",
                    values = c("Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)" = nps_pal$blue, 
                               "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)" = nps_pal$red)) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Period",
                    values = c("Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)" = nps_pal$blue, 
                               "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)" = nps_pal$red)) +
  labs(title = "Paradise Water Use: Pre- vs. Post-Leak",
       subtitle = "Post-leak summer use exceeds the wastewater plant's average monthly flow,\nconsistent with water lost to a supply-side leak rather than increased consumption",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Monthly Water Usage") +
  theme_wsva(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "gray30", face = "italic"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5)
  ),

# Plot percentage change by month to match the summary plot style
ggplot(monthly_pct_change, aes(x = m_num, y = pct_change)) +
  geom_col(fill = nps_pal$red, alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_change, 0), "%"),
                vjust = if_else(pct_change >= 0, -0.4, 1.2)),
    size = 3,
    color = "gray20") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_percent(scale = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.15))
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Average Monthly Usage Increase (%)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage Change") +
  theme_wsva(base_size = 10) + # legend stays visible (though unused) to keep vertical alignment with p1
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5)
  ),
ncol = 1, align = "hv")

leak_fig
ggsave(leak_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/leak_monthly_fig.jpg",
       width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
rm(leak_fig)


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(breaks, monthly_pct_change)
gc()
```


```{r use_per_visitor}

vis_clim_use <- monthly_visitation %>%
  select(-source) %>%
  left_join(wateruse_monthly %>% select(-source), by = "ym") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(use_per_visitor = total_use / visitors_mid,
                observed_use = total_use)

# Calculate use per visitor - pre and post leak
use_per_visitor <- vis_clim_use %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(use_per_visitor),
                ym != as.Date("2017-06-01")) %>% # Filter outlier as done in previous steps) %>%
   dplyr::mutate(period = factor(
     if_else(ym < as.Date("2019-06-01"),
            "Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)",
            "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)"),
        levels = c("Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)", "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)"))) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(min_observed_use = min(observed_use, na.rm = TRUE),
                   mean_observed_use = mean(observed_use, na.rm = TRUE),
                   max_observed_use = max(observed_use, na.rm = TRUE),
                   min_use = min(use_per_visitor, na.rm = TRUE),
                   mean_use = mean(use_per_visitor, na.rm = TRUE),
                   max_use = max(use_per_visitor, na.rm = TRUE),
                   # Effective rate used for demand: total use / total visitors
                   # over the period (ratio of totals), not the mean of the
                   # monthly ratios above, so high-visitation months carry
                   # proportionally more weight.
                   effective_use = sum(observed_use, na.rm = TRUE) /
                     sum(visitors_mid, na.rm = TRUE))

```{r}

# Therefore, we'll estimate based on visitation

# Use-per-visitor rates, derived directly from the observed pre/post-leak

low_use_per_visitor  <- use_per_visitor$effective_use[use_per_visitor$period == "Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)"]
high_use_per_visitor <- use_per_visitor$effective_use[use_per_visitor$period == "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)"]
mid_use_per_visitor  <- mean(c(low_use_per_visitor, high_use_per_visitor))

  dplyr::mutate(mid_use = visitors_mid * mid_use_per_visitor,

geom_line(aes(y = observed_use, color = "Observed"))

## - Supply Calculate monthly supply and demand

We compare monthly demand to monthly supply (WBM-modeled runoff, in gallons)
separately for each of the three candidate systems (current Edith intake,
downstream expanded Edith intake, Paradise Valley alluvial GW area). Demand
uses actual metered water use for the historical period, summarized
separately for pre- and post-2019 leak conditions (`monthly_leak_summary`,
above), rather than the per-visitor estimate, since real meter readings
exist for that period. For the future, we use the GAM-based visitation
projection converted to gallons via the use-per-visitor rates
(`monthly_use`, above), averaged by month across the 2035-2064 mid-century
window. Supply is the monthly WBM runoff total for each system, averaged by
month within the matching window, for the historical GCM and for each of
the two focal climate futures (Snowy Wet, Less Snowy Dry).

```{r supply_demand_monthly}

# --- 1. Monthly demand climatology ------------------------------------------

# Historical: real metered use, pre- vs. post-leak, by calendar month
# (from monthly_leak_summary, built above in the investigate_leak chunk).
demand_hist_monthly <- monthly_leak_summary %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    scenario = dplyr::case_when(
      period == "Pre-June 2019 (Baseline)"  ~ "Pre-Leak (Historical)",
      period == "Post-June 2019 (Post-Leak)" ~ "Post-Leak (Historical)"),
    month = m_num,
    demand_gal_mid  = avg_use,
    demand_gal_low  = min_use,
    demand_gal_high = max_use)

# Future: GAM-projected visitation x use-per-visitor rates (mid/low/high),
# averaged by calendar month across the 2035-2064 mid-century window.
demand_fut_monthly <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym), month = month(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year >= fut_yrs[1], year <= fut_yrs[2]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    demand_gal_mid  = mean(mid_use,  na.rm = TRUE),
    demand_gal_low  = mean(low_use,  na.rm = TRUE),
    demand_gal_high = mean(high_use, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Projected (2035-2064)")

demand_monthly <- dplyr::bind_rows(demand_hist_monthly, demand_fut_monthly)

# --- 2. Monthly supply climatology, per system ------------------------------

# WBM monthly runoff totals (gal), averaged by calendar month within the
# matching window for each CF -- Historical uses hist_yrs, the two future
# CFs use fut_yrs (same windows used throughout the rest of the report).
supply_monthly <- wbm_monthly %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym), month = month(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & year >= fut_yrs[1]  & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    `Edith Current`    = mean(runoff_gal_edith_wbm,      na.rm = TRUE),
    `Edith Downstream` = mean(runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Paradise GW`      = mean(runoff_gal_paradise_wbm,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(CF, month), names_to = "system", values_to = "supply_gal")

# --- 3. Pair each demand scenario with its matching supply CF(s) -----------

# Historical demand (either leak period) compares against Historical supply;
# the future projected demand compares against BOTH focal climate futures.
scenario_cf_lookup <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                 ~CF,
  "Pre-Leak (Historical)",   "Historical",
  "Post-Leak (Historical)",  "Historical",
  "Projected (2035-2064)",   "Snowy Wet",
  "Projected (2035-2064)",   "Less Snowy Dry"
)

# --- 4. Monthly D:S / S:D, per system, per scenario -------------------------

ds_monthly <- demand_monthly %>%
  dplyr::left_join(scenario_cf_lookup, by = "scenario", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(supply_monthly, by = c("CF", "month"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    DS          = demand_gal_mid  / supply_gal,
    DS_stress   = demand_gal_high / supply_gal,
    SD          = supply_gal / demand_gal_mid,
    DS_over_pt2 = DS >= 0.2,
    DS_over_1   = DS >= 1
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(system, scenario, month)

print(ds_monthly)

# --- 5. Annual version (same demand/supply totals, summed across the year) -

ds_annual <- ds_monthly %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, scenario, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    demand_gal_mid_annual = sum(demand_gal_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
    supply_gal_annual     = sum(supply_gal,     na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    DS_annual = demand_gal_mid_annual / supply_gal_annual,
    SD_annual = supply_gal_annual / demand_gal_mid_annual
  )

print(ds_annual)

# --- 6. Demand vs. routed streamflow ----------------------------------------

# The runoff-based supply above is the water generated within each month,
# which understates late-summer supply: much of that month's streamflow is
# earlier runoff draining through the routing stores. Here supply is routed
# streamflow from the 1,000-member routing ensemble (daily min/mean/max, in
# gal/day), summed to monthly volumes for each year. Two sources of spread
# are kept separate:
#   - routing parameter uncertainty: ensemble mean vs. ensemble minimum
#   - year-to-year variability: median year vs. a dry year (10th percentile
#     of the years in the window, by calendar month)
flow_monthly <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), month = month(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & year >= fut_yrs[1]  & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, year, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(`Edith Current_mean`    = sum(mean_edith_discharge),
                   `Edith Current_min`     = sum(min_edith_discharge),
                   `Edith Downstream_mean` = sum(mean_down_edith_discharge),
                   `Edith Downstream_min`  = sum(min_down_edith_discharge),
                   `Paradise GW_mean`      = sum(mean_paradise_discharge),
                   `Paradise GW_min`       = sum(min_paradise_discharge),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(CF, year, month), names_to = c("system", "ensemble"),
                      names_sep = "_", values_to = "flow_gal")

flow_month_stats <- flow_monthly %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, system, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(flow_median_year_gal = median(flow_gal[ensemble == "mean"]),
                   flow_dry_year_gal = quantile(flow_gal[ensemble == "mean"], 0.1),
                   flow_dry_year_min_gal = quantile(flow_gal[ensemble == "min"], 0.1),
                   .groups = "drop")

ds_streamflow_monthly <- demand_monthly %>%
  dplyr::left_join(scenario_cf_lookup, by = "scenario", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(flow_month_stats, by = c("CF", "month"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DS_typical = demand_gal_mid / flow_median_year_gal,
                DS_dry_year = demand_gal_mid / flow_dry_year_gal,
                DS_stress_test = demand_gal_high / flow_dry_year_min_gal) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(system, scenario, CF, month)

readr::write_csv(ds_streamflow_monthly, "data/park/MORA/Tables/ds_streamflow_monthly.csv")

# Highest monthly D:S for each case, by system and scenario
ds_streamflow_peak <- ds_streamflow_monthly %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, scenario, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(typical_max_DS = max(DS_typical),
                   typical_month = month.abb[month[which.max(DS_typical)]],
                   dry_year_max_DS = max(DS_dry_year),
                   dry_year_month = month.abb[month[which.max(DS_dry_year)]],
                   stress_test_max_DS = max(DS_stress_test),
                   stress_test_month = month.abb[month[which.max(DS_stress_test)]],
                   .groups = "drop")

print(ds_streamflow_peak, width = Inf)
readr::write_csv(ds_streamflow_peak, "data/park/MORA/Tables/ds_streamflow_peak.csv")

# Figure (Appendix A7): monthly demand vs. routed streamflow cases, by system,
# for the historical post-leak scenario and the projected scenario under each
# climate future
ds_flow_plot_dat <- ds_streamflow_monthly %>%
  dplyr::filter(scenario != "Pre-Leak (Historical)") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(panel = ifelse(CF == "Historical", "Historical (post-leak demand)",
                               paste0("Projected, ", CF)),
                panel = factor(panel, levels = c("Historical (post-leak demand)",
                                                 "Projected, Less Snowy Dry", "Projected, Snowy Wet")),
                month_date = as.Date(paste0("2021-", month, "-01")))

ds_flow_fig <- ggplot(ds_flow_plot_dat, aes(x = month_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = flow_dry_year_min_gal / 1e6, ymax = flow_median_year_gal / 1e6),
              fill = "#1b6ca8", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(aes(y = flow_median_year_gal / 1e6, linetype = "Streamflow, typical year"), color = "#1b6ca8") +
  geom_line(aes(y = flow_dry_year_gal / 1e6, linetype = "Streamflow, dry year"), color = "#1b6ca8") +
  geom_line(aes(y = flow_dry_year_min_gal / 1e6, linetype = "Streamflow, stress test"), color = "#1b6ca8") +
  geom_line(aes(y = demand_gal_mid / 1e6, color = "Demand, mid"), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(aes(y = demand_gal_high / 1e6, color = "Demand, high"), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Demand, mid" = "black", "Demand, high" = "#b02a24")) +
  scale_linetype_manual("", values = c("Streamflow, typical year" = "solid",
                                       "Streamflow, dry year" = "dashed",
                                       "Streamflow, stress test" = "dotted")) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "2 months") +
  facet_grid(system ~ panel) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Monthly volume (Mgal, log scale)") +
  theme_wsva() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")

ds_flow_fig

ggsave(ds_flow_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/ds_streamflow_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 9, height = 8)

rm(ds_flow_plot_dat)

rm(flow_monthly)

```

## - Tank storage

A single physical tank (250,000 gal, from the water supply database,
extracted above as `tank_cap_gal`) serves the Paradise system. We simulate
monthly tank level as a running mass balance for the existing Edith Current
system - storage can't exceed capacity (excess is not diverted) or drop
below zero (unmet demand is tracked as a deficit instead).

An earlier version of this simulation used the NPS WBM's modeled runoff as
tank inflow, but WBM runoff is a land-surface-model quantity (water
generated at a given grid cell that day), not routed channel discharge; it
can legitimately compute to zero on individual days even though Edith
Creek itself has never gone dry, which produced large artificial deficits
unrelated to any real supply shortfall. The real constraint on tank inflow
is not creek flow at all: only a small fraction of Edith Creek's discharge
is ever captured by the intake (see Edith Creek Discharge, above), and the
diversion/treatment train is the binding limit on how quickly water can
reach the tank. We therefore model monthly inflow as the treatment
system's actual operating capacity - 80 gallons per minute (gpm) in summer
(May-September; typically run 12 hours/day, up to 15 hours/day at peak
demand) and 50-60 gpm in winter (October-April; 12 hours/day) - rather
than as modeled creek flow. [FLAG FOR KRISTEN: confirm May-Sept/Oct-Apr is
the right summer/winter operating boundary for the treatment schedule - I
don't have a documented cutoff for this and used the visitor season as a
placeholder.]

Because this simulation now depends only on the treatment system's fixed
operating schedule and each demand scenario, not on climate-driven creek
flow, it applies to Edith Current only, the only candidate system with a
known, built treatment capacity; Edith Downstream and Paradise GW would
each need their own capacity specification once their infrastructure is
designed, and are not included here. For the same reason, results no
longer vary by climate future, and the simulation is shown as a single
repeating annual cycle rather than the multi-year sequence used in the D:S
analysis above, since neither the treatment schedule nor the demand
climatology varies from year to year; the multi-year drought-persistence
risk that motivated the original design instead lives in the D:S and
Edith Creek discharge results above, which use the actual multi-year WBM
sequence.

```{r tank_storage}

tank_cap_gal <- 250000

# --- 1. Edith Current diversion/treatment capacity, by calendar month -------
# Tank inflow is limited by how fast the existing treatment train can divert
# and process water, not by Edith Creek discharge itself (see prose above):
# only a small fraction of creek flow is ever captured, and the creek has
# never run dry. Summer (May-Sep): 80 gpm, run 12 hr/day typically, up to 15
# hr/day at peak demand. Winter (Oct-Apr): 50-60 gpm, run 12 hr/day.
treatment_capacity_monthly <- tibble::tibble(month = 1:12) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    season        = ifelse(month %in% 5:9, "Summer", "Winter"),
    gpm_typical   = ifelse(season == "Summer", 80, 50),
    gpm_max       = ifelse(season == "Summer", 80, 60),
    hours_typical = 12,
    hours_max     = ifelse(season == "Summer", 15, 12),
    days_in_month = lubridate::days_in_month(as.Date(paste0("2001-", month, "-01"))),
    # Typical monthly capacity = what the plant runs under normal operation;
    # max monthly capacity = the physical ceiling if run at the higher rate
    # (winter) or the longer hours (summer) every day that month.
    capacity_gal_typical = gpm_typical * 60 * hours_typical * days_in_month,
    capacity_gal_max     = gpm_max     * 60 * hours_max     * days_in_month
  )

# --- 2. Demand, Edith Current's three scenarios only -------------------------
# Climate future no longer matters here (tank inflow no longer depends on
# WBM supply), so "Projected" no longer needs pairing with a CF via
# scenario_cf_lookup; join demand directly to the capacity schedule by month.
tank_demand_monthly <- demand_monthly %>%
  dplyr::left_join(treatment_capacity_monthly, by = "month")

# --- 3. Storage simulation with deficit tracking -----------------------------
# Each month, the plant diverts enough to cover demand and refill the tank
# toward capacity, capped at what it can physically process that month
# (capacity_gal_max, i.e. running the higher rate / longer hours if needed).
calc_storage_details <- function(dem_vec, cap_max_vec, capacity) {
  res <- purrr::accumulate2(dem_vec, cap_max_vec, function(prev, dem, cap_max) {
    target_inflow <- dem + (capacity - prev$level)
    actual_inflow <- max(0, min(target_inflow, cap_max))
    potential_water <- prev$level + actual_inflow - dem
    actual_level <- max(0, min(capacity, potential_water))
    shortfall <- ifelse(potential_water < 0, abs(potential_water), 0)
    list(level = actual_level, deficit = shortfall, inflow = actual_inflow)
  }, .init = list(level = capacity, deficit = 0, inflow = 0))[-1]
  purrr::map_df(res, ~.)
}

tank_storage <- tank_demand_monthly %>%
  dplyr::arrange(scenario, month) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {
    avg_res  <- calc_storage_details(.x$demand_gal_mid,  .x$capacity_gal_max, tank_cap_gal)
    # "low"/"high" name the resulting tank trajectory, not the demand input -
    # higher demand draws the tank down further (the stressed/low run).
    low_res  <- calc_storage_details(.x$demand_gal_high, .x$capacity_gal_max, tank_cap_gal)
    high_res <- calc_storage_details(.x$demand_gal_low,  .x$capacity_gal_max, tank_cap_gal)
    .x %>% dplyr::mutate(
      tank_level_gal      = avg_res$level,
      deficit_gal         = avg_res$deficit,
      tank_level_gal_low  = low_res$level,
      deficit_gal_low     = low_res$deficit,
      tank_level_gal_high = high_res$level,
      deficit_gal_high    = high_res$deficit
    )
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month_label = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb))

# --- 4. Plot: tank level through a representative annual cycle --------------
# A single repeating 12-month cycle, not a multi-year sequence: neither the
# treatment schedule nor the demand climatology varies year to year, so
# there is no multi-year drought-persistence signal left to show here (that
# risk now lives in the D:S / Edith Creek discharge sections above, which
# use actual multi-year WBM sequences).
# Pre-Leak was originally gray50, but geom_ribbon's alpha = 0.2 flattens both
# black and gray50 to similar washed-out grays, making the two historical
# scenarios' ribbons visually indistinguishable (or easy to misread as
# swapped). Use a hue already in the report's palette instead of another
# gray so all three scenarios stay distinguishable at low alpha.
tank_colors <- c(
  "Pre-Leak (Historical)"   = unname(plot_colors["Snowy Wet"]),
  "Post-Leak (Historical)"  = "black",
  "Projected (2035-2064)"   = unname(plot_colors["Less Snowy Dry"])
)

tank_storage_fig <- ggplot(tank_storage, aes(x = month_label, group = scenario, color = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = tank_level_gal_low, ymax = tank_level_gal_high), alpha = 0.2, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tank_level_gal), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = -deficit_gal), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tank_cap_gal, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Tank Level (gal)",
       title = "Edith Current: simulated tank storage, treatment-capacity-limited",
       subtitle = paste0("Dotted line = tank capacity (", scales::comma(tank_cap_gal),
                         " gal); dashed line = monthly deficit below zero; single repeating annual cycle")) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = tank_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = tank_colors) +
  # Show legend swatches at full opacity so they reliably identify each
  # scenario's true color, independent of the ribbons' alpha = 0.2.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -10, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

tank_storage_fig

ggsave(tank_storage_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/tank_storage.jpg",
      dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 5)

# --- 5. Storage-to-Demand (S:D) summary table --------------------------------
# Same peak-demand framing used in other finished park WSVA reports: monthly
# peak demand (mean/high) and the implied daily peak (2x the monthly peak /
# days in that month, to account for non-uniform daily use within the
# month), against the single tank capacity, reported as an S:D ratio and
# days of buffer supply.
sd_table <- demand_monthly %>%
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(demand_gal_mid, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    days_in_peak_month = lubridate::days_in_month(as.Date(paste0("2001-", month, "-01"))),
    `Monthly (mean)`    = demand_gal_mid,
    `Monthly (high)`    = demand_gal_high,
    `Daily (mean)`      = 2 * demand_gal_mid  / days_in_peak_month,
    `Daily (high)`      = 2 * demand_gal_high / days_in_peak_month
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Monthly (mean)`, `Monthly (high)`, `Daily (mean)`, `Daily (high)`),
    names_to = "use_period", values_to = "demand_gal"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tank_capacity_gal = tank_cap_gal,
    SD             = tank_capacity_gal / demand_gal,
    days_of_supply = ifelse(grepl("Daily", use_period), SD, SD * days_in_peak_month)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(scenario, use_period, demand_gal, tank_capacity_gal, SD, days_of_supply) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(.x, 3)))

kable(sd_table,
     caption = "Storage-to-demand (S:D) ratio and days of buffer supply, by scenario and peak use period.")

readr::write_csv(sd_table, "data/park/MORA/Tables/sd_table.csv")

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(tank_demand_monthly, treatment_capacity_monthly)
gc()

```
