```{r fire_by_system}

# Per-system burned fraction (historical fire perimeters) and forested
# fraction (NLCD), each computed within that system's own AOI -- the
# three-watershed comparison, in place of the single park-wide numbers
# above.
fire_context_by_system <- purrr::imap_dfr(fire_aois, function(sys_aoi, sys_name) {

  sys_fires <- new_geomac %>%
    sf::st_filter(sf::st_transform(sys_aoi, crs = sf::st_crs(new_geomac)))

  burned_fraction <- if (nrow(sys_fires) == 0) {
    0
  } else {
    sys_fires %>%
      dplyr::summarize() %>%
      sf::st_transform(crs = sf::st_crs(sys_aoi)) %>%
      sf::st_intersection(sys_aoi) %>%
      sf::st_area() %>%
      `/`(sf::st_area(sys_aoi)) %>%
      as.numeric() %>%
      sum()
  }

  nlcd_sys <- terra::rast("data/all/nlcd_2021_land_cover_l48_20230630/nlcd_2021_land_cover_l48_20230630.img") %>%
    terra::crop(sf::st_transform(sys_aoi, crs = terra::crs(.)), mask = TRUE) %>%
    droplevels()

  forest_mask_sys <- nlcd_sys %in% c(41, 42, 43)

  forested_fraction <- terra::zonal(
    forest_mask_sys,
    terra::vect(sf::st_transform(sys_aoi, crs = terra::crs(nlcd_sys))),
    fun = "mean", weights = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE
  )[[1]]

  tibble::tibble(
    system = sys_name,
    n_historical_fires = nrow(sys_fires),
    burned_fraction = burned_fraction,
    forested_fraction = forested_fraction
  )
})

print(fire_context_by_system)

```

Fire exposure:

Gao, P., Terando, A. J., Kupfer, J. A., Varner, J. M., Stambaugh, M. C., Lei, T. L., & Hiers, J. K. (2021). Robust projections of future fire probability for the conterminous United States. *Science of The Total Environment, 789*, 147872. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2021.147872>

Fire probability is calculated using a model referred to as PC2FM, which estimates the mean yearly fire interval (MFI). Fire probability is the inverse of MFI (i.e., FP = 1 / MFI). MFI is computed using annual average temperature and precipitation as its primary inputs, as well as factors like molecular collision frequency and activation energy (which influence combustion processes). It is then calibrated using historical fire scar records. Then, future fire probabilities are projected using climate data from the MACAv2 dataset.

```{r exposure}

water_supply_pyromes <- st_read("data/all/usfs_fire/Pyromes-RDS-2020-0020/Data/Pyromes_CONUS_20200206.shp") %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%

# GRAB THE GAO 2021 FIRE PROBABILITY FOR THE APPRORIATE PYROMES AND CLIMATE FUTURES:
crosswalk <- read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021/gcm_crosswalk.csv")

# Back-casted GCMs, compared against GridMet. Really just need GridMet.
fireprob_historic <- read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021/tables3-fireprob-hist.csv") %>%
  dplyr::select(PYROME, GridMet)

# Midcentury is defined as the avg. across 2040-2070:
all_delta_fireprob <- read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021//tables12-45-midcentury.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(-PYROME, names_to = "gao") %>%
  left_join(crosswalk, by = "gao") %>%
  mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM, ".rcp45")) %>%
  # do same thing on the 85 CFs, then bind together:
  bind_rows(
    read_csv("data/all/usfs_fire/fire_projections_gao_2021//tables6-85-midcentury.csv") %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-PYROME, names_to = "gao", values_to = "value") %>%
      left_join(crosswalk, by = "gao") %>%
      mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM, ".rcp85"))
  ) %>%
  # join historic data by pyrome:
  left_join(fireprob_historic, by = "PYROME") %>%
  # Description: "The probability of a fire increases/decreases by `delta_fp` percent." 
  mutate(delta_fp = 100 * ((value - GridMet)/GridMet)) %>%
  left_join(future_differentials, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::filter(PYROME %in% water_supply_pyromes$PYROME)

delta_fireprob <- all_delta_fireprob %>%
  filter(GCM %in% selected_gcms[[1]]$GCM) %>%

# across GCMs (the line in the figure), reported in Appendix A
fire_runoff_lm <- lm(delta_fp ~ mean_runoff_in, data = all_delta_fireprob)
fire_runoff_fit <- tibble::tibble(
  n_projections = nrow(stats::na.omit(all_delta_fireprob[, c("delta_fp", "mean_runoff_in")])),
  slope_pct_per_in = coef(fire_runoff_lm)[["mean_runoff_in"]],
  r2 = summary(fire_runoff_lm)$r.squared,
  p_value = summary(fire_runoff_lm)$coefficients["mean_runoff_in", "Pr(>|t|)"],
  spearman_rho = stats::cor(all_delta_fireprob$delta_fp, all_delta_fireprob$mean_runoff_in,

  delta_fp_min = min(all_delta_fireprob$delta_fp, na.rm = TRUE),
  delta_fp_max = max(all_delta_fireprob$delta_fp, na.rm = TRUE))

Fire sensitivity:

Dillon, Gregory K. 2023. Wildfire Hazard Potential for the United States (270-m), version 2023. 4th Edition. Updated 17 July 2024. Fort Collins, CO: Forest Service Research Data Archive. <https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2015-0047-4>

The wildfire hazard potential (WHP) map is a raster geospatial product produced by the USDA Forest Service, Fire Modeling Institute that can help to inform evaluations of wildfire hazard or prioritization of fuels management needs across very large landscapes. Our specific objective with the WHP map is to depict the relative potential for high-intensity wildfire that may be difficult to manage. To create the 2023 version, we built upon spatial datasets of wildfire likelihood and intensity generated with the Large Fire Simulator (FSim), as well as spatial fuels and vegetation data from LANDFIRE 2020 and point locations of past fire occurrence (ca. 1992 - 2020). With these datasets as inputs, we produced an index of WHP for the United States at a 270-meter resolution. We present the WHP map in two forms: 1) continuous integer values, and 2) five WHP classes of very low, low, moderate, high, and very high. Areas mapped with higher WHP values represent fuels with a higher probability of experiencing torching, crowning, and other forms of extreme fire behavior under conducive weather conditions, based primarily on landscape conditions at the end of 2020.

This 2023 version of WHP was created from updated national wildfire hazard datasets of annual burn probability and fire intensity generated by the USDA Forest Service, Rocky Mountain Research Station with the large fire simulation system (FSim). Vegetation and wildland fuels data from LANDFIRE 2020 (version 2.2.0) were the primary inputs to the updated FSim modeling work and therefore form the foundation for this version of the WHP. As such, the data presented here reflect landscape conditions as of the end of 2020. LANDFIRE 2020 vegetation and fuels data were also used directly in the WHP mapping process, along with updated point locations of fire occurrence ca. 1992-2020. With these datasets as inputs, we produced an index of WHP for all of the conterminous United States at 270-meter resolution. We present the final WHP map in two forms: 1) continuous integer values, and 2) five WHP classes of very low, low, moderate, high, and very high. On its own, WHP is not an explicit map of wildfire threat or risk, but when paired with spatial data depicting highly valued resources and assets such as structures or powerlines, it can approximate relative wildfire risk to those specific resources and assets. WHP is also not a forecast or wildfire outlook for any particular season, as it does not include any information on current or forecasted weather or fuel moisture conditions. It is instead intended for long-term strategic fuels management.

GRAB MEAN WATER SUPPLY RANKING OF CONTINUOUS WHP IN THE WATER SUPPLY PYROME:

```{r WHP}

# continuous fire hazard potential, cropped to water supply pyrome:
whp_cnt <- terra::rast("data/all/usfs_fire/whp2023_GeoTIF/whp2023_cnt_conus.tif") %>%
  terra::crop(., sf::st_transform(water_supply_pyromes, 5070), 
              mask = TRUE, touches = TRUE) %>%
  na.omit()

# transform the ranked values into percentiles (at 1 percent intervals):
values <- terra::values(whp_cnt, na.rm = TRUE)

quantiles <- quantile(values, probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.01)) %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(to = c(lead(value, 1))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(to = ifelse(is.na(to), max(values) + 1, to)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(from = value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(becomes = seq(0, 1, by = 0.01))

# Return the percentiles based on 1% threshold defined above
whp_quantiled <- terra::classify(whp_cnt, rcl = quantiles, right = TRUE)

# plot(whp_quantiled)

# grab percentiles within the water supply watershed:
water_supply_fire_potential <- whp_quantiled %>%
  crop(sf::st_transform(fire_aoi, 5070), mask = TRUE) 

# calculate area-weightem mean of the water supply watershed:
mean_fire_potential <- terra::zonal(water_supply_fire_potential, 
                                    terra::vect(sf::st_transform(fire_aoi, 5070)), fun = "mean", weights = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

mapview(raster::raster(water_supply_fire_potential)) + 
  mapview(fire_aoi, alpha.regions = 0)

# # see the distribution of grid cells:
# ggplot(as.data.table(water_supply_fire_potential)) +
#   geom_histogram(aes(Band_1, fill = Band_1)) +
#   theme_wsva()

# --- Per-system: crop the (pyrome-wide) percentile raster to each
# system's own AOI and take its area-weighted mean -- the three-watershed
# WHP comparison, on the same percentile scale as mean_fire_potential
# above. ---------------------------------------------------------------
whp_by_system <- purrr::imap_dfr(fire_aois, function(sys_aoi, sys_name) {

  sys_whp <- whp_quantiled %>%
    terra::crop(sf::st_transform(sys_aoi, 5070), mask = TRUE)

  mean_whp_percentile <- terra::zonal(
    sys_whp, terra::vect(sf::st_transform(sys_aoi, 5070)),
    fun = "mean", weights = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE
  )[[1]]

  tibble::tibble(system = sys_name, mean_whp_percentile = mean_whp_percentile)
})

print(whp_by_system)

# 7. Drought (SPEI)

```{r spei}

# Calculate SPEI using the {spei} package

# 1. Configuration --------------------------------------------------------
# FIX (per {SPEI} package docs, spei()): the package is built for MONTHLY
# input - it splits the series into 12 calendar-month sub-series and fits
# each month's distribution separately, and `scale` tells it how many
# months to roll up ITSELF before standardizing (a `scale = 6` on monthly
# data gives the standard "SPEI-6": one value per month, each reflecting
# that month + the preceding 5). The previous version pre-aggregated the
# water balance into 6-month blocks (agg_label = "6 months", ts frequency
# = freq = 2) and then ALSO passed scale = freq (2) to spei() - on a
# frequency-2 series that asks spei() to roll up another 2 periods (i.e.
# another 12 months) on top of the already-6-month blocks, roughly
# double-aggregating, and it breaks the calendar-month fitting the package
# is designed around (a frequency-2 series only has 2 "months" to cycle
# through, not 12). Fixed below: aggregate to MONTHLY (not 6-month)
# resolution, keep the series at frequency = 12, and pass scale = ag_n (6)
# so spei() does the 6-month rolling itself - a standard, continuous
# monthly SPEI-6, one value per month, matching how spei() is used in its
# own documentation examples (e.g. spei(monthly_series, 6)).
ag_n <- 6 # SPEI time scale in months (the `scale` argument below) - NOT
          # the resolution agg_wbm/spei_results are aggregated to, which
          # is always monthly regardless of ag_n (see above).
freq <- 12 # periods (months) per year in agg_wbm/spei_results - used
           # below and in the event/persistence metrics to convert a
           # duration or run-length in months back to years.

# 2. Aggregate WBM Data (monthly) -----------------------------------------
agg_wbm <- wbm %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(time_ag = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(CF, time_ag) %>%
  summarize(
    across(c(precip_in_wbm, pet_in_wbm, runoff_in_wbm,
             runoff_gal_edith_wbm, runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm, runoff_gal_paradise_wbm),
           sum, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(c(tmean_C), mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(CF, time_ag) %>%
  mutate(
    balance = precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm,
    year = year(time_ag),
    month = month(time_ag)
  )

# Get timing for TS objects
end_yr <- max(agg_wbm$year)
end_mo <- agg_wbm$month[which.max(agg_wbm$time_ag)]

# 3. Calculate SPEI by Climate Future -------------------------------------
# BUG FIX (series construction): the historical GridMET download runs
# through 2026-09-20, but the future (MACA) download starts 2026-01-01, so
# Jan-Sep 2026 exists in BOTH. The old code stacked Historical + future rows
# for each CF and passed them to ts(..., end = c(end_yr, end_mo)). ts() just
# lays values out consecutively backward from `end`, so those 9 duplicated
# months made the series 9 values longer than its calendar span and slid
# EVERY earlier (historical) value 9 calendar months out of place. spei()
# fits a separate distribution for each calendar month, so the historical
# data was standardized against mis-assigned months (self-consistent, which
# is why historical SPEI looked normal, sd ~ 1), while the correctly labeled
# future months were then scored against those wrong-season distributions.
# The 3b diagnostics below showed the symptom: sd of the monthly water
# balance barely changed across the old 2025 split (9.6 vs 9.8 / 11.7) while sd of SPEI
# jumped from ~1 to ~2.7-2.9.
#
# Fix: one row per month, Historical wins wherever it has a COMPLETE month
# (September 2026 is only a partial month in the GridMET record, so the
# future run supplies it), the future CF supplies everything after, and a
# guard stops the script if the series is ever not consecutive months again.
hist_last_complete_month <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(time_ag = lubridate::floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  dplyr::count(time_ag, name = "n_days") %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_days == lubridate::days_in_month(time_ag)) %>%
  dplyr::pull(time_ag) %>%
  max() %>%
  as.Date()

calc_spei_cf <- function(cf_name, scale = ag_n) {
  dat <- agg_wbm %>%
    dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & as.Date(time_ag) <= hist_last_complete_month) |
                  (CF == cf_name & as.Date(time_ag) > hist_last_complete_month)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(time_ag)

  # Guard: spei() needs exactly one row per consecutive month.
  all_months <- seq(as.Date(min(dat$time_ag)), as.Date(max(dat$time_ag)), by = "month")
  stopifnot(length(all_months) == nrow(dat),
            all(as.Date(dat$time_ag) == all_months))

  # Calculate SPEI-`scale` on the monthly series, anchored by its START date
  s_obj <- spei(ts(dat$balance,
                   start = c(lubridate::year(min(dat$time_ag)),
                             lubridate::month(min(dat$time_ag))),
                   frequency = freq),
                scale = scale,
                # Reference (fitting) period = the project's historical period
                # (hist_yrs = 1980-2012), same baseline the other analyses use,
                # so SPEI = 0 means "typical of 1980-2012" and every later year
                # (2013-2026 observed + projected) is scored against it.
                ref.start = c(hist_yrs[1], 1),
                ref.end = c(hist_yrs[2], 12))

  dat %>% mutate(spei = as.numeric(s_obj$fitted), ym = as.Date(time_ag))
}

spei_results <- c("Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet") %>%
  set_names() %>%
  map_dfr(~ calc_spei_cf(.x, ag_n), .id = "Future_Group") %>%
  distinct(CF, ym, .keep_all = TRUE) # Remove duplicate Historical rows

# 3b. DIAGNOSTIC: why does SPEI magnitude jump so much from historical to
# projected (see drought plot below)? Three candidate explanations, checked
# in order. This block is read-only (print() only) and does not change
# spei_results or anything downstream.
#
# (a) `wbm` may still carry more than one row per (CF, date) if the two
#     retained climate grid cells were not fully collapsed to a single
#     spatially-averaged series upstream (see the "wbm_all is still
#     per-pixel at this point" note in the Hock calibration chunk above).
#     agg_wbm sums daily values to monthly within group_by(CF, time_ag),
#     so if >1 row/date slips through here, that sum silently also sums
#     across grid cells, not just across days.
wbm %>%
  dplyr::count(CF, date, name = "n_rows") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(max_rows_per_date = max(n_rows),
                    pct_dates_with_gt1_row = 100 * mean(n_rows > 1),
                    .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()

# (b) Compare the monthly water balance (precip - PET) itself, split at
#     the historical/future splice, by CF. If sd_balance jumps sharply at
#     the same point the SPEI swings widen, the balance input itself (not
#     the SPEI standardization) is the source.
agg_wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(period = dplyr::if_else(time_ag <= as.Date(paste0(hist_yrs[2], "-12-01")), "Reference (<= 2012)", "After reference")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, period) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_balance = mean(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
                    sd_balance = sd(balance, na.rm = TRUE),
                    n = dplyr::n(),
                    .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()

# (c) Compare SPEI itself, split the same way, by climate future. `ref.end
#     = c(hist_yrs[2], 12)` above fixes the distribution spei() standardizes
#     against to the 1980-2012 historical period only -- so even a modest increase
#     in month-to-month variability in the single-GCM-driven future
#     balance (vs. the smoothed historical GridMET record) will show up as
#     mechanically more extreme SPEI, independent of any true change in
#     long-run drought risk. This check shows whether that is in fact what
#     is happening here.
spei_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(period = dplyr::if_else(ym <= as.Date(paste0(hist_yrs[2], "-12-01")), "Reference (<= 2012)", "After reference")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Future_Group, period) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
                    sd_spei = sd(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
                    n = dplyr::n(),
                    .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()

# 4. Define and Identify Drought Events ------------------------------------
thresholds <- c(moderate = -1, severe = -1.5, extreme = -2)

# Analysis windows match the other analyses (e.g. the snowmelt figures):
# Historical = hist_yrs (1980-2012), projected = fut_yrs (2035-2064). SPEI itself
# is computed on the continuous monthly series above; only the summary
# statistics below are restricted to these windows.
spei_events <- spei_results %>%
  filter((year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) | (year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  drop_na(spei) %>%
  # Pivot thresholds to calculate all categories at once
  crossing(threshold_name = names(thresholds)) %>%
  mutate(threshold_val = thresholds[threshold_name],
         is_drought = spei <= threshold_val) %>%
  group_by(CF, threshold_name) %>%
  mutate(event_id = cumsum(is_drought & !lag(is_drought, default = FALSE))) %>%
  ungroup()

# 5. Summarize Metrics ----------------------------------------------------
# Event-based metrics (Duration/Intensity)
event_metrics <- spei_events %>%
  filter(is_drought) %>%
  group_by(CF, threshold_name, event_id) %>%
  summarize(duration = n(), 
            mean_spei = mean(spei), 
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(CF, threshold_name) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_duration = (mean(duration) / freq),
    max_duration  = (max(duration) / freq),
    median_duration = (median(duration) / freq),
    mean_spei_val = mean(mean_spei),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(CF, threshold_name), names_to = "stat", values_to = "value") %>%
  unite("Metric", threshold_name, stat)

# Overall Severity Stats
severity_metrics <- spei_results %>%
  filter((year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) | (year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  group_by(CF) %>%
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_spei = median(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_spei = sd(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Percents
    mod_percent = 100 * sum(spei <= -1, na.rm = TRUE) / n,
    sev_percent = 100 * sum(spei <= -1.5, na.rm = TRUE) / n,
    ext_percent = 100 * sum(spei <= -2, na.rm = TRUE) / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-CF, names_to = "Metric", values_to = "value")

# Final Join and Transpose
spei_metrics <- bind_rows(event_metrics, severity_metrics) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = CF, values_from = value) %>%
  arrange(Metric)

# 6. Drought probability framing ------------------------------------------
# Reframe the moderate/severe/extreme shares above (percent of periods in
# each category) as an annual drought probability: the fraction of years,
# within each climate future, that contain at least one period at or
# beyond each severity threshold. This is more directly decision-relevant
# than "X% of periods" -- e.g. "in a given year under Snowy Wet, there is
# a Y% chance of at least one severe-drought period."
n_years_by_cf <- spei_results %>%
  filter((year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) | (year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  distinct(CF, year) %>%
  count(CF, name = "n_years")

drought_probability_annual <- spei_events %>%
  filter(is_drought) %>%
  distinct(CF, threshold_name, year) %>%
  count(CF, threshold_name, name = "n_drought_years") %>%
  # Not every CF x threshold combination will have a drought year -- fill
  # those with 0 rather than dropping the row, so every CF/threshold still
  # gets a defined (0%) probability instead of silently disappearing.
  tidyr::complete(CF, threshold_name = names(thresholds),
                  fill = list(n_drought_years = 0)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(n_years_by_cf, by = "CF") %>%
  mutate(annual_drought_probability = n_drought_years / n_years) %>%
  arrange(threshold_name, CF)

print(drought_probability_annual)

# 7. Drought persistence: Markov-chain state transitions -------------------
# Treat SPEI categories as discrete states and estimate the empirical
# period-to-period (i.e. per agg_n-month step) transition matrix within
# each climate future, then derive persistence (probability of staying in
# a state) and expected run-length from it, and the probability a drought
# has ended within N periods -- what the "Alternative to consider later"
# note above was proposing.
drought_states <- spei_results %>%
  filter((year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) | (year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  drop_na(spei) %>%
  mutate(state = case_when(
    spei <= thresholds["extreme"]  ~ "Extreme",
    spei <= thresholds["severe"]   ~ "Severe",
    spei <= thresholds["moderate"] ~ "Moderate",
    TRUE                            ~ "Non-drought"
  )) %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = c("Non-drought", "Moderate", "Severe", "Extreme"))) %>%
  arrange(CF, ym)

calc_transition_matrix <- function(states) {
  # states: an ordered factor vector -- one CF's chronological state
  # sequence. table() keeps all 4 factor levels even where a transition
  # was never observed (giving a 0 count, not a dropped row), and
  # prop.table(..., margin = 1) row-normalizes to P(to | from).
  from <- states[-length(states)]
  to   <- states[-1]
  prop.table(table(from = from, to = to), margin = 1)
}

transition_matrices <- purrr::map(
  set_names(unique(as.character(drought_states$CF))),
  function(cf) {
    states <- drought_states %>% dplyr::filter(CF == cf) %>% dplyr::arrange(ym) %>% dplyr::pull(state)
    calc_transition_matrix(states)
  }
)

# Persistence probability (the transition matrix diagonal) and expected
# run-length, assuming a geometric holding-time distribution:
# E[run length] = 1 / (1 - P(stay)). A state that was never observed as a
# "from" state in a given CF's record has no data to estimate persistence
# from, and correctly comes back NA/NaN rather than an invented value.
persistence_by_cf <- purrr::imap_dfr(transition_matrices, function(mat, cf_name) {
  tibble::tibble(
    CF = cf_name,
    state = rownames(mat),
    p_persist = as.numeric(diag(mat)),
    expected_run_periods = 1 / (1 - p_persist),
    # FIX: periods here are now always months (agg_wbm/spei_results are
    # monthly resolution regardless of ag_n - see the spei chunk above),
    # so expected_run_periods already IS the expected run length in
    # months; multiplying by ag_n would double count the timescale.
    expected_run_months = expected_run_periods
  )
})

print(persistence_by_cf)

# Probability a drought state has ended within N periods, given it just
# started -- geometric survival function: 1 - P(stay)^N.
persistence_horizons <- persistence_by_cf %>%
  filter(state != "Non-drought") %>%
  tidyr::crossing(n_periods = 1:4) %>%
  mutate(
    # FIX: same as expected_run_months above - a period is now a month.
    n_months = n_periods,
    prob_ended_by = 1 - p_persist ^ n_periods
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(CF, state, n_months, prob_ended_by)

print(persistence_horizons)

# SPEI vs. supply, all three systems, for the same July snapshot used
# before -- fixed from the original discharge_gal_wbm (a column that
# doesn't exist in wbm/agg_wbm) to the three per-system WBM runoff
# columns.
ggplot(
  spei_results %>%
    dplyr::filter(month(ym) == 7) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = c(runoff_gal_edith_wbm, runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm, runoff_gal_paradise_wbm),
      names_to = "system", values_to = "supply_gal"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      system = dplyr::recode(
        system,
        runoff_gal_edith_wbm = "Edith Current",
        runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm = "Edith Downstream",
        runoff_gal_paradise_wbm = "Paradise GW"
      )
    ),
  aes(x = spei, y = supply_gal, color = CF, fill = CF) # Add fill mapping here
) +
  # Transparent shaded ellipses around CF groups
  stat_ellipse(geom = "polygon", alpha = 0.15, level = 0.95, color = NA) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ system, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "SPEI", y = "Mean July Supply (gal)") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) # Match fill colors to plot_colors


```

# 7b. Snow Drought (WBM)

Same Hatchett, Rhoades & McEvoy (2022) snow drought classification used for
the observed Paradise SNOTEL record above (`## -- Snow drought`), now applied
to the WBM's daily output so historical and both climate futures can be
compared directly. A methods note: `snowpack_in_wbm` - not `snow_in_wbm` - is
used as the SWE-equivalent state variable here. `snowpack_in_wbm` is the
standing snowpack depth the Hock Calibration section above already validates
against observed SNOTEL SWE (and is aggregated with `max()` elsewhere in this
document, consistent with a state variable), while `snow_in_wbm` is the daily
snowfall flux (aggregated with `sum()` elsewhere, analogous to `rain_in_wbm`)
and isn't the right variable for a percentile-based snowpack classification.
Flag if that's not what was intended and we can switch the column used below.

Cumulative water-year-to-date precipitation (the other input the
classification needs) is calculated on the fly from the WBM's daily
`precip_in_wbm`, matching how SNOTEL's already-cumulative `PREC.I` was used
above. As with SPEI above, each future climate scenario is scored against a
climatology built only from the Historical (GridMET) run, so all three
series are directly comparable.

```{r snow_drought_wbm}

# 1. Water-year cumulative precip, per GCM/CF ------------------------------
wbm_snow <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::arrange(date) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(water_year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, CF, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(precip_cum_in = cumsum(precip_in_wbm)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# 2. Classify snow drought, scoring each future CF against the shared
# historical climatology (same CF-pairing pattern used for SPEI above) -----
wbm_snow_drought <- c("Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet") %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(function(cf) {
    dat <- wbm_snow %>% dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Historical", cf))
    dat %>%
      calc_snow_drought_season(
        date_col = "date",
        swe_col = "snowpack_in_wbm",
        precip_col = "precip_cum_in",
        group_col = NULL,
        climatology_filter = dat$CF == "Historical" &
                             lubridate::year(dat$date) >= hist_yrs[1] &
                             lubridate::year(dat$date) <= hist_yrs[2]
      ) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(dat %>% dplyr::distinct(date, CF), by = "date")
  }) %>%
  # Historical rows are identical across both future comparisons (same
  # shared climatology, same data) - keep one copy
  dplyr::distinct(CF, date, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Validated all-pairs (stacked bar - any two categories can end up
# adjacent in a given stack, so treated as simultaneously visible)
drought_colors <- c("No drought" = "#1a7a4c", "Dry" = "#b0431f",
                    "Warm-Dry" = "#8a3a7a", "Warm" = "#1b6ca8")

# 3. Composition by water year, faceted by climate future ------------------
ggplot(wbm_snow_drought %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(drought_type)),
      aes(x = water_year, fill = drought_type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~CF, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = drought_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6)) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "Water Year", y = "Days", fill = "Drought Type",
       title = "WBM Snow Drought Composition by Water Year and Climate Future")

# 4. Overall % of cool-season days by drought type - WBM climate futures
# vs. observed SNOTEL, the direct comparison-with-observations view --------
wbm_drought_pct <- wbm_snow_drought %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(drought_type),
                (CF == "Historical" & lubridate::year(date) >= hist_yrs[1] & lubridate::year(date) <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & lubridate::year(date) >= fut_yrs[1] & lubridate::year(date) <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::count(CF, drought_type) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_days = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::rename(series = CF)

snotel_drought_pct <- snotel_drought %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(drought_type)) %>%
  dplyr::count(drought_type) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_days = 100 * n / sum(n),
               series = "SNOTEL (Observed)")

drought_pct_compare <- dplyr::bind_rows(wbm_drought_pct, snotel_drought_pct) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(series = factor(series,
                               levels = c("SNOTEL (Observed)", "Historical",
                                          "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

ggplot(drought_pct_compare, aes(x = series, y = pct_days, fill = drought_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = drought_colors) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "% of Cool-Season Days", fill = "Drought Type",
       title = "Snow Drought Composition: WBM Climate Futures vs. Observed SNOTEL",
       subtitle = "SNOTEL = single station (Paradise); WBM = AOI grid mean - not on identical time periods, so treat as a composition check rather than an exact match")

kable(drought_pct_compare %>% dplyr::arrange(series, drought_type) %>%
      dplyr::select(series, drought_type, n, pct_days),
     digits = 1,
     caption = "Snow drought composition (% of cool-season days) by series")


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(snotel_drought, wbm_snow, drought_colors, wbm_drought_pct, snotel_drought_pct)
gc()

```

# 7c. Snow persistence from the WBM and SNOTEL

Satellite snow persistence (Hammond et al., 2018) is the fraction of January 1
to July 3 with snow cover. The same quantity is computed here from the WBM's
daily snowpack for the selected grid cells: the fraction of January 1 to July 3
days with any modeled snowpack. This extends the record back to 1980 and into
both climate futures, at the cost of representing the two-cell average rather
than individual catchments (all three candidate systems share it).

The Paradise SNOTEL station gives a third, ground-based estimate: the fraction
of January 1 to July 3 days with measured SWE above zero. Because persistence
sits near 100% at Paradise in most years, the date of snow melt-out (first
snow-free day after the annual SWE peak) is also computed for SNOTEL and the
WBM, since it can register changes in timing that persistence cannot.

```{r wbm_snow_persistence}

wbm_sp_annual <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), doy = yday(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(doy <= 184) %>%                       # Jan 1 - Jul 3
  dplyr::group_by(CF, year) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 180) %>%                # complete seasons only
  dplyr::summarize(wbm_sp = 100 * mean(snowpack_in_wbm > 0), .groups = "drop")

sp_trend_test <- function(d, label) {
  d <- dplyr::arrange(d, year)
  tibble::tibble(period = label, first_year = min(d$year), last_year = max(d$year),
                 n_years = nrow(d), mean_sp = mean(d$wbm_sp),
                 sens_slope_per_yr = as.numeric(trend::sens.slope(d$wbm_sp)$estimates),
                 mk_p_value = trend::mk.test(d$wbm_sp)$p.value)
}

wbm_sp_hist <- dplyr::filter(wbm_sp_annual, CF == "Historical")

wbm_sp_trend <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sp_trend_test(dplyr::filter(wbm_sp_hist, year >= hist_yrs[1], year <= hist_yrs[2]), "Historical baseline"),
  sp_trend_test(dplyr::filter(wbm_sp_hist, year >= 2001), "Satellite overlap (2001 onward)"),
  sp_trend_test(dplyr::filter(wbm_sp_hist, year >= hist_yrs[1]), "Full historical record"))

wbm_sp_change <- wbm_sp_annual %>%
  dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_sp = mean(wbm_sp), min_sp = min(wbm_sp), max_sp = max(wbm_sp), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(change_pct_points = mean_sp - mean_sp[CF == "Historical"])

# Agreement with satellite snow persistence over the overlapping years
# (sp_system_ts, from the sp_trend_by_system chunk)
wbm_sat_sp <- wbm_sp_hist %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(sp_system_ts %>% dplyr::filter(system == "Edith Current") %>%
                      dplyr::select(year, satellite_sp = mean_sp), by = "year")
wbm_sat_cor <- cor(wbm_sat_sp$wbm_sp, wbm_sat_sp$satellite_sp)

print(wbm_sp_trend)
print(wbm_sp_change)
cat("WBM vs satellite snow persistence (Edith Current), r =", round(wbm_sat_cor, 2),
    "over", nrow(wbm_sat_sp), "years\n")

readr::write_csv(dplyr::bind_rows(wbm_sp_trend %>% dplyr::mutate(table = "trend"),
                                  wbm_sp_change %>% dplyr::mutate(table = "change")),
                 "data/park/MORA/Tables/wbm_snow_persistence.csv")

wbm_sp_fig <- ggplot(wbm_sp_annual %>% dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1]),
                     aes(x = year, y = wbm_sp, color = CF)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = sp_system_ts %>% dplyr::filter(system == "Edith Current"),
             aes(x = year, y = mean_sp, color = "Satellite (Edith Current)"), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c(plot_colors, "Satellite (Edith Current)" = "black")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Snow persistence, Jan 1 - Jul 3 (%)") +
  theme_wsva()

wbm_sp_fig

ggsave(wbm_sp_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/wbm_snow_persistence.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 4)

# --- SNOTEL snow persistence and melt-out date ------------------------------
snotel_swe <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  dplyr::filter(name == "Paradise") %>%
  dplyr::select(date, swe_in) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), doy = yday(date))

snotel_sp_annual <- snotel_swe %>%
  dplyr::filter(doy <= 184) %>%                       # Jan 1 - Jul 3
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::filter(sum(!is.na(swe_in)) >= 170) %>%       # nearly complete seasons only
  dplyr::summarize(snotel_sp = 100 * mean(swe_in > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Melt-out: first snow-free day on or after the annual SWE peak (peak taken
# from January-July). NA if the series has gaps around melt-out or never
# reaches zero by September 30.
melt_out_doy <- function(d, swe_col) {
  d <- d %>% dplyr::filter(doy <= 273) %>% dplyr::arrange(date)
  swe <- d[[swe_col]]
  if (sum(!is.na(swe)) < 250) return(NA_real_)
  pk <- which.max(ifelse(d$doy <= 212, swe, NA))
  after <- which(seq_along(swe) >= pk & !is.na(swe) & swe <= 0)
  if (length(after) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  first0 <- after[1]
  if (any(is.na(swe[pk:first0]))) return(NA_real_)
  d$doy[first0]
}

snotel_melt <- snotel_swe %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ tibble::tibble(melt_doy = melt_out_doy(.x, "swe_in"))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

wbm_melt <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), doy = yday(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, year) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ tibble::tibble(melt_doy = melt_out_doy(.x, "snowpack_in_wbm"))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Agreement among the three persistence records over shared years
sp_three <- snotel_sp_annual %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(wbm_sp_annual %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>%
                      dplyr::select(year, wbm_sp), by = "year") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sp_system_ts %>% dplyr::filter(system == "Edith Current") %>%
                     dplyr::select(year, satellite_sp = mean_sp), by = "year")
sp_sat <- tidyr::drop_na(sp_three, satellite_sp)

melt_pair <- snotel_melt %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(wbm_melt %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>%
                      dplyr::select(year, wbm_melt_doy = melt_doy), by = "year") %>%
  tidyr::drop_na()

mk_row <- function(y, x, label, metric) {
  ok <- !is.na(x)
  tibble::tibble(series = label, metric = metric, first_year = min(y[ok]), last_year = max(y[ok]),
                 n_years = sum(ok), mean = mean(x[ok]), min = min(x[ok]), max = max(x[ok]),
                 sens_slope_per_yr = as.numeric(trend::sens.slope(x[ok])$estimates),
                 mk_p_value = trend::mk.test(x[ok])$p.value)
}

snotel_sp_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  mk_row(snotel_sp_annual$year, snotel_sp_annual$snotel_sp, "SNOTEL (Paradise)", "persistence_pct"),
  mk_row(sp_three$year, sp_three$wbm_sp, "WBM, SNOTEL years", "persistence_pct"),
  mk_row(sp_sat$year, sp_sat$snotel_sp, "SNOTEL, satellite years", "persistence_pct"),
  mk_row(sp_sat$year, sp_sat$satellite_sp, "Satellite (Edith Current), SNOTEL years", "persistence_pct"),
  mk_row(snotel_melt$year, snotel_melt$melt_doy, "SNOTEL (Paradise)", "melt_out_doy"),
  mk_row(melt_pair$year, melt_pair$wbm_melt_doy, "WBM, SNOTEL years", "melt_out_doy"))

sp_agreement <- tibble::tibble(
  comparison = c("SNOTEL vs WBM persistence", "SNOTEL vs satellite persistence",
                 "SNOTEL vs WBM melt-out date"),
  n_years = c(nrow(sp_three), nrow(sp_sat), nrow(melt_pair)),
  r = c(cor(sp_three$snotel_sp, sp_three$wbm_sp), cor(sp_sat$snotel_sp, sp_sat$satellite_sp),
        cor(melt_pair$melt_doy, melt_pair$wbm_melt_doy)),
  mean_difference = c(mean(sp_three$wbm_sp - sp_three$snotel_sp),
                      mean(sp_sat$satellite_sp - sp_sat$snotel_sp),
                      mean(melt_pair$wbm_melt_doy - melt_pair$melt_doy)))

# WBM melt-out by period (historical baseline vs. mid-century)
wbm_melt_change <- wbm_melt %>%
  dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_melt_doy = mean(melt_doy, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n_years = sum(!is.na(melt_doy)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(change_days = mean_melt_doy - mean_melt_doy[CF == "Historical"])

print(snotel_sp_summary)
print(sp_agreement)
print(wbm_melt_change)

readr::write_csv(snotel_sp_summary, "data/park/MORA/Tables/snotel_snow_persistence.csv")
readr::write_csv(sp_agreement, "data/park/MORA/Tables/snow_persistence_agreement.csv")
readr::write_csv(wbm_melt_change, "data/park/MORA/Tables/wbm_melt_out_change.csv")

# Figure: persistence from all three sources (top) and melt-out date (bottom)
sp_obs_colors <- c(plot_colors, "Satellite (Edith Current)" = "black", "SNOTEL (Paradise)" = pal$gold)
sp_panel <- wbm_sp_fig +
  geom_line(data = snotel_sp_annual, aes(x = year, y = snotel_sp, color = "SNOTEL (Paradise)"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = sp_obs_colors)
melt_panel <- ggplot(wbm_melt %>% dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1]),
                     aes(x = year, y = as.Date(melt_doy - 1, origin = "2001-01-01"), color = CF)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = snotel_melt, aes(x = year, y = as.Date(melt_doy - 1, origin = "2001-01-01"),
                                     color = "SNOTEL (Paradise)"), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = sp_obs_colors) +
  scale_y_date(date_labels = "%b %d") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Snow melt-out date") +
  theme_wsva()
sp_three_fig <- ggarrange(sp_panel, melt_panel, ncol = 1, common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom", align = "v")
sp_three_fig
ggsave(sp_three_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/snow_persistence_three_sources.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 7, bg = "white")

rm(sp_trend_test, wbm_sp_hist, wbm_sat_sp, snotel_swe, melt_out_doy, sp_three, sp_sat, melt_pair,
   mk_row, sp_obs_colors, sp_panel, melt_panel)

cold_days <- clim_hist %>%

              dplyr::filter(year(date) >= fut_yrs[1] & year(date) <= fut_yrs[2]) %>%

##### Water Balance Magnitude Statistics

Magnitude statistics: annual water balance summary statistics (inches) for
the historical period and each climate future, plus % change relative to
historical. These are AOI-wide hydrologic fluxes (not per-system), since
inches of runoff/precip/etc. don't depend on which candidate catchment is
selected - per-system volumes are in the Demand, Supply, and D:S / S:D
Ratios table below.

```{r wb_magnitude_table}

wbm_magnitude_vars <- c("precip_in_wbm", "rain_in_wbm", "snow_in_wbm",
                        "runoff_in_wbm", "melt_in_wbm", "aet_in_wbm", "pet_in_wbm")

change <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & year >= fut_yrs[1]  & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::select(CF, dplyr::all_of(wbm_magnitude_vars)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), list(mean = mean, sd = sd), na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-CF, names_to = "variable_stat", values_to = "value") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = CF, values_from = value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    `% Change Less Snowy Dry`  = 100 * (`Less Snowy Dry` - Historical) / Historical,
    `% Change Snowy Wet` = 100 * (`Snowy Wet` - Historical) / Historical
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~signif(.x, 3)))

kable(change,
     caption = "Annual water balance magnitude statistics (inches): mean and SD of precipitation, rain, snow, runoff, melt, AET, and PET for the historical period and each climate future, plus % change relative to historical.")

readr::write_csv(change, "data/park/MORA/Tables/magnitude_stats.csv")

rm(wbm_magnitude_vars)

```

##### Drought (SPEI) Summary Statistics

Drought

```{r drought_metrics}

drought_metrics_table <- spei_metrics %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # 1. Simplify Category logic
    Category = case_when(
      str_detect(Metric, "ext") ~ "Extreme",
      str_detect(Metric, "sev") ~ "Severe",
      str_detect(Metric, "mod") ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE                      ~ "Overall"
    ),
    # 2. Simplify Statistic logic
    Statistic = case_when(
      str_detect(Metric, "mean_duration")   ~ "Mean (Duration)",
      str_detect(Metric, "max_duration")    ~ "Maximum (Duration)",
      str_detect(Metric, "median_duration") ~ "Median (Duration)",
      str_detect(Metric, "mean_spei")       ~ "Mean (SPEI)",
      str_detect(Metric, "median_spei")     ~ "Median (SPEI)",
      str_detect(Metric, "sd_spei")         ~ "Standard Deviation",
      str_detect(Metric, "percent")         ~ "% of Period",
      TRUE                                  ~ Metric
    )
  ) %>%
  # 3. Sort by Category and Statistic
  dplyr::arrange(
    factor(Category, levels = c("Overall", "Moderate", "Severe", "Extreme")),
    factor(Statistic, levels = c("% of Period", "Mean (SPEI)", "Median (SPEI)", 
                                 "Standard Deviation", "n", "Mean (Duration)", 
                                 "Median (Duration)", "Maximum (Duration)"))
  ) %>%
  # 4. DYNAMIC SELECTION AND FORMATTING
  # Move Category/Statistic to the front, then keep everything else (all CFs)
  dplyr::select(Category, Statistic, everything()) %>%
  # Apply numeric conversion and significance to all columns EXCEPT Category/Statistic
  dplyr::mutate(across(-c(Category, Statistic), ~signif(as.numeric(.x), 3)))

kable(drought_metrics_table)

readr::write_csv(drought_metrics_table, "data/park/MORA/Tables/drought_metrics.csv")

```

##### Demand, Supply, and D:S / S:D Ratios

Demand (D:S) ratio: annual demand, supply, and demand-to-supply / storage-to-demand ratios, by candidate system, demand scenario, and climate future. Demand and supply are reported in millions of gallons per year.

```{r table_ds_annual}

ds_annual_table <- ds_annual %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    demand_mgal = demand_gal_mid_annual / 1e6,
    supply_mgal = supply_gal_annual     / 1e6
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(system, scenario, CF, demand_mgal, supply_mgal, DS_annual, SD_annual) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(system, scenario, CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~signif(.x, 3)))

kable(ds_annual_table,
     col.names = c("System", "Demand Scenario", "Climate Future", "Demand (M gal/yr)",
                  "Supply (M gal/yr)", "D:S", "S:D"),
     caption = "Annual demand, supply, and demand-to-supply (D:S) / storage-to-demand (S:D) ratios by candidate system, demand scenario, and climate future.")

readr::write_csv(ds_annual_table, "data/park/MORA/Tables/ds_annual_table.csv")

```

## Site Figure

Map of the three candidate water supply systems evaluated in this report -
the current Edith Creek intake, the proposed downstream Edith Creek intake,
and the Paradise Valley groundwater-fed area - along with the stream
mainstem each system's elevation profile was extracted along (`## -
Watersheds, Flowlines, and Stream Profiles`, above), the current
system's physical location, and NPS building footprints for developed-area
context. The basemap is the National Park Service's own Park Tiles
(https://www.nps.gov/maps/tools/park-tiles/), rendered with ggplot2 via
`get_nps_basemap()` / `geom_nps_basemap()`. A companion figure below
situates these three systems relative to the nearest USGS stream gauge and
its upstream drainage basin, and the USGS Paradise Warm Springs gauge (see
USGS Gauge and Warm Springs Context Figure, below).

```{r site_fig}

# --- 1. Assemble the three watersheds with a shared label field -----------
# Ordered largest to smallest (Paradise GW encloses Edith Downstream
# encloses Edith Current) so the smaller, nested watersheds draw on top
# and stay visible rather than being obscured by the larger polygons
# around them.
site_fig_watersheds <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  paradise_river_watershed   %>% dplyr::mutate(system = "Paradise GW")      %>% dplyr::select(system),
  down_edith_creek_watershed %>% dplyr::mutate(system = "Edith Downstream") %>% dplyr::select(system),
  system_watershed           %>% dplyr::mutate(system = "Edith Current")    %>% dplyr::select(system)
) %>%
  sf::st_transform(crs_use)

# Colors matching the convention used in mapview calls throughout this doc
site_fig_colors <- c(
  "Edith Current"    = "hotpink",
  "Edith Downstream" = "lightpink",
  "Paradise GW"       = "dodgerblue",
  "PV Potential Wells"  = "tomato"
)

# --- 2. NPS Park Tiles basemap ---------------------------------------------
# Tiles are served in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857); reproject everything else
# to match rather than reprojecting the downloaded raster. zoom = 15 was
# confirmed sharp for this AOI (a few km across) without being noticeably
# slower to fetch - tune per-figure if a given map covers a larger or
# smaller area than this one.
#nps_tiles <- get_nps_basemap(aoi = site_fig_watersheds, style = "standard", buffer_km = 1, zoom = 15)

site_fig_watersheds_3857 <- sf::st_transform(site_fig_watersheds, 3857)
site_fig_mainstems_3857  <- sf::st_transform(site_fig_mainstems, 3857)
site_fig_point_3857      <- sf::st_transform(site_fig_point, 3857)
park_buildings_3857      <- sf::st_transform(park_buildings, 3857)
park_boundary_3857       <- sf::st_transform(park_boundary, 3857)
edith_trib_3857          <- sf::st_transform(edith_trib, 3857)
potential_intake_3857   <- sf::st_transform(potential_intake, 3857)
paradise_valley_3857    <- st_read("data/park/MORA/paradise_valley_approx.kml") %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857)

site_fig_bbox <- current_system %>%
  sf::st_buffer(4000) %>%
  st_transform(3857) %>%
  sf::st_bbox()

nps_tiles <- get_nps_basemap(aoi = current_system %>%
  sf::st_buffer(4000) %>% st_transform(3857), style = "standard", buffer_km = 1, zoom = 14)

# --- 3. Main map ------------------------------------------------------------
site_fig <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_nps_basemap(nps_tiles) +
  geom_sf(data = paradise_valley_3857, aes(fill = "PV Potential Wells"), alpha = 0.4, color = "tomato", linetype = "dashed", lwd = .5) +
  # NPS building footprints, dark translucent gray, drawn under the
  # candidate-system watersheds so they read as developed-area texture
  # rather than competing visually with the colored polygons.
  geom_sf(data = park_buildings_3857 %>% st_centroid, aes(color = "Buildings in Service Area"), alpha = 0.8, shape = 15) +
  geom_sf(data = site_fig_watersheds_3857, aes(fill = system),
          color = "black", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.2) +
  # Mainstem flowlines and the current system's location aren't mapped to
  # a data field (single color/shape each) - explained in the caption
  # above rather than via a second legend, to keep the legend to one block.
  geom_sf(data = site_fig_mainstems_3857, aes(linetype = "Main Flowline"),color = "dodgerblue", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = edith_trib_3857, aes(linetype = "Tributary"), color = "dodgerblue", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = site_fig_point_3857, fill = "tomato", aes(color = "Current Intake"),
          shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = potential_intake_3857, fill = NA, aes(color = "Potential Intake"),
          shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = site_fig_colors, name = "") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("seagreen", "tomato","tomato")) +
  scale_linetype_manual("", values = c("solid", "dashed")) +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.3) +
  ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(location = "tr", which_north = "true",
                                    style = ggspatial::north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(site_fig_bbox["xmin"], site_fig_bbox["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(site_fig_bbox["ymin"], site_fig_bbox["ymax"]),
           crs = 3857, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
        plot.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 5.5, r = 5.5, b = 15, l = 5.5, unit = "pt"),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0), color = NA)) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 3),
         fill = guide_legend(nrow = 3))

#site_fig


ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/site_fig.jpg", site_fig, width = 7, height = 8, dpi = 600)

```

##### USGS Gauge and Warm Springs Context Figure

This companion figure situates the three candidate systems relative to the
broader surface-water monitoring network nearby: the nearest USGS stream
gauge (`## -- USGS Surface Water`, above) and its upstream drainage basin,
and the USGS Paradise Warm Springs gauge. As noted above, the stream
gauge's catchment is far larger than, and well downstream of, any of the
three candidate systems; both gauges are shown here for broader hydrologic
context only, not as direct proxies for the candidate systems. The gauge
is marked with a dark green triangle, and Paradise Warm Springs with an
orange diamond.

```{r gauge_context_fig}

# Paradise Warm Springs USGS gauge, built directly from its coordinates
# (not isolated by the generic `park_nwis_springs` pull in the USGS
# Springs chunk above).
paradise_warm_springs <- sf::st_sf(
  name = "Paradise Warm Springs",
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(-121.716811, 46.795327)), crs = 4326)
) %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857)

# `nearest_usgs_sw` (gauge point) and `basin` (its NLDI-delineated
# upstream drainage basin) come from the `usgs_sw` chunk above.
gauge_fig_gauge <- nearest_usgs_sw %>% sf::st_transform(3857)
gauge_fig_basin <- basin %>% sf::st_transform(3857)
gauge_fig_watersheds <- site_fig_watersheds_3857
park_boundary_gauge_3857 <- park_boundary_3857

# This figure covers a much larger area than the main site figure (the
# gauge's basin sits well downstream of the candidate systems), so a
# lower zoom keeps the tile fetch reasonable - tune down further if it's
# slow, or up if it looks soft once you see the render. aoi is the union
# of everything shown, so the fetch covers the whole figure.
gauge_tiles_aoi <- sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(gauge_fig_watersheds), sf::st_geometry(gauge_fig_basin)) %>%
  sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(sf::st_buffer(paradise_warm_springs, 200)))
gauge_tiles <- get_nps_basemap(aoi = gauge_tiles_aoi %>% st_union(), style = "standard", buffer_km = 1, zoom = 12)

gauge_fig_watersheds_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(gauge_fig_watersheds)
gauge_fig_basin_bbox      <- sf::st_bbox(gauge_fig_basin)
gauge_fig_springs_bbox    <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(paradise_warm_springs, 200))

gauge_fig_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(c(
  xmin = min(gauge_fig_watersheds_bbox["xmin"], gauge_fig_basin_bbox["xmin"], gauge_fig_springs_bbox["xmin"]),
  ymin = min(gauge_fig_watersheds_bbox["ymin"], gauge_fig_basin_bbox["ymin"], gauge_fig_springs_bbox["ymin"]),
  xmax = max(gauge_fig_watersheds_bbox["xmax"], gauge_fig_basin_bbox["xmax"], gauge_fig_springs_bbox["xmax"]),
  ymax = max(gauge_fig_watersheds_bbox["ymax"], gauge_fig_basin_bbox["ymax"], gauge_fig_springs_bbox["ymax"])
), crs = 3857) %>%
  sf::st_as_sfc() %>%
  sf::st_buffer(500) %>%
  sf::st_bbox()

gauge_context_fig <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_nps_basemap(gauge_tiles) +
  geom_sf(data = park_boundary_gauge_3857, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = gauge_fig_basin, fill = "gray70", alpha = 0.25,
          color = "gray40", linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_sf(data = gauge_fig_watersheds, aes(fill = system),
          color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_sf(data = gauge_fig_gauge, fill = "darkgreen", color = "black",
          shape = 24, size = 3.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = paradise_warm_springs, fill = "darkorange", color = "black",
          shape = 23, size = 3.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = site_fig_colors, name = "Candidate System") +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.3) +
  ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(location = "tr", which_north = "true",
                                    style = ggspatial::north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(gauge_fig_bbox["xmin"], gauge_fig_bbox["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(gauge_fig_bbox["ymin"], gauge_fig_bbox["ymax"]),
           crs = 3857, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.85), color = NA))

gauge_context_fig

washington <- tigris::states(cb = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(STUSPS == "WA") %>%
  sf::st_transform(crs_use)

park_centroid <- park_boundary %>%
  sf::st_transform(crs_use) %>%
  sf::st_union() %>%
  sf::st_centroid()

# --- 2. Inset map: simple vector outline, no basemap tiles needed at this
# statewide scale -------------------------------------------------------
inset_fig <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = washington, fill = "grey90", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = park_centroid, fill = "red", color = "black",
          shape = 21, size = 3.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8))

inset_fig

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/site_fig_inset.jpg", inset_fig, width = 2.5, height = 2.5, dpi = 600)

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(site_fig_bbox, site_fig_colors, park_centroid)
gc()

##### Geology Figure

Two-panel map of (a) bedrock and (b) surficial geology around Paradise,
from the NPS Geologic Resources Inventory layers loaded in `## - Geology`
(bedrock source map USGS I-432; surficial units from the GRI surficial
geodatabase). Many source unit names are long and the surficial map splits
glacial drift, mudflows, and slope deposits into many small units, so units
are grouped under short practical names (lookup tables below, unit symbols
retained in the code). Grouped polygons are dissolved so the boundaries
drawn are the major contacts between groups, not every internal contact.
Mapped faults are from the bedrock layer. The extent is the current
intake buffered by 6 km, wider than the site figure's 4 km so the nearest
mapped fault (Stevens Peak Fault) falls inside the frame.

```{r geology_fig}

# --- 1. Practical names for bedrock and surficial units ---------------------
# Ordered youngest to oldest; factor levels set the legend order.
bedrock_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~unit_symbol, ~geo_group,
  "ice",   "Glacier ice",
  "water", "Water",
  "Qs",    "Surficial deposits and landslides",
  "Qls",   "Surficial deposits and landslides",
  "Qra",   "Mount Rainier volcanic rocks",
  "Qroa",  "Mount Rainier volcanic rocks",
  "Qrp",   "Mount Rainier volcanic rocks",
  "Tha",   "Andesite of Bee Flat",
  "Tw",    "Welded tuff of The Palisades",
  "Tg",    "Granodiorite and porphyry intrusions",
  "Tdi",   "Granodiorite and porphyry intrusions",
  "Td",    "Diabase and basalt",
  "Tf",    "Fifes Peak Formation",
  "Ts",    "Stevens Ridge Formation",
  "Tar",   "Basaltic andesite and rhyolite",
  "To",    "Ohanapecosh Formation",
  "Tol",   "Ohanapecosh Formation",
  "Tor",   "Ohanapecosh Formation"
)

surficial_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~unit_symbol, ~geo_group,
  "ice",   "Glacier ice",
  "water", "Water",
  "Qa",    "Alluvium and alluvial cones",
  "Qac",   "Alluvium and alluvial cones",
  "Qt",    "Talus and coarse rock debris",
  "Qbf",   "Talus and coarse rock debris",
  "Qpt",   "Talus and coarse rock debris",
  "Qr",    "Talus and coarse rock debris",
  "Ql",    "Landslide and avalanche deposits",
  "Qly",   "Landslide and avalanche deposits",
  "Qav",   "Landslide and avalanche deposits",
  "Qp",    "Paradise mudflow",
  "Qv",    "Other mudflows",
  "Qo",    "Other mudflows",
  "Qmf",   "Other mudflows",
  "Qf",    "Other mudflows",
  "Qfa",   "Other mudflows",
  "Qfb",   "Other mudflows",
  "Qfc",   "Other mudflows",
  "Qfd",   "Other mudflows",
  "Qg",    "Glacial drift",
  "Qgy",   "Glacial drift",
  "Qgo",   "Glacial drift",
  "Qm",    "Glacial drift",
  "Qe",    "Glacial drift",
  "Qh",    "Glacial drift",
  "Qb",    "Glacial drift",
  "Qod",   "Glacial drift",
  "Qra",   "Mount Rainier volcanic rocks",
  "Tbr",   "Rocks older than Mount Rainier",
  "Qtr",   "Other",
  "Qbb",   "Other"
)

bedrock_colors <- c(
  "Glacier ice"                          = "white",
  "Water"                                = "#9ecae1",
  "Surficial deposits and landslides"    = "#f3e5ab",
  "Mount Rainier volcanic rocks"         = "#d98880",
  "Andesite of Bee Flat"                 = "#c39bd3",
  "Welded tuff of The Palisades"         = "#f0b27a",
  "Granodiorite and porphyry intrusions" = "#f5b7d4",
  "Diabase and basalt"                   = "#6c8f3a",
  "Fifes Peak Formation"                 = "#a9cce3",
  "Stevens Ridge Formation"              = "#c9a66b",
  "Basaltic andesite and rhyolite"       = "#a3a3a3",
  "Ohanapecosh Formation"                = "#82b88a"
)

surficial_colors <- c(
  "Glacier ice"                      = "white",
  "Water"                            = "#9ecae1",
  "Alluvium and alluvial cones"      = "#fff2a8",
  "Talus and coarse rock debris"     = "#bdbdbd",
  "Landslide and avalanche deposits" = "#c7a17a",
  "Paradise mudflow"                 = "#e59866",
  "Other mudflows"                   = "#f5cba7",
  "Glacial drift"                    = "#a2d9ce",
  "Mount Rainier volcanic rocks"     = "#d98880",
  "Rocks older than Mount Rainier"   = "#b8a6c9",
  "Other"                            = "#e5e7e9"
)

# --- 2. Extent, clip, and dissolve by practical group -----------------------
geo_fig_bbox <- current_system %>%
  sf::st_buffer(6000) %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857) %>%
  sf::st_bbox()

# Dissolving by group removes internal contacts, so the polygon outlines
# that remain are the major contacts between practical groups.
dissolve_geo <- function(geo, groups, colors) {
  geo %>%
    sf::st_transform(3857) %>%
    sf::st_make_valid() %>%
    sf::st_crop(geo_fig_bbox) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(groups, by = "unit_symbol") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(geo_group = dplyr::coalesce(geo_group, "Other")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(geo_group) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(.groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(geo_group = factor(geo_group, levels = names(colors)))
}

bedrock_fig_geo   <- dissolve_geo(bedrock_geo, bedrock_groups, bedrock_colors)
surficial_fig_geo <- dissolve_geo(surficial_geo, surficial_groups, surficial_colors)

# Faults, labeled by name; positional accuracy sets the line type
geo_fig_faults <- sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/mora_geology_gpkg/mora_geology.gpkg",
                              layer = "MORA_Faults", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  sf::st_transform(3857) %>%
  sf::st_crop(geo_fig_bbox) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(accuracy = dplyr::if_else(positional_accuracy == "approximate",
                                          "Fault, approximate", "Fault, known"))

geo_fig_fault_labels <- geo_fig_faults %>%
  dplyr::group_by(feature_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(.groups = "drop") %>%
  sf::st_point_on_surface()

# Share of each candidate watershed in each practical geology group, computed
# in the equal-area analysis CRS (Web Mercator areas are inflated at this
# latitude). Used for the brief geology description in Appendix A.
geology_by_system <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  list(Bedrock = bedrock_fig_geo, Surficial = surficial_fig_geo),
  function(geo, layer) {
    sf::st_intersection(sf::st_transform(site_fig_watersheds, crs_use),
                        sf::st_transform(geo, crs_use)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(sf::st_area(.)) / 1e6) %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::group_by(system) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * area_km2 / sum(area_km2)) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(layer = layer, geo_group = as.character(geo_group))
  }) %>%
  dplyr::select(layer, system, geo_group, area_km2, pct) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(layer, system, dplyr::desc(pct))

geology_by_system

readr::write_csv(geology_by_system, "data/park/MORA/Tables/geology_by_system.csv")

# Distance from the current intake and each candidate watershed to the
# nearest mapped fault segment (full layer, not just the figure extent).
geo_faults_all <- sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/mora_geology_gpkg/mora_geology.gpkg",
                              layer = "MORA_Faults", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  sf::st_transform(crs_use) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(feature_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(.groups = "drop")

fault_distance <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  feature_name = geo_faults_all$feature_name,
  location     = c("Current intake", site_fig_watersheds$system)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(distance_km = purrr::map2_dbl(feature_name, location, function(f, l) {
    target <- if (l == "Current intake") current_system else
      dplyr::filter(site_fig_watersheds, system == l)
    as.numeric(sf::st_distance(dplyr::filter(geo_faults_all, feature_name == f),
                               sf::st_transform(target, crs_use))[1, 1]) / 1000
  }))

fault_distance

readr::write_csv(fault_distance, "data/park/MORA/Tables/fault_distance.csv")

# --- 3. Basemap and panels --------------------------------------------------
geo_tiles <- get_nps_basemap(aoi = sf::st_as_sfc(geo_fig_bbox), style = "standard",
                             buffer_km = 0.5, zoom = 13)

geo_fig_panel <- function(geo, colors, title) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_nps_basemap(geo_tiles) +
    geom_sf(data = geo, aes(fill = geo_group), color = "black",
            linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.75) +
    geom_sf(data = geo_fig_faults, aes(linetype = accuracy),
            color = "red3", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_sf_label(data = geo_fig_fault_labels, aes(label = feature_name),
                  size = 2.5, color = "red3", label.size = 0,
                  fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.8), hjust = 1, nudge_x = -200) +
    geom_sf(data = site_fig_watersheds_3857, fill = NA, color = "black",
            linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_sf(data = site_fig_point_3857, fill = "tomato", color = "black",
            shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 0.8) +
    geom_sf(data = potential_intake_3857, fill = NA, color = "black",
            shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual("", values = colors, drop = TRUE) +
    scale_linetype_manual("", values = c("Fault, known" = "solid",
                                         "Fault, approximate" = "dashed")) +
    ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.3) +
    ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(location = "tr", which_north = "true",
                                      height = unit(1, "cm"), width = unit(1, "cm"),
                                      style = ggspatial::north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(geo_fig_bbox["xmin"], geo_fig_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(geo_fig_bbox["ymin"], geo_fig_bbox["ymax"]),
             crs = 3857, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
          panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, order = 1),
           linetype = guide_legend(ncol = 1, order = 2))
}

geology_fig <- ggarrange(
  geo_fig_panel(bedrock_fig_geo, bedrock_colors, "(a) Bedrock geology"),
  geo_fig_panel(surficial_fig_geo, surficial_colors, "(b) Surficial geology"),
  ncol = 2, align = "hv"
)

geology_fig

ggsave(geology_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/geology_fig.jpg",
       width = 11, height = 7.5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")

# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(bedrock_groups, surficial_groups, bedrock_colors, surficial_colors, geo_fig_bbox,
   dissolve_geo, bedrock_fig_geo, surficial_fig_geo, geo_fig_faults,
   geo_fig_fault_labels, geo_tiles, geo_fig_panel, geology_by_system,
   geo_faults_all, fault_distance)
gc()

#### Water Budget

Plot of historical and projected annual water budget components for the
contributing area, shown with a rolling 10-year average. Split into two
figures: climate/water-balance variables (inches and temperature) in the
first, and the three candidate systems' runoff (gallons) in the second -
mixing the two in one faceted plot with `scales = "free"` let each panel
scale independently, but the inches-scale panels were visually dwarfed next
to gallons-scale panels in the low-billions, so separating them gives both
sets of panels their own comparable footing.

```{r wb_fig}

plot_dat_climate <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(year,
                GCM,
                CF,
                "Precipitation (in)" = "precip_in_wbm",
                "Temperature (F)" = "tmean_F",
                "AET (in)" = "aet_in_wbm",
                "PET (in)" = "pet_in_wbm",
                "Snowmelt (in)" = "melt_in_wbm",
                "Rain (in)" = "rain_in_wbm",
                "Snow (in)" = "snow_in_wbm",
                "Runoff (in)" = "runoff_in_wbm") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(year, GCM, CF), names_to = "vars", values_to = "vals") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(vars, CF, GCM) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(roll_vals = data.table::frollmean(vals, 10, align = c("center"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

wb_fig <- ggplot(plot_dat_climate) + 
  # Add shaded region between 2035 and 2064
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = fut_yrs[1], xmax = fut_yrs[2] + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = vals, color = CF), lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = roll_vals, group = CF), 
            lineend = "round", color = "black", lwd = 1.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = roll_vals, color = CF),
            lineend = "round") +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  labs(y = "", x = "") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(vars, levels = c("Temperature (F)",
                                       "Precipitation (in)",
                                       "Rain (in)",
                                       "Snow (in)",
                                       "Snowmelt (in)",
                                       "AET (in)",
                                       "PET (in)",
                                       "Runoff (in)")),
             scales = "free", nrow = 2) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -20, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

wb_fig

dir.create("data/park/MORA/Figs", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(wb_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/water_balance_fig.jpg", width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 600)

```

##### Per-System Runoff (Water Budget)

Same rolling-average treatment, for the three candidate systems' WBM
runoff. Values run from roughly 4e8 to 6e9 gallons/year, so plain gallons
(or even thousands of gallons - still 6-7 digits) doesn't read cleanly on
an axis; converting to millions of gallons brings the range down to a
readable ~400-6,000.

```{r wb_fig_runoff_gal}

plot_dat_runoff <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(year,
                GCM,
                CF,
                "Runoff Edith (M gal)"      = "runoff_gal_edith_wbm",
                "Runoff Edith DS (M gal)"   = "runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm",
                "Runoff Paradise (M gal)"   = "runoff_gal_paradise_wbm") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("(M gal)"), ~ .x / 1e6)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(year, GCM, CF), names_to = "vars", values_to = "vals") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(vars, CF, GCM) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(roll_vals = data.table::frollmean(vals, 10, align = c("center"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

wb_fig_runoff_gal <- ggplot(plot_dat_runoff) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = fut_yrs[1], xmax = fut_yrs[2] + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0, alpha = .1) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = vals, color = CF), lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = roll_vals, group = CF),
            lineend = "round", color = "black", lwd = 1.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = roll_vals, color = CF),
            lineend = "round") +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  labs(y = "", x = "") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(vars, levels = c("Runoff Edith (M gal)",
                                       "Runoff Edith DS (M gal)",
                                       "Runoff Paradise (M gal)")),
              ncol = 3) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -20, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

wb_fig_runoff_gal

ggsave(wb_fig_runoff_gal, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/water_balance_runoff_gal_fig.jpg",
      width = 7, height = 3, dpi = 600)

```

#### Visitation

```{r vis_plot, fig.alt=c("Two-panel figure of Paradise visitation. Left: monthly visitor seasonality as a mean line with a shaded min/max ribbon, one line each for the historical and projected mid-century periods, showing the summer peak. Right: annual visitor trend from the observed record through 2100, with a shaded uncertainty ribbon and a shaded box marking the 2035-2064 mid-century window, in the same historical/projected colors.", "Scatter plot of annual visitors against mean annual temperature for the observed historical years, with a linear trend line, showing a positive relationship between warmer years and higher visitation.")}

# plot visitation

# This whole chunk was written against an older, pre-project_visitation()
# version of the visitation pipeline (a single "vis_clim" data frame with
# vis_smooth_low/mid/high, vis_pred, TotalVisitors columns; a "comparison_df"
# comparing monthly-aggregated vs. annual GAM fits). Neither object is
# defined anywhere in the current script - the pipeline was rebuilt around
# project_visitation() (see "## - Visitation", chunks `run-methods` and
# `select_vis`), and the objects that survive that rebuild for report
# plotting are `monthly_visitor_proportions` (long format: group, month,
# month_date, mean_vis, min_vis, max_vis, fraction) and `annual_visitation`
# (year, visitors_low/mid/high, source, group), both built from the
# selected gam_logistic method. Rewritten below to use those instead.

# 1. Define shared theme and scales for consistency
# BUG FIX: legend.margin = margin(t = -15) pulled the legend 15pt up from
# its row - fine for a legend sitting directly under its own single panel,
# but vis_fig_1 and vis_fig_2 below are combined via
# ggarrange(..., common.legend = TRUE), which extracts one shared legend
# into its own row beneath both panels; the negative top margin dragged
# that shared legend up into the panels' x-axis labels instead. Dropped to
# 0 so the shared legend sits in its own row without overlapping either
# panel.
vis_theme <- list(
  theme_wsva(),
  theme(legend.margin = margin(t = 0)),
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Projected" = pal$orange, "Historical" = pal$darkblue)),
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c("Projected" = pal$orange, "Historical" = pal$darkblue))
)

# 2. Plot 1: Monthly Seasonality
vis_fig_1 <- ggplot(monthly_visitor_proportions %>% dplyr::filter(group != "Other"),
                    aes(x = month_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_vis * fraction, ymax = max_vis * fraction, fill = group), alpha = 0.35) +
  # Accessibility Outline: Slightly larger black line underneath
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_vis * fraction, group = group), color = "black", lwd = 1.6, lineend = "round") +
  # Colored data line
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_vis * fraction, color = group), lwd = 1.1, lineend = "round") +
  # Scaling and Labels
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "K")) +
  scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%b")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Monthly Visitors") +
  vis_theme

# 3. Plot 2: Annual Trends
pdat <- annual_visitation %>%
  dplyr::filter(year < 2100) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(c_group = ifelse(source == "observed", "Historical", "Projected"))

vis_fig_2 <- ggplot(pdat, aes(x = year)) +
  # Shaded mid-century box
  annotate("rect", xmin = fut_yrs[1], xmax = fut_yrs[2] + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.3) + 
  
  # Uncertainty Ribbon (collapses to zero-width for the observed years,
  # since visitors_low == visitors_mid == visitors_high there)
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = visitors_low, ymax = visitors_high, fill = c_group), alpha = 0.4) +
  
  # Accessibility Outline: Black line, split by group
  geom_line(aes(y = visitors_mid, group = c_group), 
            color = "black", lwd = 1.3, lineend = "round") +
  # Colored data lines
  geom_line(aes(y = visitors_mid, color = c_group), lwd = 0.8, lineend = "round") +
  
  # Scaling and Labels
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Annual Visitors (Paradise)") +
  vis_theme

# 4. Final Composition
vis_fig_final <- ggarrange(
  vis_fig_1, vis_fig_2, 
  common.legend = TRUE, 
  legend = "bottom", 
  align = "hv"
)

vis_fig_final

ggsave(vis_fig_final, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/vis_fig_final.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 2.5)



# Plot climate vis relationship
# Rebuilt from data that's still live: annual_visitation's observed years
# (Paradise visitors, the visitor_col the whole projection pipeline is built
# on) joined to historical mean annual temperature from wbm_annual. The
# original version plotted whole-park TotalVisitors, but that raw series
# (and the vis_clim frame it came from) was cleaned up earlier in the script
# and isn't recoverable without re-pulling the source visitation data.
clim_vis_dat <- annual_visitation %>%
  dplyr::filter(source == "observed") %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    wbm_annual %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>% dplyr::select(year, tmean_F, snowpack_in_wbm),
    by = "year"
  )

ggplot(clim_vis_dat, aes(x = snowpack_in_wbm, y = visitors_mid)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", lwd = 2, lineend = "round") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = pal$darkblue, lwd = 1.5, lineend = "round") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "Maximum Annual Snowpack (in)", y = "Annual Visitors (Paradise)")

# The original "Plot model performance comparison" block (monthly-aggregated
# GAM vs. annual GAM vs. observed, via a "comparison_df") is removed rather
# than rebuilt: comparison_df is never defined anywhere in this script, and
# project_visitation()'s monthly output is disaggregated FROM the annual
# envelope (see .disaggregate_monthly() in src/project_visitation.R), not an
# independently-fit monthly model - so this specific QA comparison would
# need new modeling work, not just reconnecting a dropped variable. The
# 5-method comparison already built and saved above (run-methods chunk:
# fig_comparison_annual / fig_comparison_monthly) covers the "did we pick
# the right method" question this was likely checking. Let me know if you
