#### Water Use

```{r water_use_fig, fig.alt=c("Two-panel figure of Paradise water use estimated from visitation. Left: monthly use as a mean line with a shaded min/max ribbon, one line each for the historical and projected mid-century periods. Right: annual total use over the observed-through-projected record, with a shaded uncertainty ribbon and a shaded box marking the 2035-2064 mid-century window, plus a text label giving the low/mid/high gallons-per-visitor rates used to derive the estimate.")}

# FIX: this chunk previously referenced monthly_use_proportions$low_use_hist /
# mid_use_fut / etc. and annual_use$low_use / c_group - none of which exist
# on the current monthly_use_proportions/annual_use objects (both now carry
# a single long-format `group` column with mean/min/max, from the
# "estimate based on visitation" chunk above, not separate hist/fut
# columns). Leftover from an older pipeline version, same root cause as the
# vis_clim issue. Rebuilt below from the current objects, same visual
# pattern as the Visitation figure above (mean line + min/max ribbon, one
# color per group).
# Legend margins in use_fig, seasonal_fig, and sm_fig set to t = 0: these
# panels are combined with ggarrange(common.legend = TRUE), and a negative
# top margin drags the shared legend into the x-axis labels (same bug
# fixed on the visitor figure above).
use_fig <- vector("list", 2)

p_dat <- monthly_use_proportions %>% dplyr::filter(group %in% c("Historical", "Projected"))

use_fig[[1]] <- ggplot(p_dat, aes(x = month_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min_use, ymax = max_use, fill = group), alpha = 0.3) +
  # BUG FIX: this black outline layer had no group aesthetic, so with two
  # series sharing the same 12 month_date x-values (Historical and
  # Projected), geom_line sorted all 24 points by x and connected them as
  # one path, zigzagging between the two groups' values every month
  # ("shark tooth" pattern). Matches the group = group already implied by
  # color = group on the colored line layer below.
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_use, group = group), color = "black", lineend = "round", lwd = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_use, color = group), lwd = 1, lineend = "round") +
  # Observed (metered) mean monthly use, pre- and post-leak, as dashed lines
  # without ribbons so the modeled envelopes stay readable.
  geom_line(data = observed_monthly_use_proportions,
            aes(y = mean_use, color = group),
            lwd = 0.8, linetype = "22", lineend = "round") +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Historical" = pal$darkblue,
                                    "Projected" = pal$orange,
                                    "Recorded Pre-Leak" = pal$teal,
                                    "Recorded Post-Leak" = pal$pink),
                     breaks = c("Historical", "Projected",
                                "Recorded Pre-Leak", "Recorded Post-Leak")) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c("Projected" = pal$orange, "Historical" = pal$darkblue),
                    guide = "none") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
    linetype = c("solid", "solid", "22", "22")), nrow = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "K", big.mark = ",")) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Monthly Use (gal)") +
  scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%b")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

# Extend the plotted record through FUTURE_END_YEAR (2099, matching
# vis_fig_2's year < 2100 above) instead of the demand_summary table's
# Historical/Projected(2035-2064)/Other split, which was silently dropping
# both the 2026-2034 gap and the 2066-2099 tail from this figure. annual_use
# itself (and its "group" column) is left untouched, since demand_summary
# below still needs that exact Historical vs. 2035-2064-Projected scheme.
# c_group here is plotting-only: Historical = observed years, Projected =
# every modeled year after that, same two-way split vis_fig_2 uses for
# visitation.
p_dat2 <- annual_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(year < 2100) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(c_group = dplyr::if_else(group == "Historical", "Historical", "Projected"))

use_fig[[2]] <- ggplot(p_dat2, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = fut_yrs[1], xmax = fut_yrs[2] + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low_use_sum, ymax = high_use_sum, fill = c_group),
              alpha = 0.4, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mid_use_sum, group = c_group), color = "black", lwd = 2, lineend = "round") +
  geom_line(aes(y = mid_use_sum, color = c_group), lwd = 1, lineend = "round") +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Projected" = pal$orange,
                                    "Historical" = pal$darkblue)) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c("Projected" = pal$orange,
                                   "Historical" = pal$darkblue)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual Use (gal)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)) +
   annotate("label",
            x = -Inf,
            y = Inf,
            label = paste0("Low = ", round(low_use_per_visitor,2), " gal/visitor\n",
                            "Mid = ", round(mid_use_per_visitor,1), " gal/visitor\n",
                            "High = ", round(high_use_per_visitor,1),  " gal/visitor"),
            hjust = -.07,
            vjust = 1.1,
            label.size = 0,             # FORCE thickness to zero
            label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"),
            label.r = unit(0.25, "lines"),
            fill = "white",
            color = "black",
            size = 3
  )


# Compile figures

# Historic and future water use figure
hf_use_fig <- ggarrange(use_fig[[1]], use_fig[[2]], common.legend = TRUE, align = "hv", legend = "bottom")
hf_use_fig
ggsave(hf_use_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/hf_use_fig.jpg",

##### Water Demand Summary

Summary table: historical vs. mid-century (2035-2064) projected annual visitation
and water demand for Paradise, observed annual metered water use (for
comparison against the visitation-based estimate), and observed use-per-visitor
rates (pre-/post-2019 leak periods). Built for the report's Estimating Water
Demand section - pulls together numbers that were previously only plotted
(vis_fig_final, hf_use_fig) or printed individually (use_per_visitor) into one
place.

```{r water_demand_summary_table}

# Visitation: mean/min/max annual Paradise visitors, historical (observed)
# vs. projected (2035-2064 mid-century window), from annual_visitation
# (built above in the select_vis chunk).
visitation_summary <- annual_visitation %>%
  dplyr::filter(group %in% c("Historical", "Projected")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_years = dplyr::n(),
    mean_visitors = mean(visitors_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_visitors  = min(visitors_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_visitors  = max(visitors_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_change_from_hist = 100 * (mean_visitors - mean_visitors[group == "Historical"]) /
      mean_visitors[group == "Historical"]
  )

# Annual water demand (visitation x use-per-visitor rates): mean mid/low/high
# annual demand in million gallons, historical vs. projected, from
# annual_use (built above in the "estimate based on visitation" chunk).
demand_summary <- annual_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(group %in% c("Historical", "Projected")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_years = dplyr::n(),
    mean_demand_mgal = mean(mid_use_sum, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6,
    low_demand_mgal  = mean(low_use_sum, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6,
    high_demand_mgal = mean(high_use_sum, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_change_from_hist = 100 * (mean_demand_mgal - mean_demand_mgal[group == "Historical"]) /
      mean_demand_mgal[group == "Historical"]
  )

# Observed annual water use (metered, complete 12-month years only) - a
# direct sanity check against the visitation-based demand estimate above.
observed_annual_summary <- wateruse_annual %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_years = dplyr::n(),
    mean_use_mgal = mean(total_use, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6,
    min_use_mgal  = min(total_use, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6,
    max_use_mgal  = max(total_use, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6
  )

# Modeled monthly use: mean monthly use and the peak month of the mean
# monthly climatology, historical vs. projected (mid and high rates)
modeled_monthly_summary <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(group %in% c("Historical", "Projected"), !is.na(mid_use)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = month(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mid_use = mean(mid_use), high_use = mean(high_use), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_monthly_gal = mean(mid_use),
                   peak_month = month.abb[month[which.max(mid_use)]],
                   peak_month_mid_gal = max(mid_use),
                   peak_month_high_gal = high_use[which.max(mid_use)],
                   peak_month_days = lubridate::days_in_month(as.Date(paste0("2021-", month[which.max(mid_use)], "-01"))),
                   .groups = "drop")

# Potential maximum daily use: twice the average daily use of the peak month
peak_factor <- 2

water_use_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~metric, ~observed, ~modeled_historical, ~modeled_projected,
  "Daily use, mean (gal/day)",
    observed_daily_summary$mean_daily_gal, NA, NA,
  "Daily use, maximum (gal/day)",
    observed_daily_summary$max_daily_gal, NA, NA,
  "Monthly use, mean (Mgal/month)",
    observed_monthly_summary$mean_monthly_gal / 1e6,
    modeled_monthly_summary$mean_monthly_gal[modeled_monthly_summary$group == "Historical"] / 1e6,
    modeled_monthly_summary$mean_monthly_gal[modeled_monthly_summary$group == "Projected"] / 1e6,
  "Monthly use, peak month (Mgal/month)",
    observed_monthly_summary$max_monthly_gal / 1e6,
    modeled_monthly_summary$peak_month_mid_gal[modeled_monthly_summary$group == "Historical"] / 1e6,
    modeled_monthly_summary$peak_month_mid_gal[modeled_monthly_summary$group == "Projected"] / 1e6,
  "Annual use, mean (Mgal/yr)",
    observed_annual_summary$mean_use_mgal,
    demand_summary$mean_demand_mgal[demand_summary$group == "Historical"],
    demand_summary$mean_demand_mgal[demand_summary$group == "Projected"],
  "Potential maximum daily use, mid rate (gal/day)",
    peak_factor * observed_monthly_summary$max_monthly_gal /
      lubridate::days_in_month(observed_monthly_summary$max_month),
    with(dplyr::filter(modeled_monthly_summary, group == "Historical"), peak_factor * peak_month_mid_gal / peak_month_days),
    with(dplyr::filter(modeled_monthly_summary, group == "Projected"), peak_factor * peak_month_mid_gal / peak_month_days),
  "Potential maximum daily use, high rate (gal/day)",
    NA,
    with(dplyr::filter(modeled_monthly_summary, group == "Historical"), peak_factor * peak_month_high_gal / peak_month_days),
    with(dplyr::filter(modeled_monthly_summary, group == "Projected"), peak_factor * peak_month_high_gal / peak_month_days)
)

print(visitation_summary)
print(demand_summary)
print(observed_annual_summary)
print(use_per_visitor)
print(modeled_monthly_summary)
print(water_use_summary)
readr::write_csv(water_use_summary, "data/park/MORA/Tables/water_use_summary.csv")

```

Treatment capacity, filter loading, and share of Edith Creek baseflow. The
treatment system is rated at 100 gpm on the Washington State Department of
Health facilities form, but staff report an operating maximum closer to 80 gpm,
and the plant runs up to 15 hours per day. These calculations compare daily
demand with what the plant can treat, estimate how filter loading scales with
the volume treated, and express withdrawals as a share of Edith Creek baseflow
(about 1 cfs, measured September 3, 2026, near the annual low flow).

```{r treatment_capacity_and_baseflow}

cfs_to_gpm <- 7.48052 * 60   # gpm per cfs

# --- 1. Daily treatment capacity vs. daily demand ---------------------------

treatment_capacity <- tidyr::crossing(rate_gpm = c(80, 100), hours_per_day = c(15, 24)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(capacity_gal_day = rate_gpm * hours_per_day * 60)

mm <- function(grp, col) {
  r <- dplyr::filter(modeled_monthly_summary, group == grp)
  r[[col]] / r$peak_month_days
}

daily_demand_cases <- tibble::tribble(
  ~case,                                          ~gal_day,
  "Observed: highest metered day",                observed_daily_summary$max_daily_gal,
  "Modeled historical: peak-month average day",   mm("Historical", "peak_month_mid_gal"),
  "Modeled historical: potential max day, mid",   peak_factor * mm("Historical", "peak_month_mid_gal"),
  "Modeled historical: potential max day, high",  peak_factor * mm("Historical", "peak_month_high_gal"),
  "Projected: peak-month average day, mid",       mm("Projected", "peak_month_mid_gal"),
  "Projected: peak-month average day, high",      mm("Projected", "peak_month_high_gal"),
  "Projected: potential max day, mid",            peak_factor * mm("Projected", "peak_month_mid_gal"),
  "Projected: potential max day, high",           peak_factor * mm("Projected", "peak_month_high_gal")
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(required_gpm_15h = gal_day / (15 * 60),
                required_gpm_24h = gal_day / (24 * 60),
                exceeds_80gpm_15h = gal_day > 80 * 15 * 60,
                exceeds_80gpm_24h = gal_day > 80 * 24 * 60,
                exceeds_100gpm_15h = gal_day > 100 * 15 * 60,
                exceeds_100gpm_24h = gal_day > 100 * 24 * 60)

print(treatment_capacity)
print(daily_demand_cases, width = Inf)
readr::write_csv(daily_demand_cases, "data/park/MORA/Tables/treatment_capacity_vs_demand.csv")

# --- 2. Filter loading: volume treated relative to current operation --------

# With the same sediment concentration, filter loading (and so the frequency
# of filter changes) scales with the volume of water treated. Current
# operation is the post-leak period; pre-leak is shown for comparison.
leak_climatology <- monthly_leak_summary %>%
  dplyr::group_by(period) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(annual_gal = sum(avg_use), aug_gal = avg_use[m_num == 8], .groups = "drop")

post <- dplyr::filter(leak_climatology, grepl("Post", period))
pre  <- dplyr::filter(leak_climatology, grepl("Pre", period))
proj <- dplyr::filter(modeled_monthly_summary, group == "Projected")
proj_annual_mid  <- demand_summary$mean_demand_mgal[demand_summary$group == "Projected"] * 1e6
proj_annual_high <- demand_summary$high_demand_mgal[demand_summary$group == "Projected"] * 1e6

filter_loading <- tibble::tribble(
  ~case,                         ~annual_gal,       ~aug_gal,
  "Pre-leak (observed)",         pre$annual_gal,    pre$aug_gal,
  "Post-leak, current (observed)", post$annual_gal, post$aug_gal,
  "Projected, mid rate",         proj_annual_mid,   proj$peak_month_mid_gal,
  "Projected, high rate",        proj_annual_high,  proj$peak_month_high_gal
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(annual_vs_current = annual_gal / post$annual_gal,
                aug_vs_current = aug_gal / post$aug_gal,
                annual_vs_preleak = annual_gal / pre$annual_gal,
                aug_vs_preleak = aug_gal / pre$aug_gal)

print(filter_loading, width = Inf)
readr::write_csv(filter_loading, "data/park/MORA/Tables/filter_loading.csv")

# --- 3. Share of Edith Creek baseflow ---------------------------------------

measured_baseflow_cfs <- 0.85  # official field measurement, September 3, 2026

# Future baseflow: scale the measurement by the modeled change in Edith
# Current's late-summer low flow, the lowest point of the mean July-October
# routed hydrograph (routing-ensemble mean, averaged across years)
late_summer_low <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), doy = yday(date), month = month(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter((CF == "Historical" & year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (CF != "Historical" & year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2]),
                month %in% 7:10) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, doy) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_gpm = mean(mean_edith_discharge) / 1440, .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(low_flow_gpm = min(mean_gpm),
                   low_flow_date = format(as.Date(doy[which.min(mean_gpm)] - 1, origin = "2021-01-01"), "%b %d"),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ratio_to_historical = low_flow_gpm / low_flow_gpm[CF == "Historical"],
                baseflow_cfs = measured_baseflow_cfs * ratio_to_historical,
                baseflow_gpm = baseflow_cfs * cfs_to_gpm)

withdrawal_cases <- tibble::tribble(
  ~withdrawal,                                      ~gpm,
  "Intake at operating maximum (80 gpm)",           80,
  "Intake at rated capacity (100 gpm)",             100,
  "Observed highest metered day (daily average)",   observed_daily_summary$max_daily_gal / 1440,
  "Projected potential max day, mid (daily average)",  peak_factor * mm("Projected", "peak_month_mid_gal") / 1440,
  "Projected potential max day, high (daily average)", peak_factor * mm("Projected", "peak_month_high_gal") / 1440
)

baseflow_share <- tidyr::crossing(late_summer_low %>% dplyr::select(CF, baseflow_cfs, baseflow_gpm),
                                  withdrawal_cases) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_of_baseflow = 100 * gpm / baseflow_gpm)

print(late_summer_low)
print(baseflow_share, n = Inf)
readr::write_csv(late_summer_low, "data/park/MORA/Tables/edith_late_summer_low_flow.csv")
readr::write_csv(baseflow_share, "data/park/MORA/Tables/edith_baseflow_share.csv")

rm(mm, post, pre, proj, proj_annual_mid, proj_annual_high)

```

#### Annual Runoff Variability

Plot showing runoff variability for historical and future CFs.

```{r}

# This chunk previously referenced a single "runoff_gal_wbm" column from an
# earlier, single-system version of the script; that column doesn't exist on
# wbm_annual (which carries the three per-system runoff columns instead -
# see the Water Budget figure fix above). Updated the same way: pivoted to
# long format by system, in millions of gallons, and faceted by system so
# each candidate system gets its own row of panels.
pdat <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(runoff_gal_edith_wbm, runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm, runoff_gal_paradise_wbm),
    names_to = "system", values_to = "Runoff"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    system = dplyr::recode(system,
      runoff_gal_edith_wbm = "Edith Current",
      runoff_gal_down_edith_wbm = "Edith Downstream",
      runoff_gal_paradise_wbm = "Paradise GW"),
    system = factor(system, levels = c("Edith Current", "Edith Downstream", "Paradise GW")),
    Runoff = Runoff / 1e6
  )

# Historical reference stats (median, 0.1/0.9 quantile), computed per system
hist_stats <- pdat %>%
  dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(hist_median = median(Runoff, na.rm = TRUE),
                   hist_q_low  = quantile(Runoff, .1, na.rm = TRUE),
                   hist_q_high = quantile(Runoff, .9, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop")

pdat <- pdat %>% dplyr::left_join(hist_stats, by = "system")

runoff_var <- ggplot(pdat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rect_min = ifelse(CF != "Historical", fut_yrs[1], hist_yrs[1]),
                rect_max = ifelse(CF != "Historical", fut_yrs[2], hist_yrs[2]),
                CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = rect_min, xmax = rect_max, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = year, y = Runoff, fill = CF), stat = "identity", width = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(data = hist_stats, aes(yintercept = hist_median, color = "Historical Median")) +
  geom_hline(data = hist_stats, aes(yintercept = hist_q_low, color = "Historical 0.1 and 0.9 Quantile"), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(data = hist_stats, aes(yintercept = hist_q_high, color = "Historical 0.1 and 0.9 Quantile"), linetype = "dashed") +
 theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual Runoff (M gal)") +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  facet_grid(system ~ CF, scales = "free") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(strip.background =element_rect(fill="gray95")) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(colour = 'black', face = "bold")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) 


runoff_var

# Calculate consecutive dry years, per system x CF
t <- pdat %>%
  dplyr::filter((year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) | (year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(r_lt_p1 = ifelse(Runoff <= hist_q_low, 1, 0),
                r_gt_p90 = ifelse(Runoff  >= hist_q_high, 1, 0),
                tot = ifelse(Runoff > 0, 1, 0)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(r_lt_p1, r_gt_p90, tot, CF, system, Runoff, year)

consec_dry <- t %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, CF) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {
    r <- rle(.x$r_lt_p1)
    tibble::tibble(max_consec_dry_yrs = suppressWarnings(max(r$lengths[r$values == 1], na.rm = TRUE)))
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(max_consec_dry_yrs = ifelse(is.infinite(max_consec_dry_yrs), 0, max_consec_dry_yrs))

print(consec_dry)

# Get maximum runoff during each time period, per system
max_run <- t %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(max_runoff = max(Runoff, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Percentage increase for warm/wet max compared to historical max, per system
max_run %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = CF, values_from = max_runoff) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_wet_vs_hist = 100 * (`Snowy Wet` - Historical) / Historical)

# Print summary of extreme wet and dry years, per system
t %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(c(r_lt_p1, r_gt_p90, tot), list(mean = mean, sum = sum)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(lt_per = 100 * r_lt_p1_sum / tot_sum,
                gt_per = 100 * r_gt_p90_sum / tot_sum)


ggsave(runoff_var, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/runoff_var_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 8, height = 7)

##### Precip Extreme Events

Frequency of extreme (p99) precipitation events.

```{r precip_extreme_events}

# FIX: renamed from "extreme_runoff_frequency" - that label was reused by
# the Runoff Extreme Events chunk below (now "runoff_extreme_events"). A
# duplicate chunk label is a hard knitr error.
df <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::rename(cf = CF) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cf) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rolling_3day = frollapply(precip_in_wbm, FUN = "sum", n = 3, align = "center"),
                date = as_date(date),
                year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(rolling_3day))

 df %>% dplyr::filter(year < 2070) %>% dplyr::group_by(cf) %>% dplyr::summarize(r = max(rolling_3day))

var = "precip_in_wbm"
q1 = 0.05 
q2 = 0.99

historic <- df %>%
  dplyr::filter(cf == "Historical") %>%
  dplyr::rename("variable" = var) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Explore runoff events ONLY:
  dplyr::filter(rolling_3day > 0,
                # AND only data from 1980-2012
                year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2]) %>%
  dplyr::select(rolling_3day) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(QLOW = quantile(rolling_3day, probs = as.numeric(q1)),
                   QHIGH = quantile(rolling_3day, probs = as.numeric(q2)))

year_counts <- df %>%
  dplyr::rename("variable" = var) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(low_day = ifelse(rolling_3day <= historic$QLOW, 1, 0),
                high_day = ifelse(rolling_3day >= historic$QHIGH, 1, 0)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cf, year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(n_low_days = sum(low_day),
                   n_high_days = sum(high_day)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(type = ifelse(cf == "Historical", "Historical", "Future"))

sanity_check <- df %>%
  dplyr::filter(rolling_3day >= historic$QHIGH)

stats_precip <- year_counts %>%
  dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2] | year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2]) %>%
  group_by(cf) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(n_high_days, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(n_high_days, na.rm = TRUE))


ggplot(year_counts %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rect_min = ifelse(cf != "Historical", fut_yrs[1], hist_yrs[1]),
                rect_max = ifelse(cf != "Historical", fut_yrs[2], hist_yrs[2]),
                CF = factor(cf, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = rect_min, xmax = rect_max, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0,  alpha = .1) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = year, y = n_high_days, fill = CF), stat = "identity", width = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
 theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Number Precipitation Events ≥ p99") +
  #scale_y_continuous(labels = unit_format(unit = "M", scale = 1e-6)) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("gray30", pal$black, "gray30")) +
  facet_wrap(~CF, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(strip.background =element_rect(fill="gray95")) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(colour = 'black', face = "bold")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))


ggsave(filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/precip_extreme_fig.jpg", dpi = 600, height = 3, width = 7.5)
```

#### Seasonality

A plot of the seasonality of historical and projected rain, snowmelt, actual ET, runoff, recharge, and discharge.

```{r figure_12}
# Create Seasonal Dataframe
# Note: dropped "runoff_gal_wbm" from this list - it doesn't exist on wbm
# (leftover from a single-system version of the script, see the Water
# Budget / Annual Runoff Variability fix notes below) and isn't referenced
# anywhere downstream in this chunk, so it's safe to remove rather than fix.
sum_cols <- c("aet_in_wbm","melt_in_wbm","pet_in_wbm","rain_in_wbm","runoff_in_wbm","snow_in_wbm", "precip_in_wbm")
mean_cols <- c("tmean_C") 

seasonal_wbm <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(season = case_when(month(date) %in% c(12,1,2) ~ "Winter",
                                   month(date) %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Spring",
                                   month(date) %in% c(6,7,8) ~ "Summer",
                                   month(date) %in% c(9,10,11) ~ "Fall")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(y = year(date)) %>%
  # Restrict to the analysis windows (seasonal_stats below feeds the seasonal
  # % change in the report, so it must not average over all years).
  dplyr::filter((y >= hist_yrs[1] & y <= hist_yrs[2]) | (y >= fut_yrs[1] & y <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(date,GCM)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(y,season,CF)%>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    across(all_of(sum_cols),sum),  # Sum of columns in sum_cols list
    across(all_of(mean_cols),mean),
    .groups = "keep") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

seasonal_stats <- seasonal_wbm %>%
  dplyr::group_by(y, CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_fraction = as.numeric(100* runoff_in_wbm/sum(runoff_in_wbm))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, season) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(runoff = mean(runoff_in_wbm),
                   runoff_fraction = mean(runoff_fraction)) %>%
  #dplyr::filter(season %in% c("Spring", "Fall")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF, season) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(runoff_fraction = sum(runoff_fraction),
                   runoff = mean(runoff)) 

hist_seasonal_stats <- seasonal_stats %>% dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>%
  dplyr::rename(c("runoff_fraction_hist" = "runoff_fraction",
                  "runoff_hist" = "runoff")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(season, runoff_hist)

seasonal_stats <- seasonal_stats %>%
  left_join(hist_seasonal_stats , by = "season") %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF != "Historical") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_change = 100 * (runoff - runoff_hist) / runoff_hist)

print(seasonal_stats)



seasonal_fig <- ggarrange(
  
  ggplot(seasonal_wbm %>% dplyr::filter(y >= hist_yrs[1] & y <= hist_yrs[2] | y >= fut_yrs[1] & y <= fut_yrs[2])) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")), 
                     y = rain_in_wbm, fill = CF),
                 outlier.shape = NA,
                 linewidth = .2) +
    theme_wsva() +
    labs(x = "", y = "Rain (in)") +
    scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)),
  ggplot(seasonal_wbm %>% dplyr::filter(y >= hist_yrs[1] & y <= hist_yrs[2] | y >= fut_yrs[1] & y <= fut_yrs[2])) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),  
                     y = snow_in_wbm, fill = CF),
                 outlier.shape = NA,
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
    theme_wsva() +
    labs(x = "", y = "Snowmelt (in)") +
    scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)),
  ggplot(seasonal_wbm %>% dplyr::filter(y >= hist_yrs[1] & y <= hist_yrs[2] | y >= fut_yrs[1] & y <= fut_yrs[2])) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),  
                     y = aet_in_wbm, fill = CF),
                 outlier.shape = NA,
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
    theme_wsva() +
    labs(x = "", y = "AET (in)") +
    scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)),
  ggplot(seasonal_wbm %>% dplyr::filter(y >= hist_yrs[1] & y <= hist_yrs[2] | y >= fut_yrs[1] & y <= fut_yrs[2])) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),  
                     y = runoff_in_wbm, fill = CF),
                 outlier.shape = NA,
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
    theme_wsva() +
    labs(x = "", y = "Runoff (in)") +
    scale_fill_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)),
  common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom", nrow = 2, ncol = 2
)

seasonal_fig

ggsave(seasonal_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/seasonal_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 5)

##### Snowmelt Timing and Fraction

A plot of the fraction of snowmelt-derived runoff plotted through time across climate futures:

```{r snowmelt_timing_fig}

# Daily Snowmelt Statistics
snowmelt_stats_d <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::filter((year(date) >= hist_yrs[1] & year(date) <= hist_yrs[2]) |
                (year(date) >= fut_yrs[1] & year(date) <= fut_yrs[2])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(melt_run = (melt_in_wbm / (melt_in_wbm + rain_in_wbm)) * runoff_in_wbm,
                              rain_run = (rain_in_wbm / (melt_in_wbm + rain_in_wbm)) * runoff_in_wbm,
                              snow_frac_precip = (precip_in_wbm - rain_in_wbm) / precip_in_wbm,
                              melt_frac = melt_run / (melt_run + rain_run),
                              rain_frac = rain_run/ (melt_run + rain_run),
                              doy = yday(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(doy, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(melt_frac_min = min(melt_frac, na.rm = TRUE),
                   melt_frac_mean = mean(melt_frac, na.rm = TRUE),
                   melt_frac_max = max(melt_frac, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow_frac_precip_min = min(snow_frac_precip, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow_frac_precip_mean = mean(snow_frac_precip, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow_frac_precip_max = max(snow_frac_precip, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snowmelt = mean(melt_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   # "discharge_gal_wbm" doesn't exist on wbm (same
                   # single-system leftover as the other fixes in this doc -
                   # see the SPEI section note). Rather than fabricate a
                   # per-system WBM-runoff-based discharge series here (peak
                   # timing is essentially area-invariant across the three
                   # candidate systems, since they're all scaled from the
                   # same runoff_in_wbm), this uses the already-calibrated
                   # routed discharge at the current system
                   # (mean_edith_discharge, in GPD - see the Hock/routing
                   # calibration section) converted to gpm.
                   discharge = mean(mean_edith_discharge / 1440, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(snowmelt_mov = data.table::frollmean(snowmelt, 5, align = c("center"), na.rm = TRUE),
                discharge_mov = data.table::frollmean(discharge, 5, align = c("center"), na.rm = TRUE),
                doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

# Extract Peak Melt
peak_melt <- snowmelt_stats_d %>%
  slice_max(snowmelt_mov)

# Exctract Peak Discharge
peak_discharge <- snowmelt_stats_d %>%
  slice_max(discharge_mov)
  
# Snowmelt Fraction Figure
pdat <- wbm_annual %>%
                ungroup() %>%
                #dplyr::select(-c("name")) %>%
                dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
                dplyr::mutate(melt_run = (melt_in_wbm / (melt_in_wbm + rain_in_wbm)) * runoff_in_wbm,
                              rain_run = (rain_in_wbm / (melt_in_wbm + rain_in_wbm)) * runoff_in_wbm,
                              snow_frac_precip = (precip_in_wbm - rain_in_wbm) / precip_in_wbm,
                              melt_frac = melt_run / (melt_run + rain_run),
                              rain_frac = rain_run/ (melt_run + rain_run)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

snowmelt_stats <- pdat %>%
 dplyr::filter(year >= hist_yrs[1] & year <= hist_yrs[2] | year >= fut_yrs[1] & year <= fut_yrs[2]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(melt_frac_min = min(melt_frac),
                  melt_frac_mean = mean(melt_frac),
                   max_frac_mean = max(melt_frac),
                   snow_frac_min = min(snow_frac_precip),
                   snow_frac_mean = mean(snow_frac_precip),
                   snow_frac_max = max(snow_frac_precip)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = factor(CF, levels = c("Historical", "Less Snowy Dry", "Snowy Wet")))

print(peak_melt %>% dplyr::select(CF, doy, doy_date, snowmelt_mov))
print(snowmelt_stats)


# Snowmelt Fraction Figure
sm_fraction_fig <- ggplot(pdat) +
  # Add shaded region between 2035 and 2064
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = fut_yrs[1], xmax = fut_yrs[2] + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), 
            fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.1) + 
  # FIX: "type" is not a real ggplot aesthetic (silently dropped), so this
  # background line had no group aesthetic and connected all three CF
  # series into one continuous/zigzag line instead of three separate ones -
  # same bug class as the color="group" fix elsewhere in this doc.
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = melt_frac, group = CF), color = "black", lwd = 2, lineend = "round") +
  geom_line(aes(x = year, y = melt_frac, color = CF), lwd = 1.5, lineend = "round") +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Snowmelt Fraction of Runoff") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

# Snowmelt timing figure
sm_timing_fig <- ggplot(snowmelt_stats_d, aes(x = doy_date, color = CF)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = snowmelt), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = snowmelt_mov, group = CF), linewidth = 2, color = "black", lineend = "round") +
  geom_line(aes(y = snowmelt_mov), linewidth = 1.5, lineend = "round") +
  geom_vline(data = peak_melt, aes(color = CF, xintercept = doy_date, linetype = "Peak Melt"), lwd = 1.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("DOY Mean & \n5-Day \nRolling Mean", values = plot_colors) +
  scale_linetype_manual("", values = c(1)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %d") +

sm_timing_fig

# Discharge timing figure
dis_timing_fig <- ggplot(snowmelt_stats_d, aes(x = doy_date, color = CF)) +

sm_fig <- ggarrange(sm_fraction_fig, sm_timing_fig, dis_timing_fig, ncol = 1, common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom", align = "hv")

#### SPEI Drought plot

```{r spei_plot}

# All years are plotted (observed 2013-2026 included). Only 1980-2012 is used to
# fit the SPEI reference distribution (see ref.start/ref.end in the spei chunk).
drought <- ggplot(spei_results, aes(x = ym, y = spei)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.Date("2035-01-01"), xmax = as.Date("2065-01-01"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), 
            fill = "lightgrey", alpha = 0.1) + 
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = -1), linetype = "dashed", color = "pink3") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = -1.5), linetype = "dashed", color = "red2") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = -2), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred") +
   # FIX: at lwd = 2/1.5 these lines were thick enough, combined with full
   # overlap between the two projected CFs (Less Snowy Dry and Snowy Wet
   # share the same 1980-2099 x-range post-2025), that the black outline
   # was fully covered by the colored line on top of it and the panel read
   # as a dense smear rather than two distinguishable series. Thinned both
   # layers and added alpha to the colored line so the black edge stays
   # visible and both CFs read through where they overlap.
   geom_line(aes(group = CF), col = "black", lineend = "round", lwd = 1) +
   geom_line(aes(col = CF), lwd = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors) +
  labs(x = "", y = "SPEI") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = as.Date("1980-01-01"), y = -1, label = "Moderate Drought"),
            hjust = .25, vjust = 1.1, check_overlap = TRUE, color = "pink3", size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = as.Date("1980-01-01"), y = -1.5, label = "Severe Drought"),
            hjust = .25, vjust = 1.1, check_overlap = TRUE, color = "red2", size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = as.Date("1980-01-01"), y = -2, label = "Extreme Drought"),
            hjust = .25, vjust = 1.1, check_overlap = TRUE, color = "darkred", size = 3)

#### Demand vs Supply

```{r demand_vs_supply_fig, fig.alt=c("Monthly supply and demand volume by candidate water supply system, one row of panels per system (Edith Current, Edith Downstream, Paradise GW), with a dashed demand ribbon and line per scenario (pre-leak, post-leak, and each projected climate future) plotted against a solid supply line for the matching climate future, and a dotted reference line for tank capacity.", "Monthly demand-to-supply (D:S) ratio by system and scenario, on a log scale, with solid and dashed reference lines at D:S = 1 and D:S = 0.2.", "Annual D:S ratio by system and scenario as a bar chart (each scenario's demand and supply summed across its analysis window, so this is a single value per scenario rather than a year-by-year series), with the same D:S = 1 and D:S = 0.2 reference lines.")}

# FIX: this chunk previously referenced monthly_supply_proportions,
# monthly_use_long, and DS_df - none of which are defined anywhere in this
# script (same leftover-pipeline root cause as the vis_clim/Water Use
# issues above), and it predates the three-candidate-system structure the
# rest of the report is built around (no per-system faceting). Rebuilt
# below from ds_monthly/ds_annual (built in the supply_demand_monthly
# chunk), faceted by system to match tank_storage_fig, and reusing
# tank_colors (same scenario_label convention: Pre-Leak/Post-Leak
# Historical, Projected x each future CF) for consistency with that figure.

ds_monthly_labeled <- ds_monthly %>%
  dplyr::mutate(scenario_label = ifelse(
    scenario == "Projected (2035-2064)",
    paste0(scenario, " - ", CF),
    scenario))

# Sub-figure 1: raw monthly supply vs. demand, per system. Demand has a
# low/high range (from the use-per-visitor low/mid/high rates for the
# future, and observed min/max for the historical periods); supply here is
# the monthly climatology mean only (supply_monthly, built above, doesn't
# retain a min/max range at that step), so it's shown as a line, not a
# ribbon - no fabricated range.
supply_demand_fig <- ggplot(ds_monthly_labeled, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = demand_gal_low, ymax = demand_gal_high, fill = scenario_label),
              alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = demand_gal_mid, color = scenario_label, linetype = "Demand"),
            linewidth = 1, lineend = "round") +
  geom_line(aes(y = supply_gal, color = scenario_label, linetype = "Supply"),
            linewidth = 1, lineend = "round") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tank_cap_gal, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = tank_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = tank_colors) +
  scale_linetype_manual("", values = c("Demand" = 2, "Supply" = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k gal")) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Monthly Volume (gal)",
       subtitle = paste0("Dotted line = tank capacity (", scales::comma(tank_cap_gal), " gal)")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(t = -10, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

supply_demand_fig

ggsave(supply_demand_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/supply_demand_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 8, height = 7)

# Sub-figure 2: monthly D:S ratio, per system (DS to DS_stress as the
# ribbon - mean-demand to high-demand D:S).
monthly_ds_fig <- ggplot(ds_monthly_labeled, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = DS, ymax = DS_stress, fill = scenario_label), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = DS, color = scenario_label), linewidth = 1, lineend = "round") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~system, ncol = 1) +
  theme_wsva() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Monthly D:S") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual("", values = tank_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = tank_colors)

# Sub-figure 3: annual D:S. ds_annual is a single summed-across-the-window
# total per system/scenario (not a year-by-year series like SPEI above -
# demand/supply climatologies here are averaged within their hist_yrs/
# fut_yrs window, not tied to individual calendar years), so this is a bar
# comparison across scenarios rather than a time series.
annual_ds_fig <- ggplot(
  ds_annual %>% dplyr::mutate(scenario_label = ifelse(
    scenario == "Projected (2035-2064)", paste0(scenario, " - ", CF), scenario)),
  aes(x = scenario_label, y = DS_annual, fill = scenario_label)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~system) +
  theme_wsva() +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = tank_colors) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual D:S") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom")

ds_fig <- ggarrange(monthly_ds_fig, annual_ds_fig, ncol = 1, common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom")

ds_fig

ggsave(ds_fig, filename = "data/park/MORA/Figs/ds_fig.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 9)


# Tightest month (lowest monthly supply:demand) for each system, demand
# scenario, and climate future (Appendix A)
ds_monthly_tightest <- ds_monthly %>%
  dplyr::group_by(system, scenario, CF) %>%
  dplyr::slice_min(SD, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::transmute(system, scenario, CF, month = month.abb[month],
                   demand_gal = demand_gal_mid, supply_gal, DS, SD)

print(ds_monthly_tightest)
readr::write_csv(ds_monthly_tightest, "data/park/MORA/Tables/ds_monthly_tightest.csv")

#### Wildfire Hazard Potential (WHP) Map

Contextual data (known fires, landcover classification):

Map of wildfire hazard potential (WHP) across a shared bounding box spanning both the current-system (Edith Creek) and Paradise GW watersheds, cropped (not masked) to that box so the raster fills the full extent, with the two watersheds outlined in white for reference.

```{r whp_fig}

# --- 1. Shared AOI: current-system (Edith) + Paradise GW watersheds, used
# by both this figure and the Forest Cover Map below. ----------------------
map_aoi <- sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(system_watershed), sf::st_geometry(paradise_river_watershed))
buff_dist <- 1000
map_bbox <- sf::st_buffer(map_aoi, buff_dist)

# NPS Park Tiles basemap for both this figure and the Forest Cover Map
# below - fetched once here and reused there so the tiles aren't
# downloaded twice. Same zoom as the main site figure; lower it if this
# AOI turns out too large to fetch quickly.
nps_tiles_whp <- get_nps_basemap(aoi = map_bbox, style = "standard", buffer_km = 1, zoom = 15)
map_bbox_3857 <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(map_bbox, 3857))

colfunc <- colorRampPalette(c("#FFF176", "orange", "tomato"))
fire_pal <- colfunc(3)

# WHP raster for the map: crop (not mask) whp_conus_cls to map_bbox so the
# full rectangular bbox shows WHP color, rather than being clipped to a
# single watershed's shape.
whp_map_cls <- whp_conus_cls %>%
  terra::crop(sf::st_transform(map_bbox, 5070), mask = FALSE, touches = TRUE) %>%
  terra::na.omit()

reclass_map <- cats(whp_map_cls)[[1]] %>%
  dplyr::mutate(class_short = str_sub(cats(whp_map_cls)[[1]][, 2], 4))
whp_map_cls <- categories(whp_map_cls, layer = 1, value = reclass_map, active = 2)

# Reproject (nearest-neighbor, to preserve categories) to match the Web
# Mercator basemap, then convert to a data frame for geom_raster().
whp_map_cls_3857 <- terra::project(whp_map_cls, "EPSG:3857", method = "near")
whp_df <- terra::as.data.frame(whp_map_cls_3857, xy = TRUE)
names(whp_df)[ncol(whp_df)] <- "class_short"
whp_df$class_short <- factor(whp_df$class_short, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Non-burnable"))

system_watershed_3857         <- sf::st_transform(system_watershed, 3857)
paradise_river_watershed_3857 <- sf::st_transform(paradise_river_watershed, 3857)
site_fig_point_whp_3857       <- sf::st_transform(site_fig_point, 3857)

# WHP - Categorical
whp_fig <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_nps_basemap(nps_tiles_whp) +
  geom_raster(data = whp_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = class_short), alpha = 0.5) +
  # Current-system (Edith) and Paradise GW watersheds, outlined in white so
  # they read clearly against the raster and basemap.
  geom_sf(data = system_watershed_3857, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = paradise_river_watershed_3857, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # site_fig_point (the current-system point captured for the Site Figure,
  # with a "label" column reading "Current System") is reused here.
  geom_sf(data = site_fig_point_whp_3857, fill = pal$black, color = "white",
          shape = 23, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = site_fig_point_whp_3857,
                            aes(label = label, geometry = geometry),
                            stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 2.5, label.size = 0,
                            fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Wildfire\nHazard Potential",
                    values = c("Low" = fire_pal[1], "Moderate" = fire_pal[2],
                               "High" = fire_pal[3], "Non-burnable" = "grey50"),
                    breaks = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Non-burnable"),
                    na.translate = FALSE) +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.3) +
  ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl", which_north = "true",
                                    style = ggspatial::north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(map_bbox_3857["xmin"], map_bbox_3857["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(map_bbox_3857["ymin"], map_bbox_3857["ymax"]),
           crs = 3857, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.98, 0.98), legend.justification = c(1, 1),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.8), color = NA))

whp_fig

dir.create("data/park/MORA/Figs", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/whp_fig.jpg", whp_fig, width = 6, height = 2.65, dpi = 600)

```

#### Forest Cover Map

```{r forest_cover_fig}

# Forest cover raster for the map: crop (not mask) NLCD to the same shared
# bbox as the WHP map above (map_bbox), rather than reusing the
# fire_aoi-masked `nlcd` object built for the burned/forested-fraction
# stats above. Reuses `nps_tiles_whp` (same map_bbox) fetched in the WHP
# chunk above rather than downloading the same tiles twice.
nlcd_raw_map <- terra::rast("data/all/nlcd_2021_land_cover_l48_20230630/nlcd_2021_land_cover_l48_20230630.img")
nlcd_map <- nlcd_raw_map %>%
  terra::crop(sf::st_transform(map_bbox, crs = terra::crs(nlcd_raw_map)), mask = FALSE)

# Build a fill palette from the NLCD raster's own embedded color table
# (the same colors tmap's default tm_raster() was using for this raster).
# terra's coltab()/cats() column names have varied a bit across versions -
# this is the piece most worth double-checking against the actual render.
nlcd_ct   <- terra::coltab(nlcd_map)[[1]]
nlcd_cats <- terra::cats(nlcd_map)[[1]]
names(nlcd_cats)[1] <- "value"

nlcd_lookup <- nlcd_cats %>%
  dplyr::left_join(nlcd_ct, by = "value") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(hex = grDevices::rgb(red, green, blue, maxColorValue = 255))

nlcd_class_col <- names(nlcd_cats)[2]
nlcd_palette <- setNames(nlcd_lookup$hex, nlcd_lookup[[nlcd_class_col]])

nlcd_map_3857 <- terra::project(nlcd_map, "EPSG:3857", method = "near")
nlcd_df <- terra::as.data.frame(nlcd_map_3857, xy = TRUE)
names(nlcd_df)[ncol(nlcd_df)] <- "class"

# Current-system (Edith) and Paradise GW watersheds, outlined in white -
# same treatment as the WHP map above.
system_watershed_3857_fc         <- sf::st_transform(system_watershed, 3857)
paradise_river_watershed_3857_fc <- sf::st_transform(paradise_river_watershed, 3857)
site_fig_point_fc_3857           <- sf::st_transform(site_fig_point, 3857)

# Forest Cover
forest_cover_fig <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_nps_basemap(nps_tiles_whp) +
  geom_raster(data = nlcd_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = class), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_sf(data = system_watershed_3857_fc, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = paradise_river_watershed_3857_fc, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # See the WHP map note above - reusing site_fig_point in place of the
  # undefined "select_system".
  geom_sf(data = site_fig_point_fc_3857, fill = pal$black, color = "white",
          shape = 23, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = site_fig_point_fc_3857,
                            aes(label = label, geometry = geometry),
                            stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 2.5, label.size = 0,
                            fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "NLCD Land Cover Class", values = nlcd_palette, na.translate = FALSE) +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.3) +
  ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl", which_north = "true",
                                    style = ggspatial::north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(map_bbox_3857["xmin"], map_bbox_3857["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(map_bbox_3857["ymin"], map_bbox_3857["ymax"]),
           crs = 3857, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = c(1, 1), legend.justification = c(1, 1),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.8), color = NA))

forest_cover_fig

ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/forest_fig.jpg", forest_cover_fig, width = 8, height = 2.65, dpi = 600)

# Combined land cover (left) and WHP (right) map for the main-text Fire
# section, with both legends outside the map panels so they don't cover
# the catchments.
legend_right <- theme(legend.position = "right",
                      legend.justification = "center",
                      legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
                      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
                      legend.title = element_text(size = 8))
landcover_whp_fig <- ggarrange(forest_cover_fig + legend_right,
                               whp_fig + legend_right,
                               ncol = 2, labels = c("a", "b"))
ggsave("data/park/MORA/Figs/landcover_whp_fig.jpg", landcover_whp_fig,
       width = 10, height = 4.5, dpi = 500, bg = "white")
rm(legend_right, landcover_whp_fig)

### Historic Fires

```{r figure_B7}

# --- 1. NPS Park Tiles basemap for the fire extent -------------------------
buff_dist <- 30000
colfunc <- colorRampPalette(c(pal$yellow, pal$orange, pal$pink, pal$lightpink))

fires_labeled <- park_new_geomac %>%
  dplyr::arrange(FIRE_YEAR) %>%
  tidyr::unite("Historical Fires", FIRE_YEAR, INCIDENT, sep = " ")

fire_extent <- fires_labeled %>% sf::st_union() %>% sf::st_buffer(buff_dist)
nps_tiles_fires <- get_nps_basemap(aoi = fire_extent, style = "standard", buffer_km = 1, zoom = 8)
fire_bbox_3857 <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(fire_extent, 3857))

# colfunc(4) in the original tmap version hardcoded 4 colors regardless of
# how many distinct fires are actually in park_new_geomac; sized
# dynamically here to the real number of fire labels so the palette
# always has enough colors to cover them.
fire_labels <- unique(fires_labeled[["Historical Fires"]])
fire_pal_hist <- setNames(colfunc(length(fire_labels)), fire_labels)

park_boundary_fire_3857     <- sf::st_transform(park_boundary, 3857) %>% dplyr::mutate(name = park_boundary$UNIT_NAME)
fires_labeled_3857          <- sf::st_transform(fires_labeled, 3857)
site_fig_point_fire_3857    <- sf::st_transform(site_fig_point, 3857)

# --- 2. Map -----------------------------------------------------------------

figure_B7 <-

                            fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(fire_pal_hist, "Park Boundary" = pal$teal, "Contributing Area" = "navy"),
                    name = "") +
  scale_color_manual(values = fire_pal_hist, guide = "none") +

           ylim = c(fire_bbox_3857["ymin"], fire_bbox_3857["ymax"]),
           crs = 3857, expand = FALSE) +

For context, how does this storm compare to typical summer hourly precip at Paradise?

```{r}

# Typical summer hourly precip - full historical record, Paradise SNOTEL
summer_months <- 6:9  # NOTE, snow could be happening September (and other months)
# but wanted to get a general idea

precip_paradise_full <- snotel_hourly %>%
  filter(name == "Paradise", sensor_id == "PREC.I") %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  group_by(water_year) %>%
  mutate(gap_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(datetime, lag(datetime), units = "hours")),
         raw_increment = value - lag(value)) %>%
  ungroup()

# There was an hourly precip amount of >2000 inches at one point so likely
# a data quality issue, setting an arbitrary limit to filter those out
implausible_increment_in <- 5

# Typical sampling interval = median gap between consecutive readings;
# readings after a gap > 1.5x this are dropped (increment spans missing data).
typical_gap_hrs <- median(precip_paradise_full$gap_hrs, na.rm = TRUE)

summer_hourly_precip <- precip_paradise_full %>%
  dplyr::mutate(value = dplyr::if_else(is.na(raw_increment) |
                                       raw_increment < 0 |
                                       raw_increment > implausible_increment_in |
                                       gap_hrs > typical_gap_hrs * 1.5,
                                      NA_real_, raw_increment)) %>%
  filter(month(datetime) %in% summer_months)

summer_precip_stats <- summer_hourly_precip %>%
  summarize(
    n_hours = n(),
    n_wet_hours = sum(value > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_wet_hours = 100 * n_wet_hours / n_hours,
    mean_in = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_in = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_in = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_in = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    p90_in = quantile(value, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95_in = quantile(value, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    p99_in = quantile(value, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),
    p99_9_in = quantile(value, 0.999, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(summer_precip_stats, digits = 4,
     caption = paste0("Typical hourly precip - Paradise SNOTEL, summer months (",
                      paste(month.abb[summer_months], collapse = "-"), ")"))

# Where does the storm's peak hourly rate fall in the typical summer distribution?
storm_summary %>%
  mutate(pctile_of_summer_hourly = 100 * mean(summer_hourly_precip$value <= peak_hourly_precip_in, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  select(peak_hourly_precip_in, pctile_of_summer_hourly) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Sep 6 storm peak hourly rate vs. typical summer hourly precip")

# 99.8 percentile of summer hourly for the peak hourly event in Sep 2025
# so this was a pretty large event


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(implausible_increment_in, precip_paradise_full, snotel_hourly, summer_hourly_precip, summer_months, summer_precip_stats)
gc()
```

Now want to see what that means for rainfall daily amounts since we only have daily
for projections

```{r}

# Typical daily precip - full historical record, Paradise SNOTEL
# (daily, since climate projections/WBM can only be compared at a daily timestep)
precip_paradise_daily_full <- snotel_daily_tidy %>%
  filter(name == "Paradise") %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  group_by(water_year) %>%
  mutate(gap_days = as.numeric(difftime(date, lag(date), units = "days")),
               raw_increment = precip_in - lag(precip_in)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Sanity-check remaining large increments before deciding a cutoff
precip_paradise_daily_full %>%
  dplyr::filter(raw_increment > 10) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, water_year, gap_days, precip_in, raw_increment)

# Use 10 as a cutoff (there aren't any days over 10 so doesn't matter much here)
implausible_daily_in <- 10
typical_gap_days <- median(precip_paradise_daily_full$gap_days, na.rm = TRUE)

# Rain only - restrict to Jun-Sep (again this is quick and dirty so likely some snow in this record)
rain_months <- 6:9
rain_temp_threshold_F <- 32

summer_daily_precip <- precip_paradise_daily_full %>%
  dplyr::mutate(daily_precip_in = dplyr::if_else(is.na(raw_increment) |
                                                 raw_increment < 0 |
                                                 raw_increment > implausible_daily_in |
                                                 gap_days > typical_gap_days * 1.5,
                                                NA_real_, raw_increment)) 

summer_daily_precip_stats <- summer_daily_precip %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_days = n(),
    n_wet_days = sum(daily_precip_in > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_wet_days = 100 * n_wet_days / n_days,
    mean_in = mean(daily_precip_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_in = median(daily_precip_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_in = sd(daily_precip_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_in = max(daily_precip_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    p90_in = quantile(daily_precip_in, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95_in = quantile(daily_precip_in, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    p99_in = quantile(daily_precip_in, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),
    p99_9_in = quantile(daily_precip_in, 0.999, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(summer_daily_precip_stats, digits = 4,
     caption = paste0("Typical daily rain - Paradise SNOTEL, ",
                      paste(month.abb[rain_months], collapse = "-"),
                      " (days above ", rain_temp_threshold_F, "F only)"))

# Where does the Sep 6 storm's total daily precip fall in the typical rain distribution?
storm_daily_total <- storm_summary$total_precip_in

data.frame(storm_daily_total_in = storm_daily_total,
          pctile_of_rain_daily = 100 * mean(summer_daily_precip$daily_precip_in <= storm_daily_total, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Sep 6 storm daily total vs. typical daily rain")


# Workspace cleanup: these are no longer used after this point.
rm(implausible_daily_in, precip_paradise_daily_full, rain_months, rain_temp_threshold_F, storm_daily_total, storm_summary, summer_daily_precip, summer_daily_precip_stats)
gc()
